| `<InputAccessoryView>` | `nsh/ios` | a bar over the keyboard (iOS only) | [nsh/ios](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-ios.md) |
| `<If>`, `<Each>` | nothing: globals | none: control flow | [Control flow](https://nsh.dev/elements/control-flow.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> A string is only drawn inside a `<Text>`. A string child of a `<View>` creates no native view and takes no part in
> layout.

## Common props

Every host element accepts the props below (the `CommonProps` type). Element pages list only their own props.

### Styling

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` (`TextStyle` for `<Text>` and `<Input>`, `ImageStyle` for `<Image>`) | Inline style, or an array of styles merged left to right (falsy entries skipped; arrays may nest, so `style={[base, props.style]}` takes a `props.style` that is itself an array). Wins over `class`. See the [style reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference.md). |
| `class` | `string` | Tailwind classes, resolved natively (`"flex-row gap-2 p-4 dark:bg-zinc-900"`). Later classes win over earlier ones. See [Tailwind](https://nsh.dev/docs/tailwind.md). |
| `classList` | `Record<string, boolean \| null \| undefined>` | Classes applied while their value is truthy (`{ "opacity-50": busy() }`). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Ignores presses (no press feedback either), applies `disabled:` classes and disables controls such as inputs. |

### Presses and feedback

Press handling runs natively: the platform recognizes the press and shows the feedback, and JS only hears about it
afterwards. Only the innermost pressable view responds; inside scroll views a press-in waits about 130 ms so a scroll can
start first.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onPress` | `() => void` | | A tap ended inside the view. |
| `onLongPress` | `() => void` | | The finger stayed down for `delayLongPress`. |
| `onPressIn` | `() => void` | | A finger went down on the view. |
| `onPressOut` | `() => void` | | The finger lifted or left. |
| `delayLongPress` | `number` | `500` | Milliseconds before a press becomes a long press. |
| `activeOpacity` | `number` | | The view's opacity while pressed. |
| `underlayColor` | `ColorValue` | | The background while pressed; the children fade to `underlayOpacity`. |
| `underlayOpacity` | `number` | `0.85` | The children's opacity while `underlayColor` shows. |
| `hitSlop` | `number \| { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` | | Extends the touch area beyond the bounds, in points. |
| `pointerEvents` | `"auto" \| "none" \| "box-none" \| "box-only"` | `"auto"` | Which touches the view and its children receive: `"none"` neither, `"box-none"` only the children, `"box-only"` only the view itself. |

`active:` Tailwind classes also apply while a view is pressed, with no JS round trip.

### Hover

On macOS, Linux and the GPUI backend, JS can hear the mouse come over a view and leave it (other platforms do not raise these events
yet; `hover:` classes style hovered views everywhere the platform tracks hover).

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `onHoverIn` | `() => void` | The mouse came over the view or a view inside it. |
| `onHoverOut` | `() => void` | The mouse left the view and the views inside it, or the window. |

Like CSS `:hover`, a view counts as hovered while the mouse is over it or over anything inside it, so the views around
the one under the mouse hear `onHoverIn` too (from the outside in; `onHoverOut` from the inside out). The events come
after the fact and never on touches. A view removed from under the mouse hears `onHoverOut`, on Linux at the next mouse
move.

```tsx
const hovered = signal<string | null>(null);

<View onHoverIn={() => hovered.set(file.path)} onHoverOut={() => hovered.set(null)} class="hover:bg-zinc-100">
  <Text>{file.name}</Text>
</View>
```

### Layout and identity

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `onLayout` | `(e: LayoutEvent) => void` | The view's frame relative to its parent, `{ x, y, width, height }`, after each layout that changes it. |
| `ref` | `YNode \| (node: YNode) => void` | The native node (see [ref methods](#ref-methods)). `ref={el}` assigns a variable, `ref={fn}` calls a function. |
| `nativeID` | `string` | Names the view for others, e.g. the `InputAccessoryView` an input refers to. |
| `testID` | `string` | An identifier for UI tests (on Android, the view's resource id). |

### Gestures driving native values

These props bind a gesture to [native animated values](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md) that move on the UI thread, with no
JS per frame. See [touch and gestures](https://nsh.dev/docs/touch-and-gestures.md).

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pan` | `{ x?: NativeValue; y?: NativeValue }` | Drags drive these values (points). |
| `onPanStart` | `(e: PanEvent) => void` | A drag started. |
| `onPanEnd` | `(e: PanEvent) => void` | A drag ended, with the release velocity (e.g. to start a `decay`). |
| `pinch` | `{ scale?: NativeValue }` | Two-finger pinches drive `scale`. |
| `onPinchStart` / `onPinchEnd` | `(e: { scale: number; velocity: number }) => void` | A pinch started / ended. |
| `rotation` | `{ angle?: NativeValue }` | Two-finger rotations drive `angle` (degrees). |
| `onRotationStart` / `onRotationEnd` | `(e: { rotation: number; velocity: number }) => void` | A rotation started / ended. |

`PanEvent` is `{ translationX, translationY, velocityX, velocityY, valueX?, valueY? }`: the translation since the start,
the velocity in points per second, and the bound values at that moment (a drag can grab a value mid-animation).

### Raw touches and the responder system

For gestures the props above do not cover, every element takes the touch and responder props:
`onTouchStart`, `onTouchMove`, `onTouchEnd`, `onTouchCancel` (and their `…Capture` forms),
`onStartShouldSetResponder`, `onMoveShouldSetResponder` (and `…Capture`), `onResponderGrant`, `onResponderReject`,
`onResponderStart`, `onResponderMove`, `onResponderEnd`, `onResponderRelease`, `onResponderTerminate` and
`onResponderTerminationRequest`. Each handler gets a `GestureResponderEvent`
(`{ identifier, locationX, locationY, pageX, pageY, target, timestamp, touches, changedTouches, nativeEvent,
stopPropagation() }`); the `…ShouldSetResponder` handlers also get a `gestureState` (`dx`, `dy`, `vx`, `vy`, ...).
Returning `true` from `onResponderGrant` keeps native scroll views from taking the touches. `panActivation`
(`{ activeOffsetX, activeOffsetY, failOffsetX, failOffsetY }`) makes the view the responder only once the platform
activates its pan, so drags inside scroll views leave the other axis to them
([Touch and gestures](https://nsh.dev/docs/touch-and-gestures.md#pans-inside-scroll-views-panactivation)).
`PanResponder` in [`nsh/gesture`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-gesture.md) builds on them.

### Accessibility

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accessible` | `boolean` | The view is one element for assistive technologies; its children are not exposed separately. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | What screen readers read. Views without a label read their texts. |
| `accessibilityHint` | `string` | What activating the element does. |
| `accessibilityRole` / `role` | `AccessibilityRole` | What the element is (`"button"`, `"header"`, `"link"`, `"switch"`, …). |
| `accessibilityState` | `{ disabled?, selected?, checked?, busy?, expanded? }` | The state assistive technologies report (`checked` may be `"mixed"`). |
| `accessibilityValue` | `{ min?, max?, now?, text? }` | The value of a range or textual element. |
| `accessibilityElementsHidden` | `boolean` | Hides the view and its subtree from assistive technologies. |
| `importantForAccessibility` | `"auto" \| "yes" \| "no" \| "no-hide-descendants"` | Whether the view is exposed. |
| `accessibilityActions` | `{ name: string; label?: string }[]` | Custom actions offered to assistive technologies. |
| `onAccessibilityAction` | `(e: { actionName: string }) => void` | The user invoked one of `accessibilityActions`. |

See [accessibility](https://nsh.dev/docs/accessibility.md).

### Platform-only props

Props that exist on one platform go in an object named after it, so the shared props stay the same everywhere. Only the
current platform's object is sent; the others are ignored.

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `ios={{…}}` | iOS and Mac Catalyst. `<Input>`, `Modal` and `WebView` add their own keys. |
| `android={{…}}` | Android. Every element takes `ripple`, `elevation` and `accessibilityLiveRegion` (below). |
| `desktop={{…}}` | Desktop platforms and desktop browsers; ignored on mobile. Every element takes `windowDrag` (below). |
| `web={{…}}` | Browsers; ignored elsewhere. |

| `android` key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ripple` | `{ color?, borderless?, radius?, foreground? }` | The material ripple while pressed. |
| `elevation` | `number` | The material shadow (points), from the view's shape. |
| `accessibilityLiveRegion` | `"none" \| "polite" \| "assertive"` | How changes of the view are announced to TalkBack. |

| `desktop` key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `windowDrag` | `boolean` | Pressing the view drags the window, as its title bar would; `false` keeps a part of a draggable view clickable. See [a title bar of your own](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-desktop.md#a-title-bar-of-your-own). |

```tsx
<View onPress={save} android={{ ripple: { color: "#00000022" }, elevation: 2 }} class="rounded-lg bg-white p-4">
  <Text>Save</Text>
</View>
```

See [platform-specific code](https://nsh.dev/docs/platform-specific.md).

## Ref methods

`ref` receives a `YNode`. Its methods send commands to the native view, in order with the changes made before them in the
same turn. Each element page says which apply to it.

| Method | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `focus()` / `blur()` | `<Input>` | Focuses (shows the keyboard) / unfocuses. |
| `setSelection(start, end?)` | `<Input>` | Selects `start..end` in UTF-16 units; a caret without `end`. |
| `scrollTo({ x?, y?, animated? })` | `<Scroll>`, `List` | Scrolls to an offset. |
| `zoomTo({ scale, x?, y?, animated? })` | zoomable `<Scroll>` | Zooms to `scale` around a content point. |
| `scrollToOffset({ offset, animated? })` | `List` | Scrolls to an offset along the list's axis. |
| `scrollToIndex({ index, animated?, viewPosition?, viewOffset? })` | `List` | Scrolls an item into view. |
| `scrollToEnd({ animated? })` | `List` | Scrolls to the end of the content. |
| `reload()`, `goBack()`, `goForward()`, `stopLoading()`, `injectJavaScript(script)`, `postMessage(data)` | `WebView` | Controls the page. |
| `seek(seconds)` | `Video` | Jumps to a time. |
| `command(name, args?)` | native components | Calls a command of a registered native component ([`nsh/native`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-native.md)). |

```tsx
import { Input, View, type YNode } from "nsh";

let input!: YNode;
<View onPress={() => input.focus()}>
  <Input ref={input} placeholder="Tap the row to type" />
</View>;
```

## Why handlers never block the UI

The main thread never waits for JS. When the system needs an answer on the spot (may this text change, may the back
button pop, may this sheet close), NSH answers it natively from props set beforehand (`maxLength`, `preventBack`,
`dismissible`, `pointerEvents`, …), and the event reaches JS afterwards. This is why such behavior is a prop, not a
return value of a handler.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements

---

# View

`<View>` is the building block of every screen: a native container (a UIView on iOS and Mac Catalyst, a ViewGroup on
Android) that lays out its children with flexbox or grid, draws a background, borders, shadows and gradients, and handles
presses. Buttons, cards, rows and screens are all views.

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";

function App() {
  const liked = signal(false);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 16, backgroundColor: "#f6f8fa" }}>
      <View
        style={{
          backgroundColor: "#ffffff",
          borderRadius: 16,
          padding: 16,
          boxShadow: "0 4px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
          flexDirection: "row",
          alignItems: "center",
          gap: 12,
        }}
      >
        <View style={{ width: 40, height: 40, borderRadius: 20, backgroundColor: "#8250df" }} />
        <Text style={{ flex: 1, fontSize: 16 }}>A card</Text>
        <View onPress={() => liked.set(!liked())} activeOpacity={0.5} hitSlop={8}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 22 }}>{liked() ? "♥" : "♡"}</Text>
        </View>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Layout

A view lays out its children with flexbox, with these defaults: `flexDirection: "column"`, `flexShrink: 0`,
`alignContent: "flex-start"`, `position: "relative"`. `display: "grid"` switches to CSS grid and `display: "block"` to
block layout. Sizes are in points. See [layout](https://nsh.dev/docs/layout.md) and the [style reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference.md).

The Tailwind `flex` class follows CSS rather than the style default: `class="flex"` is a row. Use `flex-col` for a column.

## Props

`<View>` has no props of its own beyond the [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#common-props): `style` (`ViewStyle`), `class`,
`classList`, `disabled`, the press props (`onPress`, `onLongPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `delayLongPress`,
`activeOpacity`, `underlayColor`, `underlayOpacity`, `hitSlop`, `pointerEvents`), `onHoverIn` / `onHoverOut`,
`onFileDragEnter` / `onFileDragLeave` / `onFileDrop`, `onLayout`, `ref`, `nativeID`,
`testID`, the gesture props (`pan`, `pinch`, `rotation` and their events), the touch and responder props, the
accessibility props and `ios` / `android` / `desktop`.

## Press feedback

A pressable view is any view with a press handler. Three kinds of feedback run natively while the finger is down, with no
JS round trip:

```tsx
// Fade the whole view.
<View onPress={open} activeOpacity={0.6}>…</View>

// Show a background and fade the children (default 0.85).
<View onPress={open} underlayColor="#e5e7eb" underlayOpacity={0.7}>…</View>

// Change any style while pressed with active: classes.
<View onPress={open} class="bg-blue-600 active:bg-blue-800 active:scale-95">…</View>
```

On Android, `android={{ ripple: { color: "#0000001f" } }}` adds the material ripple (`borderless`, `radius` and
`foreground` adjust it).

`disabled` removes the press listeners from the native view (no press, no feedback) and applies `disabled:` classes:

```tsx
<View onPress={submit} disabled={!valid()} class="bg-green-600 disabled:opacity-40">…</View>
```

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onPress` | none | A tap ended inside the view. |
| `onLongPress` | none | The finger stayed down for `delayLongPress` (500 ms). |
| `onPressIn` / `onPressOut` | none | A finger went down / lifted or left. |
| `onHoverIn` / `onHoverOut` | none | The mouse came over the view (or a view inside it) / left it or the window; macOS, Linux and GPUI ([hover](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#hover)). |
| `onFileDragEnter` / `onFileDragLeave` | none | A local-file drag entered / left the active desktop destination. |
| `onFileDrop` | `{ uris: string[] }` | Local files or directories were dropped on the desktop destination. |
| `onLayout` | `{ x, y, width, height }` | The frame relative to the parent changed. |
| `onPanStart` / `onPanEnd` | `PanEvent` | A drag bound with `pan` started / ended. |
| `onPinchStart` / `onPinchEnd` | `{ scale, velocity }` | A pinch bound with `pinch` started / ended. |
| `onRotationStart` / `onRotationEnd` | `{ rotation, velocity }` | A rotation bound with `rotation` started / ended. |
| `onAccessibilityAction` | `{ actionName }` | A custom accessibility action ran. |

Touch and responder events: see [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#raw-touches-and-the-responder-system).

## Desktop file drops

On AppKit, GTK and Win32, a view with `onFileDrop` receives local files and
directories dragged from another application. `onFileDragEnter` and
`onFileDragLeave` track the active destination; `onFileDrop` receives
`{ uris: string[] }` in the native file-list order. Each entry is an absolute
`file:` URL with escaped spaces and non-ASCII characters. Parse the URL to
obtain a filesystem path rather than removing the prefix by hand.

```tsx
const hovering = signal(false);
const files = signal<string[]>([]);

<View
  onFileDragEnter={() => hovering.set(true)}
  onFileDragLeave={() => hovering.set(false)}
  onFileDrop={(event) => {
    files.set(event.uris);
    hovering.set(false);
  }}
  style={{ minHeight: 160, padding: 24 }}
>
  <Text>{hovering() ? "Release files here" : "Drop files here"}</Text>
  <Text>{files().join("\n")}</Text>
</View>
```

Rust components use the same events through `Interactive`:

```rust
use nsh_core::ui::prelude::*;

fn drop_area() -> impl IntoElement {
    let files = signal(Vec::<String>::new());
    view()
        .min_h(px(160.0))
        .p_6()
        .on_file_drop(move |event: &FileDropEvent| files.set(event.uris.clone()))
        .child(text(move || files.get().join("\n")))
}
```

The closest enabled ancestor listening to `onFileDrop` receives the drop.
A modal root bounds that search. `disabled` removes file-drag/drop listeners;
leaving, cancellation, completion and destination removal clear the active
state. Acceptance uses the Copy operation and mounted native state. The app
decides whether to read, open or transfer the received files.

## Ref methods

A plain view has no commands of its own. `ref` gives you the `YNode`, e.g. to pass to
`AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus` ([`nsh/accessibility`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-accessibility.md)).

## Views inside text

A `<View>` placed inside a `<Text>` is an inline attachment: it sits on the baseline and wraps with the words, and it
takes presses of its own. See [text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text.md#inline-views-and-images).

## Platform notes

- `boxShadow` and the shadow props (`shadowColor`, `shadowOpacity`, `shadowRadius`, `shadowOffset`) draw on
  both platforms; `android={{ elevation }}` gives Android's material shadow instead. On Android a shadow needs a
  background color (a view with a transparent background casts none).
- `filter` on views: iOS supports only `opacity()`, `brightness()` up to 1 and `drop-shadow()` (images take every color
  filter and `blur()`); Android supports them all from API 31, and only the color filters below it.
- `backdropFilter: "blur(…)"` is a system material on iOS (an approximation) and needs API 31 on Android.
- Android has no `skewX` / `skewY` transforms.
- `borderCurve: "continuous"` draws corners that ease into the edges (as iOS app icons), on both platforms.
- The `cursor` style applies where there is a pointer (Mac Catalyst, iPad with a pointer, desktops).

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/view

---

# Text

`<Text>` draws a paragraph. It is the only element that shows strings: a string child of a `<View>` draws nothing. The
paragraph is typeset natively (CoreText on iOS and Mac Catalyst, `StaticLayout` on Android) and measured on the engine
thread, so the main thread only draws it.

```tsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, color: "#1f2328" }}>
  Read the <Text style={{ fontWeight: "700" }}>terms</Text> before you continue.
</Text>
```

## Spans

A `<Text>` inside a `<Text>` is a span of the same paragraph, not a separate view. Spans inherit the text styles of the
paragraph (`color`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, …) and override what they set. The whole block is one native view.

```tsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 17 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontWeight: "300" }}>Light </Text>
  <Text style={{ fontWeight: "bold" }}>Bold </Text>
  <Text style={{ fontStyle: "italic", color: "#8250df" }}>Italic</Text>
</Text>
```

### Links

A span with a press handler is a link: a press on its characters goes to the span, a press elsewhere to the paragraph.

```tsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 15 }} onPress={() => log("the sentence")}>
  {"By continuing you agree to the "}
  <Text style={{ color: "#0969da", textDecorationLine: "underline" }} onPress={() => open("terms")}>
    Terms of service
  </Text>
  .
</Text>
```

### Inline views and images

Any other element inside a `<Text>` (a `<View>`, an `<Image>`, even inside spans) is an inline attachment: it is laid out
at its own size, sits on the baseline and wraps with the words. It takes presses of its own.

```tsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 26 }}>
  {"Made with "}
  <Image src={logo} style={{ width: 18, height: 18, borderRadius: 4 }} />
  {" nsh. Status "}
  <View style={{ backgroundColor: "#1a7f37", borderRadius: 9, paddingHorizontal: 7, height: 18, justifyContent: "center" }}>
    <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 11, fontWeight: "700" }}>LIVE</Text>
  </View>
</Text>
```

Attachments cut off by `numberOfLines` or an ellipsis are hidden. Copying a selectable text leaves them out.

### Whitespace

JSX text follows React's rules: lines are trimmed except at the text's ends, whitespace-only lines are dropped and the
remaining lines are joined with one space. Spaces on one line are kept (`{a} {b}` keeps its space). Write
`{" "}` or a string expression when a span needs a leading or trailing space.

## Props

Besides the [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#common-props) (with `style` typed as `TextStyle`):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numberOfLines` | `number` | `0` | The most lines shown; `0` is unlimited. |
| `ellipsizeMode` | `"tail" \| "head" \| "middle" \| "clip"` | `"tail"` | Where text that does not fit `numberOfLines` is cut. |
| `allowFontScaling` | `boolean` | `true` | Follow the system text size setting. |
| `maxFontSizeMultiplier` | `number` | `0` | The upper bound of the system scale; `0` is none. |
| `adjustsFontSizeToFit` | `boolean` | `false` | Shrink the font until the text fits its lines (`numberOfLines`) and its box. |
| `minimumFontScale` | `number` | | How far `adjustsFontSizeToFit` shrinks at most (0..1; at least 0.1). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | | The user can select ranges of the text: a long press selects a word, handles extend it, the edit menu copies it. Unset, text is not selectable, except in desktop browsers, where it is unless it is inside an interactive element; `false` keeps it unselectable there too. |
| `selectionColor` | `ColorValue` | | The highlight (and handles) of the selection of selectable text; the platform's accent by default. |
| `onTextLayout` | `(e: { lines: TextLayoutLine[] }) => void` | | The laid-out lines after each layout. |

The `select-text` Tailwind class is the same as `selectable`.

## Text styles

`TextStyle` adds to the view styles: `color`, `fontSize`, `fontWeight` (`"normal"`, `"bold"` or 100–900), `fontStyle`,
`fontFamily`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `textAlignVertical`, `textTransform`, `textDecorationLine`,
`textDecorationColor`, `textDecorationStyle`, `textDecorationThickness`, `textUnderlineOffset`, `textShadowColor`,
`textShadowOffset`, `textShadowRadius`, `fontVariant` and `writingDirection`. See the
[style reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference.md#textstyle) and [text](https://nsh.dev/docs/text.md).

`fontFamily` takes a system family or the name an imported font evaluates to:

```tsx
import { Text } from "nsh";
import Inter from "./fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf";

<Text style={{ fontFamily: Inter, fontSize: 17 }}>Inter</Text>;
```

The font is registered before the first frame. See [fonts](https://nsh.dev/docs/fonts.md).

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onTextLayout` | `{ lines: TextLayoutLine[] }` | After each layout of the paragraph. |
| `onPress`, `onLongPress`, … | none | As on [view](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md#events); on a span, presses on its characters. |
| `onLayout` | `{ x, y, width, height }` | The block's frame changed. |

`TextLayoutLine` is `{ text, x, y, width, height, ascender, descender, capHeight, xHeight }`, in the text's content box:

```tsx
const lines = signal(0);
<Text onTextLayout={(e) => lines.set(e.lines.length)}>{article}</Text>;
```

## Ref methods

None of its own.

## Platform notes

- Selection stays inside one text block (one `<Text>` and its spans); it does not run across blocks. iOS shows its edit menu (Copy, Select All, Look Up, Translate, Share), Android a floating toolbar (Copy, Select all, Share).
- Text decorations other than a solid single line (`double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `wavy`) are drawn by NSH on iOS.
- iOS texts draw no gradient backgrounds or inset shadows.
- `fontScale()` from [`nsh/device`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-device.md) reports the current system text scale.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/text

---

# Image

`<Image>`, imported from [`nsh/image`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-image.md), shows a picture from the app's assets or from a URL. Images are downloaded and decoded off the main thread,
downsampled to the size the view shows them at, and cached in memory. Animated GIF, WebP and APNG images play.

```tsx
import { View } from "nsh";
import { Image } from "nsh/image";
import logo from "./assets/logo.png";

<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 12 }}>
  <Image src={logo} />
  <Image
    src="https://example.com/avatar.jpg"
    defaultSource={logo}
    resizeMode="cover"
    style={{ width: 64, height: 64, borderRadius: 32 }}
  />
</View>;
```

An imported asset knows its size: without a `width` or `height` the image takes it, and with only one of them the other
follows the asset's aspect ratio. A URL has no known size before it loads, so give remote images a `width` and a `height`
(or an `aspectRatio` with one of them).

## Sources

`src` (and `defaultSource`) takes:

| Value | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|
| An imported asset | `import logo from "./logo.png"` | An `ImageAsset` `{ uri, width, height }`, sized in points: a `@2x` file counts half its pixels. `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp` and `.heic` can be imported. |
| A URL | `"https://example.com/a.jpg"` | Downloaded and cached. Downloads of the same URL are shared between views. |
| An asset path | `"asset:/images/a.png"` | A file of the app's assets. |
| `{ uri }` | `{ uri: "https://…" }` | The same as the string. |

During development assets are served by the dev server; `nsh build` and `nsh package` copy them into the app. See
[images and assets](https://nsh.dev/docs/images-and-assets.md).

> [!NOTE]
> If the app declares [capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md), remote images are allowed only from the hosts
> it lists; a refused image fails with `onError`. `asset:` URIs are always allowed.

## Props

Besides the [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#common-props) (with `style` typed as `ImageStyle`):

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string \| ImageAsset \| { uri: string }` | | The image. |
| `resizeMode` | `"cover" \| "contain" \| "stretch" \| "center"` | `"cover"` | How the image fits its box. |
| `defaultSource` | `string \| ImageAsset \| { uri: string }` | | Shown until `src` has loaded; best a local asset. |
| `blurRadius` | `number` | | Blurs the image by this radius in points (applied once while decoding, off the main thread). |
| `fadeDuration` | `number` | iOS `0`, Android `300` | How long a loaded image fades in, in milliseconds. |
| `onLoadStart` | `() => void` | | Loading began. |
| `onProgress` | `(e: { loaded: number; total: number }) => void` | | Download progress in bytes (`total` is 0 when unknown), at most every 100 ms. |
| `onLoad` | `(e: { width: number; height: number }) => void` | | Loaded; the source image's size in pixels (not the decoded, downsampled one). |
| `onError` | `(e: { message: string }) => void` | | Loading failed. |
| `onLoadEnd` | `() => void` | | After `onLoad` or `onError`. |

`ImageStyle` adds `tintColor` to the view styles: it recolors a template image (an icon drawn in one color).

```tsx
<Image src={icon} style={{ width: 24, height: 24, tintColor: "#0969da" }} />
```

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onLoadStart` | none | Loading began. |
| `onProgress` | `{ loaded, total }` | Bytes arrived (at most every 100 ms). |
| `onLoad` | `{ width, height }` | The image is shown; its source size in pixels. |
| `onError` | `{ message }` | Loading or decoding failed, or the host is not allowed. |
| `onLoadEnd` | none | After `onLoad` or `onError`. |

```tsx
const state = signal("loading");
<Image
  src={url}
  style={{ width: "100%", aspectRatio: 16 / 9 }}
  onLoad={(e) => state.set(`${e.width}×${e.height} px`)}
  onError={(e) => state.set(e.message)}
/>;
```

To know an image's size or load it before showing it, call `Image.getSize(uri)` and `Image.prefetch(uri)`: the same
`Image` from [`nsh/image`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-image.md) that renders the element carries them.

## Ref methods

None of its own.

## Platform notes

- The cache key includes the decode size and the blur radius: the same URL shown at two sizes is decoded twice but
  downloaded once.
- iOS plays animated images as a keyframe animation (up to 600 frames); a tinted animated image shows its first frame.
- Android plays animated images from API 28 (`AnimatedImageDrawable`); animated images are not cached there and are not
  blurred.
- On Android borders are drawn above the image, as on iOS.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/image

---

# Scroll

`<Scroll>` is a native scroll view (UIScrollView on iOS and Mac Catalyst, a ScrollView on Android). It lays out all its
children as its content and scrolls them natively: scrolling, flinging, bouncing and snapping never wait for JS.

```tsx
<Scroll style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <View style={{ padding: 16, gap: 8 }}>
    <Each of={rows}>{(row) => <Text>{row().title}</Text>}</Each>
  </View>
</Scroll>
```

`<Scroll>` creates every child, which suits pages of moderate size. For long or unbounded data use a
[list](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md): it creates only the rows near the viewport and recycles them.

A scroll view must have a bounded size along its axis: give it `flex: 1` (or a `height`) inside a container that has
one. Its content is laid out at the scroll view's width (height when `horizontal`) and as tall (wide) as it needs.

## Props

Besides the [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#common-props) (with `style` typed as `ViewStyle`):

### Scrolling

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `horizontal` | `boolean` | `false` | Scrolls sideways. |
| `scrollEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | The user can scroll it. |
| `showsIndicator` | `boolean` | `true` | The scroll indicator shows. On the desktop and in desktop browsers a horizontal view keeps it: it is the mouse's scroll bar. |
| `bounces` | `boolean` | `true` | Overscroll past the edges. |
| `pagingEnabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Stops at multiples of the viewport. |
| `snapToInterval` | `number` | `0` | Stops at multiples of this length (0: off). |
| `snapToOffsets` | `number[]` | | Stops at these offsets. |
| `snapToAlignment` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"start"` | Which point of an item aligns with the viewport with `snapToInterval`. |
| `disableIntervalMomentum` | `boolean` | `false` | A fling moves one snap point at most. |
| `decelerationRate` | `"normal" \| "fast" \| number` | platform | How fast a fling slows down: the velocity kept per millisecond (`normal` 0.998, `fast` 0.99). |
| `contentInset` | `{ top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` | | Room around the content. |
| `contentOffset` | `{ x?, y? }` | | Where it starts. |
| `keyboardDismissMode` | `"none" \| "on-drag" \| "interactive"` | `"none"` | Whether dragging dismisses the keyboard. |
| `keyboardShouldPersistTaps` | `"never" \| "always" \| "handled" \| boolean` | `"never"` | Whether a tap dismisses the keyboard: `never` (the tap only dismisses it), `always` (it stays up), `handled` (it stays up when something handles the tap). |
| `scrollValue` | `NativeValue` | | A native value fed with the scroll offset (main axis), for scroll-linked animations. |
| `scrollEventThrottle` | `number` | | Minimum milliseconds between `onScroll` events (at most one per frame anyway). |

### Pull to refresh

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `refreshing` | `boolean` | The refresh spinner shows. |
| `onRefresh` | `() => void` | The user pulled to refresh: start loading and set `refreshing` until it ends. |

```tsx
const refreshing = signal(false);
async function reload() {
  refreshing.set(true);
  await load();
  refreshing.set(false);
}

<Scroll style={{ flex: 1 }} refreshing={refreshing()} onRefresh={reload}>
  …
</Scroll>;
```

### Zooming

Setting `maximumZoomScale` above `minimumZoomScale` makes the content zoomable with a pinch; zoomed in, it scrolls both
ways. Lists do not zoom.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minimumZoomScale` | `number` | `1` | The smallest zoom. |
| `maximumZoomScale` | `number` | `1` | The largest zoom. |
| `zoomScale` | `number` | | Zooms to this scale when it changes; otherwise the user's zoom is kept. |
| `bouncesZoom` | `boolean` | `true` | Pinching may go past the limits and springs back. |
| `pinchGestureEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | The user can pinch to zoom. |
| `centerContent` | `boolean` | `false` | Content smaller than the viewport (zoomed out) is centered. |

```tsx
let photo!: YNode;
<Scroll ref={photo} maximumZoomScale={4} centerContent style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#000" }}>
  <Image src={picture} style={{ width: 390, height: 520 }} onPress={() => photo.zoomTo({ scale: 1, animated: true })} />
</Scroll>;
```

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onScroll` | `ScrollEvent` | The offset changed (at most once per frame, and no more often than `scrollEventThrottle`). |
| `onScrollBeginDrag` / `onScrollEndDrag` | `{ x, y }` | The user started / stopped dragging. |
| `onMomentumScrollBegin` / `onMomentumScrollEnd` | `{ x, y }` | A glide after the drag started / stopped. A glide caught by a new drag still ends with `onMomentumScrollEnd`. |
| `onScrollEnd` | `{ x, y }` | Scrolling came to rest. |
| `onRefresh` | none | Pulled to refresh. |

`ScrollEvent` is `{ x, y, contentWidth, contentHeight, width, height, zoomScale }`: the offset, the (zoomed) content
size, the viewport size and the zoom scale (1 unless the view zooms).

> [!TIP]
> To move something with the scroll position (a shrinking header, a parallax image), bind `scrollValue` to a native
> value and interpolate it in a style. It runs on the UI thread at the display's rate, which `onScroll` (a JS event per
> frame) cannot guarantee. See [animation](https://nsh.dev/docs/animation.md).

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `scrollTo({ x?, y?, animated? })` | Scrolls to an offset. |
| `zoomTo({ scale, x?, y?, animated? })` | Zooms to `scale` (clamped to the limits) with the content point (`x`, `y`, unzoomed points) in the middle of the viewport, or around the middle. E.g. a double tap zooming in on the tapped point. |

```tsx
let scroller!: YNode;
<Scroll ref={scroller}>…</Scroll>;
scroller.scrollTo({ y: 0, animated: true });
```

## Keyboard

Inputs inside a scroll view are kept clear of the keyboard natively: the scroll view gets a bottom inset and scrolls to
the focused input, with no JS involved. For content outside scroll views use `KeyboardAvoidingView` from
[`nsh/ui/mobile`](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md). See [forms and the keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).

## Right to left

Horizontal scroll views start at the right end in right-to-left layouts and keep their distance from it as the content
changes; their children are mirrored.

## Platform notes

- Android: pull to refresh is drawn by NSH (overscroll stays native), `contentInset` is applied as padding, and
  `decelerationRate` only shapes snapping glides.
- Android has no zooming scroll view: NSH switches to its own, which scales the content around its top left and scrolls
  both ways. Pinches start after Android's minimum span between the fingers (about 27 mm).
- Mac Catalyst (Mac idiom) has no system refresh control; NSH detects the pull and shows a spinner.
- iOS redraws texts and canvases at the zoomed resolution when a zoom ends.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll

---

# Input

`<Input>` is a native text field: a UITextField (single line) or UITextView (`multiline`) on iOS and Mac Catalyst, an
EditText on Android. Typing, the caret, selection, autocorrection and autofill are the platform's own.

```tsx
import { Input, signal } from "nsh";

function NameField() {
  const name = signal("");
  return (
    <Input
      value={name()}
      onChangeText={(text) => name.set(text)}
      placeholder="Your name"
      autoCapitalize="words"
      returnKeyType="done"
      style={{ fontSize: 16, padding: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#d0d7de", borderRadius: 8 }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

- **Controlled**: pass `value` and update it in `onChangeText`. JS can rewrite what the user typed (trim it, format it):
  the text shows the edit at once and is corrected when the new `value` arrives. Each native edit carries a count, and a
  `value` from JS is applied only if it is based on the latest edit, so a slow JS turn never overwrites newer typing.
- **Uncontrolled**: pass `defaultValue` (or nothing) and read the text from `onChangeText` or `onSubmitEditing`.

Rules that must hold while the user types are props, answered natively without asking JS: `maxLength` limits the length
and `submitBehavior` (or `blurOnSubmit`) decides what return does. See [forms and the keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).

## Props

Besides the [common props](https://nsh.dev/elements.md#common-props) (with `style` typed as `TextStyle`: font, color, alignment and the
view styles apply):

### Text

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | | The text, controlled by JS. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | | The initial text. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | | Shown while the input is empty. |
| `placeholderTextColor` | `ColorValue` | | The placeholder's color. |
| `multiline` | `boolean` | `false` | Several lines; return inserts a line break unless `submitBehavior` says otherwise. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | | The most characters the user can enter. |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `true` | The user can change the text. |
| `secureTextEntry` | `boolean` | `false` | The text is hidden (passwords). |
| `allowFontScaling` | `boolean` | `true` | Follow the system text size. |
| `maxFontSizeMultiplier` | `number` | `0` | The upper bound of the system scale (0 is none). |

### Keyboard

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keyboardType` | `"default" \| "number-pad" \| "decimal-pad" \| "numeric" \| "numbers-and-punctuation" \| "email-address" \| "phone-pad" \| "url"` | `"default"` | The keyboard layout ([the values](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md#keyboards-and-autofill); `numbers-and-punctuation` has a minus sign on iOS). |
| `returnKeyType` | `"default" \| "done" \| "go" \| "next" \| "search" \| "send"` | `"default"` | The label of the return key. |
| `autoCapitalize` | `"none" \| "sentences" \| "words" \| "characters"` | `"sentences"` | Automatic capitalization. |
| `autoCorrect` | `boolean` | `true` | The system's corrections. |
| `autoComplete` | `AutoComplete \| TextContentType` | | What the input holds, for autofill: `"username"`, `"current-password"`, `"new-password"`, `"one-time-code"`, `"email"`, `"tel"`, `"postal-code"`, `"cc-number"`, `"off"`, … |
| `submitBehavior` | `"submit" \| "blurAndSubmit" \| "newline"` | `"blurAndSubmit"` (single line), `"newline"` (multiline) | What return does: `"submit"` reports `onSubmitEditing` and keeps the focus, `"blurAndSubmit"` also unfocuses, `"newline"` inserts a line break (multiline only; a single line submits). A multiline input that submits still takes line breaks from Shift+Return or Option / Alt+Return on hardware keyboards. Wins over `blurOnSubmit`. |
| `blurOnSubmit` | `boolean` | `true` | Return unfocuses a single-line input; `false` keeps the keyboard up (e.g. to send several messages). `submitBehavior` replaces it. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focused when it appears. |

### Caret and selection

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `caretHidden` | `boolean` | No caret is drawn. |
| `selectionColor` | `ColorValue` | The color of the caret and the selection. |
| `selection` | `{ start: number; end?: number }` | The controlled selection, in UTF-16 units; `end` defaults to `start` (a caret). |

### iOS

| `ios` key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `textContentType` | `AutoComplete \| TextContentType` | iOS's names for `autoComplete` (`"oneTimeCode"`, `"newPassword"`, …). |
| `inputAccessoryViewID` | `string` | The `nativeID` of an `InputAccessoryView` ([`nsh/ios`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-ios.md)) shown over the keyboard while the input has focus. |
| `keyboardAppearance` | `"default" \| "light" \| "dark"` | The keyboard's look; `"default"` follows the system's appearance. Android's keyboards follow the system's theme. |

```tsx
<Input autoComplete="one-time-code" keyboardType="number-pad" ios={{ textContentType: "oneTimeCode" }} />
```

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onChangeText` | `(text: string)` | The user changed the text. |
| `onSubmitEditing` | `{ text }` | The return key was pressed in an input that submits (single line, or `submitBehavior` `"submit"` / `"blurAndSubmit"`). |
| `onFocus` / `onBlur` | none | The input gained / lost focus. |
| `onSelectionChange` | `{ start, end }` | The caret or selection moved (UTF-16 units). |
| `onKeyPress` | `{ key }` | Before the text changes: `key` is the typed text, `"Backspace"` or `"Enter"`. |
| `onContentSizeChange` | `{ width, height }` | The size of the text changed (at the input's width when multiline). |

A multiline input that grows with its text:

```tsx
const height = signal(40);
<Input
  multiline
  onContentSizeChange={(e) => height.set(Math.min(120, Math.max(40, e.height + 16)))}
  style={{ height: height(), paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8 }}
/>;
```

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `focus()` | Focuses the input and shows the keyboard. |
| `blur()` | Unfocuses it. |
| `setSelection(start, end?)` | Selects `start..end` (UTF-16 units); a caret without `end`. |

Moving focus to the next field on return:

```tsx
let password!: YNode;
<>
  <Input returnKeyType="next" onSubmitEditing={() => password.focus()} />
  <Input ref={password} secureTextEntry autoComplete="current-password" />
</>;
```

`Keyboard.dismiss()` from [`nsh/ui/mobile`](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md) hides the keyboard whichever input has it.

## Platform notes

- Inputs inside a [`<Scroll>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md#keyboard) are kept clear of the keyboard natively. Elsewhere use
  `KeyboardAvoidingView`.
- `disabled` disables the input as well as applying `disabled:` classes.
- `inputAccessoryViewID` has no effect on Android, which has no keyboard accessory bar.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/input

---

# List

`<List>` shows long or unbounded data. Only the rows near the viewport exist: as the user scrolls, rows that leave are
recycled for the rows that come in. Which rows exist, their positions, columns, sticky headers and viewability are all
computed natively, so scrolling a list of thousands of items costs no more than a list of twenty.

```tsx
import { mount, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { List } from "nsh/list";

const contacts = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i, name: `Contact ${i + 1}` }));

function App() {
  return (
    <List each={contacts} estimatedItemSize={56} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      {(contact, index) => (
        <View style={{ height: 56, paddingHorizontal: 16, justifyContent: "center" }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 16 }}>
            {index() + 1}. {contact().name}
          </Text>
        </View>
      )}
    </List>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

`List` comes from [`nsh/list`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-list.md). It is generic: `List<T>` checks that `each` and the row
function agree on the item type, which TypeScript infers from `each`.

For a short list whose rows should all exist (a settings page, a form), an [`<Each>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/control-flow.md) inside a
[`<Scroll>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md) is simpler. For a list styled as a grouped table, see
[`ListView`](https://nsh.dev/components/list-view.md). The [lists guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/lists.md) covers patterns: infinite loading, chat,
sections.

## Rows are recycled

The row function runs once per cell, not once per item. When a cell is reused for another item, its `item()` and
`index()` accessors change and everything that reads them updates:

```tsx
<List each={messages()}>
  {(message) => <Text>{message().body}</Text>}
</List>
```

So keep per-item state in your data (keyed by id), not in signals created inside the row function: such a signal would
stay with the cell and show up on another item.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `each` | `readonly T[]` | | The items. |
| `children` | `(item: () => T, index: () => number) => JSX.Element` | | Renders one row. |
| `estimatedItemSize` | `number` | `50` | The size of items not measured yet, in points. Close estimates keep the scroll bar steady. |
| `horizontal` | `boolean` | `false` | Scrolls sideways. |
| `numColumns` | `number` | `1` | Items per row (vertical lists). |
| `inverted` | `boolean` | `false` | Laid out from the end, item 0 last (chat style): starts scrolled to the end and keeps its distance from the end as content changes. |
| `maintainVisibleContentPosition` | `{ autoscrollToBottomThreshold?: number }` | | Not inverted: at the end of the content, or within that many points of it, the list stays at the end as the content grows or the viewport shrinks; scrolled further up, the visible content stays. |
| `stickyHeaderIndices` | `number[]` | | Items that stick to the start while scrolled past (one column, not inverted). |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `ListContentStyle` | | Padding and gaps of the content, in points: `padding`, `paddingHorizontal`, `paddingVertical`, `paddingTop`, `paddingRight`, `paddingBottom`, `paddingLeft`, `gap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap`. |
| `ListHeaderComponent` | `ListSlot` | | Before the items: a component (`Header`) or an element (`<Header />`). |
| `ListFooterComponent` | `ListSlot` | | After the items. |
| `ListEmptyComponent` | `ListSlot` | | Shown instead of the items while `each` is empty. |
| `ItemSeparatorComponent` | `ListSlot` | | Between items (one column). |
| `initialScrollIndex` | `number` | | Scrolls to this item before the first frame. |
| `keyExtractor` | `(item: T, index: number) => string` | `item.key`, `item.id` or the index | The key of an item in viewability tokens. |
| `onEndReached` | `() => void` | | The end is near: load more. |
| `onEndReachedThreshold` | `number` | `1` | How close to the end (in viewports) `onEndReached` fires. |
| `onViewableItemsChanged` | `(info: { viewableItems: ViewToken<T>[]; changed: ViewToken<T>[] }) => void` | | Items became viewable or stopped being viewable. |
| `viewabilityConfig` | `ViewabilityConfig` | | When items count as viewable (below). |
| `refreshing` | `boolean` | | The pull-to-refresh spinner shows. |
| `onRefresh` | `() => void` | | The user pulled to refresh. |
| `showsIndicator` | `boolean` | `true` | The scroll indicator shows. On the desktop and in desktop browsers a horizontal view keeps it: it is the mouse's scroll bar. |
| `scrollValue` | `NativeValue` | | A native value fed with the scroll offset, for scroll-linked animations. |
| `keyboardDismissMode` | `"none" \| "on-drag" \| "interactive"` | `"none"` | Whether dragging dismisses the keyboard. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | | The list's own style (it needs a bounded size: `flex: 1` or a height). |
| `ref` | `YNode \| (node: YNode) => void` | | The list's node (see [ref methods](#ref-methods)). |

Lists also take the scrolling props of [`<Scroll>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md#scrolling): `pagingEnabled`, `snapToInterval`,
`snapToOffsets`, `snapToAlignment`, `disableIntervalMomentum`, `decelerationRate`, `bounces`, `contentInset`,
`contentOffset`, `keyboardShouldPersistTaps`, `scrollEventThrottle` and `scrollEnabled`. Lists do not zoom.

`ViewabilityConfig`:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `itemVisiblePercentThreshold` | `number` | Percent of an item that must be visible. |
| `viewAreaCoveragePercentThreshold` | `number` | Percent of the viewport an item must cover. Without either threshold, any visible pixel counts. |
| `minimumViewTime` | `number` | Milliseconds items must stay viewable before they are reported. |

`ViewToken<T>` is `{ item, key, index, isViewable }`.

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onScroll` | `ScrollEvent` | The offset changed. |
| `onScrollBeginDrag` / `onScrollEndDrag` | `{ x, y }` | Dragging started / stopped. |
| `onMomentumScrollBegin` / `onMomentumScrollEnd` | `{ x, y }` | A glide started / stopped. |
| `onScrollEnd` | `{ x, y }` | Scrolling came to rest. |
| `onEndReached` | none | Within `onEndReachedThreshold` viewports of the end. |
| `onViewableItemsChanged` | `{ viewableItems, changed }` | Viewability changed. |
| `onRefresh` | none | Pulled to refresh. |

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `scrollToIndex({ index, animated?, viewPosition?, viewOffset? })` | Scrolls item `index` into view. `viewPosition` places it: 0 at the start of the viewport (default), 0.5 in the middle, 1 at the end; `viewOffset` shifts it further. Resolved natively with the current (measured or estimated) item sizes. |
| `scrollToOffset({ offset, animated? })` | Scrolls to an offset along the list's axis. |
| `scrollToEnd({ animated? })` | Scrolls to the end of the content (the start of an inverted list). |
| `scrollTo({ x?, y?, animated? })` | Scrolls to an offset. |

## Examples

A grid with a header and viewability:

```tsx
const visible = signal("");
let list!: YNode;

<List
  ref={list}
  each={photos}
  numColumns={3}
  estimatedItemSize={120}
  contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 12, gap: 8 }}
  viewabilityConfig={{ itemVisiblePercentThreshold: 50 }}
  onViewableItemsChanged={({ viewableItems }) => visible.set(`${viewableItems.length} visible`)}
  ListHeaderComponent={<Text onPress={() => list.scrollToIndex({ index: 60, viewPosition: 0.5 })}>Jump to 60</Text>}
  style={{ flex: 1 }}
>
  {(photo) => <Image src={photo().url} style={{ height: 120, borderRadius: 8 }} />}
</List>;
```

A chat:

```tsx
<List each={messages()} inverted estimatedItemSize={64} keyboardDismissMode="interactive" style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  {(m) => <Bubble message={m()} />}
</List>
```

Item 0 is the newest message, drawn at the bottom; new messages prepended to `each` appear without moving what the
user is reading.

## Platform notes

- Inserting items above the visible rows keeps the visible rows in place on both platforms.
- Horizontal lists in right-to-left layouts are mirrored natively.
- Sticky headers are pinned natively on every scroll frame.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/list

---

# Canvas

A canvas is a view you draw yourself with the HTML Canvas 2D API: charts, gauges, rings, signatures, custom shapes.
The drawing function only records operations; the platform replays them natively (Core Graphics on iOS and Mac
Catalyst, `android.graphics.Canvas` on Android) at the screen's resolution.

```tsx
import { mount } from "nsh";
import { Canvas } from "nsh/canvas";

function Ring(props: { progress: number }) {
  return (
    <Canvas
      style={{ width: 120, height: 120 }}
      draw={(ctx, { width, height }) => {
        const cx = width / 2, cy = height / 2, r = width / 2 - 10;
        ctx.lineWidth = 12;
        ctx.lineCap = "round";
        ctx.strokeStyle = "#e5e7eb";
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, 0, Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.stroke();
        ctx.strokeStyle = "#6366f1";
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, -Math.PI / 2, -Math.PI / 2 + props.progress * Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.stroke();
      }}
    />
  );
}

mount(() => <Ring progress={0.7} />);
```

`Canvas` comes from [`nsh/canvas`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-canvas.md). It creates the native canvas view, measures it, and runs
your `draw` function with a context and the canvas's size.

## Props

`Canvas` takes the props of a [view](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md) (`style`, `class`, press and gesture props, `onLayout`, accessibility,
`ref`, …) plus:

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `draw` | `(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, size: { width: number; height: number }) => void` | Draws the canvas. Runs once the size is known, again when the canvas resizes, and again when signals it reads change. |

Give the canvas a size through its style (`width` / `height`, `flex`, `aspectRatio`): it has no content size of its own.

## When it redraws

`draw` is tracked like an effect: reading a signal inside it subscribes the drawing to that signal.

```tsx
const values = signal([12, 40, 28, 64]);

<Canvas
  style={{ height: 160 }}
  draw={(ctx, { width, height }) => {
    const data = values(); // a change of values() redraws
    const step = width / data.length;
    ctx.fillStyle = "#0969da";
    data.forEach((v, i) => ctx.fillRect(i * step + 4, height - v, step - 8, v));
  }}
/>;
```

Numbers and colors may also be [native animated values](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md) (`CanvasNumber`,
`CanvasPaint`): the platform then redraws on its own while they animate, without running `draw` or any JS per frame.

```tsx
import { Animated, createNativeValue } from "nsh/animated";
import { Canvas } from "nsh/canvas";

const angle = createNativeValue(0);
Animated.timing(angle, { toValue: Math.PI * 2, duration: 1000 }).start();

<Canvas
  style={{ width: 80, height: 80 }}
  draw={(ctx) => {
    ctx.translate(40, 40);
    ctx.rotate(angle); // animates natively
    ctx.fillStyle = "#cf222e";
    ctx.fillRect(-20, -4, 40, 8);
  }}
/>;
```

## The context

`CanvasRenderingContext2D` is a subset of the browser's: the state stack (`save`, `restore`), transforms, paths
(`moveTo`, `lineTo`, `arc`, `arcTo`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `roundRect`, Bézier curves), `fill` / `stroke` / `clip` (also of
a `Path2D`, which accepts SVG path data), rectangles, text (`fillText`, `strokeText`, `measureText`), linear / radial /
conic gradients, line dashes, shadows, `globalAlpha`, `globalCompositeOperation` and `drawImage` (images by URL or
imported asset). Every member is listed in the [`nsh/canvas` reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-canvas.md); the
[canvas guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/canvas.md) walks through drawing charts and animated graphics.

Coordinates are in points with the origin at the top left. `measureText` is synchronous and returns only `width`.

Not supported: `getImageData` / `putImageData`, `filter`, `isPointInPath` and SVG images.

## Events

The [view events](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md#events): `onPress`, `onLayout`, gestures and touches. To handle drawing-relative taps, read
`locationX` / `locationY` in `onTouchEnd`, or track a drag with `onResponderMove`.

## Ref methods

None of its own.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/canvas

---

# WebView

A web view shows a web page, or HTML you pass in, inside the app: WKWebView on iOS and Mac Catalyst,
`android.webkit.WebView` on Android. Because NSH renders with native views, a web view sits in the layout like any other
view: no overlay, no layering problems with views around it.

```tsx
import { signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { WebView, type WebViewNavigation } from "nsh/webview";

function Browser() {
  const nav = signal<WebViewNavigation | null>(null);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Text numberOfLines={1}>{nav()?.title ?? "Loading…"}</Text>
      <WebView
        source="https://example.com"
        style={{ flex: 1 }}
        onNavigationStateChange={(e) => nav.set(e)}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

`WebView` comes from [`nsh/webview`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-webview.md); `source` is required. The
[web view and video guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/web-view-and-video.md) covers messaging patterns and capabilities.

## Props

`WebView` takes the props of a [view](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md) (without `children`) plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string \| { uri: string } \| { html: string; baseUrl?: string }` | | A URL, or an HTML string with the base URL its relative links resolve against. |
| `injectedJavaScript` | `string` | | Runs after each page loads. |
| `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` | `string` | | Runs before each page's own scripts. |
| `userAgent` | `string` | | The browser's user agent string. |
| `javaScriptEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Pages run scripts. |
| `scrollEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | The user can scroll the page. |

| `ios` key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures` | `boolean` | Swipe from the edges to go back and forward. |

| `desktop` key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures` | `boolean` | macOS: swipe with two fingers on the trackpad to go back and forward; Windows: swipe on a touchscreen; Linux: swipe on the touchpad. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onLoadStart` | `WebViewNavigation` | A page started loading. |
| `onLoad` | `WebViewNavigation` | A page finished loading. |
| `onError` | `{ message }` | Loading failed. |
| `onNavigationStateChange` | `WebViewNavigation` | The URL, title, loading state or history changed. |
| `onMessage` | `{ data: string }` | The page called `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(data)`. |

`WebViewNavigation` is `{ url, title, loading, canGoBack, canGoForward }`.

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `reload()` | Reloads the page. |
| `goBack()` / `goForward()` | Moves in the page's history. |
| `stopLoading()` | Stops loading. |
| `injectJavaScript(script)` | Runs JavaScript in the page. |
| `postMessage(data)` | Sends a string to the page, which receives a `message` event on `window`. |

## Messaging

The app and the page exchange strings. The page posts with `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(data)`; the app posts
with the ref's `postMessage(data)`. Send JSON for structured data.

```tsx
import { signal, Text, View, type YNode } from "nsh";
import { WebView } from "nsh/webview";

const page = `<!doctype html>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width">
<button onclick="window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage('hello from the page')">Post to the app</button>
<p id="got"></p>
<script>
  window.addEventListener("message", (e) => { document.getElementById("got").textContent = e.data; });
</script>`;

function Bridge() {
  const message = signal("");
  let web!: YNode;
  return (
    <View style={{ gap: 12 }}>
      <WebView ref={web} source={{ html: page }} style={{ height: 200 }} onMessage={(e) => message.set(e.data)} />
      <Text onPress={() => web.postMessage("hi from the app")}>Post to the page · got: {message()}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Capabilities

If the app declares [capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md) in `nsh.json`, a web view may only show and
navigate to the hosts listed under `webview`. A refused `source` shows nothing; a refused top-level navigation (a
link the user taps) is cancelled natively.

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "webview": { "hosts": ["example.com", "*.example.com"] }
  }
}
```

## Platform notes

- iOS loads WebKit the first time a web view is created, so apps that never show one do not pay for it.
- On Android the page's `postMessage` calls arrive on a background thread and are forwarded to the app in order.
- To round the corners of a web view, give it `borderRadius` and `overflow: "hidden"`.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/web-view

---

# Video

A video view plays a video file or stream with the platform's player: AVPlayer on iOS and Mac Catalyst, MediaPlayer on
Android. Playback is controlled with props (`paused`, `muted`, `rate`, …), so the player follows your state like any
other view.

```tsx
import { signal, Text, View, type YNode } from "nsh";
import { Video } from "nsh/video";

function Player() {
  const paused = signal(true);
  const time = signal("");
  let video!: YNode;
  return (
    <View style={{ gap: 12 }}>
      <Video
        ref={video}
        source="https://example.com/clip.mp4"
        paused={paused()}
        repeat
        resizeMode="contain"
        style={{ height: 220, backgroundColor: "#000000" }}
        onProgress={(e) => time.set(`${e.currentTime.toFixed(1)} / ${e.duration.toFixed(1)} s`)}
      />
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 16 }}>
        <Text onPress={() => paused.set(!paused())}>{paused() ? "Play" : "Pause"}</Text>
        <Text onPress={() => video.seek(0)}>Restart</Text>
        <Text>{time()}</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

`Video` comes from [`nsh/video`](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-video.md); `source` is required. See the
[web view and video guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/web-view-and-video.md).

## Props

`Video` takes the props of a [view](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md) (without `children`) plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string \| { uri: string }` | | The video's URL. |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | Playback is paused. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` | No sound. |
| `volume` | `number` | `1` | 0..1. |
| `rate` | `number` | `1` | The playback speed. |
| `repeat` | `boolean` | `false` | Plays again from the start at the end. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the platform's playback controls. |
| `resizeMode` | `"cover" \| "contain" \| "stretch" \| "center"` | | How the video fits its box. |
| `progressUpdateInterval` | `number` | `250` | Milliseconds between `onProgress` events. |

Give the video a size through its style; it does not size itself to the video. Use the `width` and `height` of `onLoad`
to set an `aspectRatio` if you need the video's own proportions.

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onLoadStart` | none | Loading began. |
| `onLoad` | `{ duration, width, height }` | The video is ready: its duration in seconds and its size. |
| `onProgress` | `{ currentTime, duration }` | Every `progressUpdateInterval` while playing (seconds). |
| `onBuffer` | `{ isBuffering }` | Playback stalled for data / resumed. |
| `onEnd` | none | Playback reached the end (with `repeat`, at the end of each loop). |
| `onError` | `{ message }` | Loading or playback failed. |

```tsx
const ratio = signal(16 / 9);
<Video source={url} style={{ width: "100%", aspectRatio: ratio() }} onLoad={(e) => ratio.set(e.width / e.height)} />;
```

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `seek(seconds)` | Jumps to a time. |

## Capabilities

If the app declares [capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md), video sources must be allowed by `network`;
a refused source shows nothing.

## Platform notes

- iOS draws the video in an `AVPlayerLayer`, or in the system player view with `controls`; AVFoundation is loaded the
  first time a video is created.
- Android plays with MediaPlayer on a TextureView, with a MediaController for `controls`.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/video

---

# Modal

A modal presents content over the rest of the app in its own native window layer: a presented view controller on iOS
and Mac Catalyst, a Dialog on Android. It is used for full-screen flows, sheets and dialogs. The system's own gestures
(swiping a sheet down, the Android back button) work, and are decided natively.

```tsx
import { signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Modal, SafeAreaView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function Example() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24 }}>
      <Button title="Open" onPress={() => open.set(true)} />
      <Modal visible={open()} ios={{ presentationStyle: "pageSheet" }} onRequestClose={() => open.set(false)}>
        <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1, padding: 20, gap: 12, backgroundColor: "#ffffff" }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700" }}>A sheet</Text>
          <Button title="Close" onPress={() => open.set(false)} />
        </SafeAreaView>
      </Modal>
    </View>
  );
}
```

`Modal` comes from [`nsh/ui/mobile`](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md). It is presented while `visible` is not `false` and
dismissed when it becomes `false`, and it gives its content the modal's safe-area insets, which `SafeAreaView` and
`useSafeAreaInsets()` inside it read.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Presented while true. |
| `animationType` | `"slide" \| "fade" \| "none"` | `"slide"` | How the modal appears. |
| `transparent` | `boolean` | `false` | The background shows what is behind (for dialogs drawn by the app). |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `false` | The user closes it natively (iOS sheet swiped down, Android back button), then `onRequestClose` and `onDismiss` follow. Without it, those gestures only ask to close. |
| `onRequestClose` | `() => void` | | The user asked to close: set `visible` to false to close it. |
| `onShow` | `() => void` | | The modal finished appearing. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | | The modal finished disappearing. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | | The modal's root view. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | | The content. |

| `ios` key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `presentationStyle` | `"fullScreen" \| "pageSheet" \| "formSheet"` | `"fullScreen"` | `pageSheet` and `formSheet` keep what is behind visible; `formSheet` is a smaller centered sheet on large screens. |
| `supportedOrientations` | `("portrait" \| "portrait-upside-down" \| "landscape" \| "landscape-left" \| "landscape-right")[]` | the presenter's | The orientations the modal allows. |

| `android` key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `statusBarTranslucent` | `boolean` | `false` | The content reaches under the status bar; otherwise it starts below it. |

## Controlled by default

A modal is controlled: when the user swipes a sheet down or presses back, NSH asks with `onRequestClose` and the modal
stays until you set `visible` to `false`. This lets you confirm before closing. Since the main thread never waits for
JS, the decision cannot be made in the handler; `dismissible` tells the platform beforehand that it may close the
modal by itself:

```tsx
<Modal visible={open()} dismissible ios={{ presentationStyle: "pageSheet" }} onRequestClose={() => open.set(false)}>
  …
</Modal>
```

With `dismissible`, the sheet follows the finger and closes natively; `onRequestClose` then tells you to update your
state.

## A dialog

A transparent modal with a fade draws its own dialog over a dimmed background:

```tsx
<Modal visible={confirm()} transparent animationType="fade" onRequestClose={() => confirm.set(false)}>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.4)", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", padding: 32 }}>
    <View style={{ alignSelf: "stretch", backgroundColor: "#ffffff", borderRadius: 14, padding: 20, gap: 12 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" }}>Delete this item?</Text>
      <Button title="Delete" onPress={remove} />
    </View>
  </View>
</Modal>
```

For a system alert or action sheet, use `Alert` and `ActionSheet` from `nsh/ui/mobile` instead
([alert](https://nsh.dev/components/alert.md), [action sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md)). For a sheet drawn by the app, see
[`Sheet`](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md).

## Ref methods

None.

## Platform notes

- Android: the back button goes to the topmost modal first, before stacks and `BackHandler` listeners.
- `presentationStyle` and `supportedOrientations` are iOS only and ignored on Android. On a desktop, `desktop={{ presentationStyle }}`
  makes `pageSheet` / `formSheet` a card centered in the window over a dimmed backdrop.
- Without `statusBarTranslucent`, an Android modal's content starts below the status bar.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/modal

---

# If / Each

`<If>` and `<Each>` are the components for conditional and repeated content. They create no native view; they decide which
elements exist. Both are compiled into calls to the native renderer, which updates only what changed: `<If>` swaps a
branch when the condition's truthiness changes, `<Each>` adds, moves and removes rows by key instead of rebuilding the
list.

```tsx
<View>
  <If when={user()} else={<Text>Signed out</Text>}>
    <Text>Hello, {user()!.name}</Text>
  </If>
  <Each of={todos()}>{(todo) => <Text>{todo().title}</Text>}</Each>
</View>
```

They are globals: they need no import (a binding of the same name in scope takes their place). Inside JSX expressions you can still use plain JavaScript (`cond ? a : b`, `items.map(…)`), but those
rebuild their elements every time what they read changes; `<If>` and `<Each>` keep the elements that stay.

## `<If>`

Renders its children while `when` is truthy, else the `else` element (or nothing).

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `when` | `unknown` | The condition. Only its truthiness matters. |
| `else` | `JSX.Element` | Rendered while `when` is falsy. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | Rendered while `when` is truthy. |

The branch is created again only when the truthiness of `when` changes. A `when` that goes from one truthy value to
another (`user()` changing from one object to another) keeps the branch, and the expressions inside it update on their
own.

```tsx
const loading = signal(true);

<If when={!loading()} else={<Text style={{ color: "#6e7781" }}>Loading…</Text>}>
  <Profile />
</If>;
```

## `<Each>`

Renders `children(item, index)` for each item of `of`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `of` | `readonly any[] \| null \| undefined` | The items. `null` and `undefined` render nothing. |
| `key` | `(item: any) => unknown` | The identity of an item. Default: the item itself (objects by identity, primitives by value). |
| `children` | `(item: () => any, index: () => number) => JSX.Element` | Renders one row. |

The row function gets **accessors**, not values: call `item()` and `index()`. When `of` changes, rows whose key is still
there are kept (and moved if their position changed); their `item()` and `index()` update, and only the expressions
reading them run again. New keys get new rows; rows whose key is gone are removed.

```tsx
interface Todo {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  done: boolean;
}

const todos = signal<Todo[]>([]);

<Each of={todos()} key={(t: Todo) => t.id}>
  {(todo, index) => (
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
      <Text>{index() + 1}.</Text>
      <Text style={{ textDecorationLine: todo().done ? "line-through" : "none" }}>{todo().title}</Text>
    </View>
  )}
</Each>;
```

### Choosing a key

- Items replaced by new objects on every update (immutable updates, `{ ...t, done: true }`) need a `key`, usually an id.
  Without it each new object is a new row and its elements are created again.
- Arrays of strings or numbers work without a key: they are compared by value.
- Each row has its own owner: effects and cleanups created in a row end when the row is removed.

> [!NOTE]
> `Each` is generic: TypeScript infers the item type from `of`, so the row function's `todo()` and the `key` parameter
> are typed without annotations.

## `<Each>` or a list

`<Each>` creates every row. That is right for tens or a few hundred items, in a `<View>` or a [`<Scroll>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md).
For long or unbounded data, use a [list](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md): it creates only the rows near the viewport and recycles them.

See [JSX and components](https://nsh.dev/docs/jsx-and-components.md) and [reactivity](https://nsh.dev/docs/reactivity.md) for how expressions
update.

Source: https://nsh.dev/elements/control-flow

---

# Mobile UI

`nsh/ui/mobile` is NSH's UI set for phones and tablets: buttons, cards, lists, text fields, sheets, safe areas, the
keyboard, the status bar, system dialogs and navigation. Import what you need:

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Group, Sheet, Stack, Screen, createNavigator } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

Use it on top of the [host elements](https://nsh.dev/elements.md) (`<View>`, `<Text>`, `<Input>`, ...). The elements are
the building blocks every UI set uses. The components are a finished mobile look built from those elements.

## How the components work

The components are written in Rust, not in JavaScript. In your app a `<Button>` is still one JSX node. Its props go to
the native core, and the core renders the button from host elements in the same layout pass as the rest of your UI.
Its events come back to your handlers. This has a few practical consequences:

- **The same look on iOS and Android.** A component draws itself with NSH's own views, not UIKit or Android
  widgets, so a `Button` looks the same on both platforms. The exceptions are [Alert](https://nsh.dev/components/alert.md) and
  [ActionSheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md), which show the platform's system dialogs.
- **Interaction stays native.** Press feedback, the drag of a [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md) and the repeat of a held
  [Stepper](https://nsh.dev/components/stepper.md) button run in the core or on the UI thread. JS only receives the events (`onPress`,
  `onChange`, `onClose`, ...).
- **Typed from the source.** The TypeScript declarations in `.nsh/types/nsh/ui/mobile.d.ts` are generated from the
  Rust props, so your editor shows each prop and its documentation.
- **Your content stays yours.** Slots (`header`, `footer`), children and list rows are your JSX. The component
  positions them but never creates or changes them, so their signals, handlers and refs work as usual.

Every component accepts `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout` and `ref` on its root view
(`ComponentHostProps`). Your `class` is applied after the component's own styles, so it overrides them:

```tsx
<Button title="Continue" class="rounded-full" onPress={next} />
<Card class="mx-4" variant="outlined">…</Card>
```

## Components

| Component | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Button](https://nsh.dev/components/button.md) | A press target with a label: `primary`, `secondary`, `danger` or `plain` |
| [Card](https://nsh.dev/components/card.md) | A rounded surface with an optional header and footer |
| [Group](https://nsh.dev/components/group.md) | Settings-style rows in a rounded box, divided by hairlines |
| [ListView](https://nsh.dev/components/list-view.md) | A virtualized list of your rows, plain or inset |
| [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md) | A view padded by the safe area, a screen's header or a modal's insets |
| [SelectList](https://nsh.dev/components/select-list.md) | A scrolling list of options with a check mark on the chosen one |
| [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md) | A bottom sheet over a dimmed backdrop, dragged down to close |
| [StatusBar](https://nsh.dev/components/status-bar.md) | The status bar's content color and visibility, rendered or set by function |
| [Stepper](https://nsh.dev/components/stepper.md) | A number with − and + buttons; holding a button repeats |
| [TextField](https://nsh.dev/components/text-field.md) | A labeled text input with a clear button |
| [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md) | Keeps content outside scroll views above the software keyboard |

Modules and navigation:

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Alert](https://nsh.dev/components/alert.md) | `Alert.alert(title, message?, buttons?, options?)`: a system alert, resolves with the button's index |
| [ActionSheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md) | `ActionSheet.show(options)`: a system action sheet, resolves with the action's index |
| [Keyboard](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md) | `Keyboard.dismiss()` and the reactive `keyboard()` accessor |
| [Navigation](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md) | `createNavigator`, `Stack`, `Screen` and `Modal`: native navigation stacks and modals |

The set also re-exports three environment accessors from the runtime: `safeArea()`, `keyboard()` and
`useSafeAreaInsets()` (see [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md) and [Keyboard](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md)).

## Theming

All components use colors from one theme and never use fixed color values. Each color has a light and a dark value.
When the system switches between light and dark appearance, the components change color natively, with no render and
no JS.

The default theme is gpui-kit's default theme, a neutral black-and-white palette, with mobile corner radii. To use
your own theme, set `"theme"` in `nsh.json`. Its value is the path of a theme file, relative to `nsh.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "My App",
  "id": "com.example.myapp",
  "theme": "brand-theme.json"
}
```

You can also write the theme's content inline as the value. The format is gpui-kit's theme file format. Each entry in
`themes` sets the colors for one appearance (`mode`: `"light"` or `"dark"`; without `mode`, an entry is light):

```json
{
  "themes": [
    {
      "mode": "light",
      "radius": 8,
      "radius.lg": 14,
      "font.size": 16,
      "colors": {
        "primary.background": "#7c3aed",
        "primary.foreground": "white",
        "border": "neutral-200"
      }
    },
    {
      "mode": "dark",
      "colors": {
        "primary.background": "#a78bfa",
        "primary.foreground": "neutral-950"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

- Your theme is applied over the default theme, so you only list what you change.
- Colors are CSS colors (`#7c3aed`, `rgb(…)`, `white`) or names from Tailwind's default palette (`neutral-900`,
  `red-500`). Custom colors from `nsh.json`'s `tailwind` key are not available here.
- `radius` is the corner radius of controls (buttons, inputs, stepper buttons). `radius.lg` is the radius of large
  surfaces (cards, groups, inset lists, sheets). `font.size` is the base font size of button labels, card headers and the stepper. All values are in points.
- If you leave out a pressed color (`primary.active.background`, `secondary.active.background`,
  `danger.active.background`, ...), NSH derives it from the base color: 12% darker in light mode, 12% lighter in
  dark mode.
- Keys that only gpui-kit's desktop components use (sidebars, title bars, ...) are ignored, so you can use a gpui-kit
  theme file as it is.
- The bundler checks the theme when it builds. A missing file, invalid JSON, an unknown `mode` or a value that is not
  a color fails the build with an `nsh.json: theme: …` error.

These are the theme keys the mobile components use, with their default light and dark values:

| Key | Light | Dark | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | `white` | `neutral-950` | ListView, SelectList and TextField backgrounds, the Sheet panel |
| `foreground` | `neutral-950` | `neutral-50` | Text in ListView, SelectList and Stepper; Plain buttons |
| `border` | `neutral-200` | `neutral-800` | Dividers, Card borders |
