| `primary.background` / `.active.background` / `.foreground` | `neutral-900` / `neutral-950` / `neutral-50` | `neutral-50` / `neutral-200` / `neutral-900` | Primary buttons; SelectList check mark, TextField selection (`primary.background`) |
| `secondary.background` / `.active.background` / `.foreground` | `neutral-200` / `neutral-300` / `neutral-900` | `neutral-800` / `#212121` / `neutral-50` | Secondary buttons, Stepper buttons |
| `danger.background` / `.active.background` / `.foreground` | `red-500` / `red-600` / `neutral-50` | `red-400` / `red-500` / `red-600` | Danger buttons |
| `accent.background` | `neutral-100` | `neutral-800` | Plain buttons while pressed |
| `muted.background` | `neutral-100` | `neutral-800` | Inset ListView page, Sheet grabber, TextField clear button |
| `muted.foreground` | `neutral-500` | `neutral-400` | Group captions, TextField labels and placeholders |
| `group_box.background` / `.foreground` | `#f5f5f5` / `#171717` | `neutral-950` / `neutral-50` | Card and Group surfaces |
| `input.border` | `neutral-200` | `#2f2f2f` | TextField border |
| `ring` | `neutral-400` | `neutral-500` | TextField border while focused |
| `list.active.background` | `#bfdbfe33` | `#1e40af33` | SelectList row while pressed |
| `overlay` | `#0000000d` | `#00000033` | Sheet backdrop |

> [!TIP]
> To adjust one component instance, pass `class` or `style`; they apply to the component's root view and override
> its styles. To change the look of a component everywhere, change the theme.

## Related

- [Styling](https://nsh.dev/docs/styling.md) and [Tailwind](https://nsh.dev/docs/tailwind.md): styling your own views.
- [Navigation guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/navigation.md) and [Forms and keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).
- [Platform-specific code](https://nsh.dev/docs/platform-specific.md): `ios={{…}}` / `android={{…}}` props.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components

---

# Button

`Button` is a press target with a text label. It is filled with a theme color, darkens while pressed and reports
presses with `onPress`. It looks the same on iOS and Android.

```tsx
import { Button } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Button } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const count = signal(0);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12, justifyContent: "center" }}>
      <Text>{`Pressed ${count()} times`}</Text>
      <Button title="Press me" onPress={() => count.set(count() + 1)} />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

The button lays its label out in a row, centered, with 16 pt of horizontal and 12 pt of vertical padding. In a column
it stretches to the column's width, like any view. Pass `class` or `style` to size or round it differently:

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
  <Button class="flex-1" title="Cancel" variant="secondary" onPress={cancel} />
  <Button class="flex-1" title="Save" onPress={save} />
</View>
```

## Variants

```tsx
<Button title="Save" />                         {/* primary (default) */}
<Button title="Not now" variant="secondary" />
<Button title="Delete" variant="danger" />
<Button title="Learn more" variant="plain" />
```

| Variant | Background | Pressed | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primary` (default) | `primary.background` | `primary.active.background` | `primary.foreground` |
| `secondary` | `secondary.background` | `secondary.active.background` | `secondary.foreground` |
| `danger` | `danger.background` | `danger.active.background` | `danger.foreground` |
| `plain` | transparent | `accent.background` | `foreground` |

Use `danger` for destructive actions and `plain` for low-emphasis actions such as a card footer's secondary action.

## Disabled

```tsx
<Button title="Submit" disabled={!valid()} onPress={submit} />
```

A disabled button is shown at 50% opacity, does not respond to presses and shows no press feedback.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | required | The label. |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "danger" \| "plain"` | `"primary"` | The look (see [Variants](#variants)). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No presses, no feedback, 50% opacity. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string \| null` | `title` | What screen readers read, when `title` is not enough. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the button's root view. `class` and `style` override the button's own styles. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onPress` | none | The button was pressed (released inside it). Not sent while `disabled`. |

## Theming

The label uses the theme's `font.size` (16 pt by default) with a semibold weight. The corners use `radius` (12 pt by
default). The colors come from the theme keys in the [variants table](#variants). See
[Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

The button has the `button` role. Screen readers read `accessibilityLabel` if you set it, otherwise `title`. While
`disabled`, the button is reported as disabled.

## Related

- [View](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md): `onPress`, `activeOpacity` and `underlayColor` for custom press targets.
- [Touch and gestures](https://nsh.dev/docs/touch-and-gestures.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/button

---

# Card

`Card` is a rounded surface that groups related content. It can have a header above the content and a footer below
it. The header, the content and the footer are your JSX; the card adds the surface, the padding and the divider.

```tsx
import { Card } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Card } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48 }}>
      <Card
        header={<Text>Weekly summary</Text>}
        footer={<Button title="Details" variant="plain" onPress={() => console.log("details")} />}
      >
        <Text>You walked 42 km this week.</Text>
        <Text>That is 8 km more than last week.</Text>
      </Card>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Layout

- **Header**: 16 pt padding at the sides and the top. Text in the header is semibold and 1 pt larger than the theme's
  `font.size`, so a plain `<Text>` works as a title. A header can be any JSX, for example an avatar and a name in a
  row.
- **Content**: the children are stacked in a column with 8 pt gaps. With a header, the content has 8 pt padding at the
  top and 16 pt at the sides and the bottom. Without a header, it has 16 pt padding on all sides.
- **Footer**: a row aligned to the end, with 8 pt gaps, 16 pt horizontal and 12 pt vertical padding, and a divider
  above it. Put actions here.

```tsx
<Card
  variant="outlined"
  header={
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 10 }}>
      <View style={{ width: 32, height: 32, borderRadius: 16, backgroundColor: "#a78bfa" }} />
      <Text>Ada Lovelace</Text>
    </View>
  }
  footer={
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
      <Button title="Ignore" variant="plain" onPress={ignore} />
      <Button title="Reply" onPress={reply} />
    </View>
  }
>
  <Text>Can we move the meeting to Thursday?</Text>
</Card>
```

The header and footer only exist while you pass them: `header={cond() ? <Text>…</Text> : undefined}` adds and
removes the header, and the content's padding changes to match.

## Variants

| Variant | Look |
|---|---|
| `elevated` (default) | A 1 pt border and a small shadow. |
| `outlined` | A 1 pt border, no shadow. |

```tsx
<Card>…</Card>
<Card variant="outlined">…</Card>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `"elevated" \| "outlined"` | `"elevated"` | Whether the card has a shadow. |
| `header` | `JSX.Element` | none | Above the content: a title or an avatar row. Its text is semibold. |
| `footer` | `JSX.Element` | none | Below the content, after a divider: actions, aligned to the end. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The content. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the card's root view. `class` and `style` override the card's own styles. |

`Card` has no events. Put handlers on your own content.

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Surface | `group_box.background` |
| Text color (inherited by the content) | `group_box.foreground` |
| Border and footer divider | `border` |
| Corner radius | `radius.lg` (16 pt by default) |
| Header text size | `font.size` + 1 |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

The card adds no role or label. Screen readers read the header, content and footer in order, as separate elements.

## Related

- [Group](https://nsh.dev/components/group.md): rows in a rounded box with dividers.
- [Button](https://nsh.dev/components/button.md): actions in a footer.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/card

---

# Group

`Group` shows rows in a rounded box with a hairline between them, like a section of a settings screen. Each JSX child
becomes one row. You can add a short caption above the box and an explanation below it.

```tsx
import { Group } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Group } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const sounds = signal(true);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f5f5f5", padding: 16, paddingTop: 48 }}>
      <Group
        header={<Text>NOTIFICATIONS</Text>}
        footer={<Text>Sounds play for new messages only.</Text>}
      >
        <Text>Show previews</Text>
        <View
          onPress={() => sounds.set(!sounds())}
          style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}
        >
          <Text>Sounds</Text>
          <Text>{sounds() ? "On" : "Off"}</Text>
        </View>
      </Group>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Rows

Group wraps each child in a row with 16 pt horizontal and 12 pt vertical padding and a minimum height of 44 pt, the
smallest comfortable touch target. The content is centered vertically. Every row except the first has a 1 pt divider
at its top.

A row is whatever you pass, so put a `<View>` with `flexDirection: "row"` in it to place a label and a value, and an
`onPress` on that view to make the row pressable. When a child is added or removed, for example with
[`<If>` or `<Each>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/control-flow.md), the group updates the rows and dividers.

```tsx
<Group header={<Text>DEVICES</Text>}>
  <Each of={devices()}>
    {(device) => (
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
        <Text>{device().name}</Text>
        <Text style={{ color: "#737373" }}>{device().status}</Text>
      </View>
    )}
  </Each>
</Group>
```

> [!TIP]
> Group renders every row. For long or unbounded lists, use [ListView](https://nsh.dev/components/list-view.md) with `variant="inset"`,
> which has the same rounded-box look and only creates the rows that are near the screen.

## Header and footer

The header is placed 16 pt in from the left, in small (`text-sm`) muted text. The footer is in extra-small
(`text-xs`) muted text. There is an 8 pt gap between the header, the box and the footer. Both are optional.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `header` | `JSX.Element` | none | Above the box: a short caption. |
| `footer` | `JSX.Element` | none | Below the box: an explanation. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The rows, one per child. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the group's root view (the column holding the header, box and footer). |

`Group` has no events.

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Box | `group_box.background`, corner radius `radius.lg` |
| Row text color | `group_box.foreground` |
| Dividers | `border` |
| Header and footer text | `muted.foreground` |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

Group adds no roles or labels. Each row's content is read as you wrote it. If a row is pressable, give its view an
`accessibilityRole` (for example `"button"`) and, if needed, an `accessibilityLabel`. See
[Accessibility](https://nsh.dev/docs/accessibility.md).

## Related

- [Card](https://nsh.dev/components/card.md): one surface with a header and footer.
- [ListView](https://nsh.dev/components/list-view.md): virtualized rows with the same inset look.
- [Stepper](https://nsh.dev/components/stepper.md): a common control inside a row.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/group

---

# ListView

`ListView` is a scrolling list of rows that you render. Like [List](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md), it only creates the rows
near the screen and reuses their cells as you scroll, so a list of thousands of items costs about as much as the
visible rows. ListView adds the look: padding around each row, dividers between rows and an optional inset style.

```tsx
import { ListView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

Pass the data as `each` and a row renderer as the child function, the same way as with `List`:

```tsx
import { mount, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { ListView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

const people = Array.from({ length: 1000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i, name: `Person ${i + 1}` }));

function App() {
  return (
    <ListView each={people} keyExtractor={(p) => String(p.id)}>
      {(person, index) => (
        <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
          <Text style={{ fontWeight: "600" }}>{person().name}</Text>
          <Text style={{ color: "#737373" }}>{`#${index() + 1}`}</Text>
        </View>
      )}
    </ListView>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

The row function receives accessors: `person()` and `index()`. It runs once per cell, and the accessors change when
the cell is reused for another item. Keep per-item state in your data, not in signals created inside the row. See
[Lists](https://nsh.dev/docs/lists.md) for details on recycling.

ListView fills its parent (`flex: 1`). Put it in a parent with a height, such as the root view or a
[Screen](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md).

## Rows

ListView wraps each row in a view with 16 pt horizontal and 12 pt vertical padding and a minimum height of 48 pt. The
content is centered vertically. With `dividers` (the default), every row except the first has a 1 pt divider at its
top.

The end of the list has extra bottom padding equal to the safe area's bottom inset. This lets the last row scroll
above the home indicator.

## Variants

| Variant | Look |
|---|---|
| `plain` (default) | Full-width rows on the `background` color. |
| `inset` | Rows in a rounded box with a 16 pt margin, on a `muted.background` page, like grouped settings. The first row has rounded top corners and the last row has rounded bottom corners. |

```tsx
<ListView variant="inset" each={settings} dividers={false}>
  {(item) => <Text>{item().label}</Text>}
</ListView>
```

## Headers, footers and list behavior

ListView accepts the data props of [List](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md). ListView sets the layout itself (estimated row size,
padding), so `List`'s layout props such as `numColumns`, `horizontal`, `estimatedItemSize` and
`contentContainerStyle` are not available.

```tsx
<ListView
  each={messages()}
  keyExtractor={(m) => m.id}
  ListHeaderComponent={<Text style={{ padding: 16, fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" }}>Inbox</Text>}
  ListEmptyComponent={<Text style={{ padding: 16 }}>No messages</Text>}
  refreshing={loading()}
  onRefresh={reload}
  onEndReached={loadMore}
>
  {(m) => <Text numberOfLines={1}>{m().subject}</Text>}
</ListView>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `each` | `readonly T[]` | required | The items. |
| `children` | `(item: () => T, index: () => number) => JSX.Element` | required | Renders one row. Called once per recycled cell. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "inset"` | `"plain"` | Full-width rows, or rows in a rounded box with a margin. |
| `dividers` | `boolean` | `true` | Hairlines between rows. |
| `keyExtractor` | `(item: T, index: number) => string` | `item.key`, `item.id` or the index | The key of an item. |
| `ListHeaderComponent` | `ListSlot` | none | Shown before the first row (a component or an element). |
| `ListFooterComponent` | `ListSlot` | none | Shown after the last row. |
| `ListEmptyComponent` | `ListSlot` | none | Shown instead of the rows while `each` is empty. |
| `stickyHeaderIndices` | `number[]` | none | Items that stick to the top while scrolled past. |
| `initialScrollIndex` | `number` | none | Scrolls to this item before the first frame. |
| `refreshing` | `boolean` | `false` | The pull-to-refresh spinner shows. |
| `onRefresh` | `() => void` | none | The user pulled to refresh. Set `refreshing` while you load. |
| `onEndReached` | `() => void` | none | The end of the list came near (to load more). |
| `onEndReachedThreshold` | `number` | `1` | How close to the end, in viewports, `onEndReached` fires. |
| `onViewableItemsChanged` | `(info) => void` | none | Items became viewable or stopped being viewable. |
| `viewabilityConfig` | `ViewabilityConfig` | none | When items count as viewable. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the list's root view. |

`ListView` has no events of its own; the list props above are its callbacks.

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Page background | `background` (plain), `muted.background` (inset) |
| Row background (inset) | `background` |
| Text color | `foreground` |
| Dividers | `border` |
| Inset box corners | `radius.lg` |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

ListView adds no roles or labels to rows. If a row is pressable, give its view an `accessibilityRole` and, if needed,
an `accessibilityLabel`.

## Related

- [List](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md): the virtualized list ListView is built on, with full layout control.
- [Lists guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/lists.md): recycling, keys, paging.
- [SelectList](https://nsh.dev/components/select-list.md): a list of options with a check mark.
- [Group](https://nsh.dev/components/group.md): a few rows in a rounded box, without virtualization.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/list-view

---

# SafeAreaView

`SafeAreaView` adds padding so that its content is not covered by the notch, the status bar, the home indicator, a
navigation header or the Mac Catalyst title bar. The padding is the insets **where the view renders**. Inside a
[Screen](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md) these are the insets below the screen's header. Inside a [Modal](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md#modal)
they are the modal's insets. Elsewhere they are the surface's safe area.

```tsx
import { SafeAreaView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, Text } from "nsh";
import { SafeAreaView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  return (
    <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#fff8c5", padding: 16 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700" }}>Never under the notch</Text>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

The insets are **added** to the view's own padding. In the example, the content starts 16 pt below the top inset, and
the background color fills the whole area, including the area behind the status bar.

## Choosing edges

By default all four edges are padded. Pass `edges` to pad only some of them, for example when a tab bar or a custom
bottom bar handles the bottom inset:

```tsx
<SafeAreaView edges={["top", "left", "right"]} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  …
</SafeAreaView>
```

## Screens and modals

A [Screen](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md) with a visible, opaque header already places its content below the header, so the top
inset there is 0. SafeAreaView is mainly useful in these cases:

- the root of an app without a navigation stack,
- a screen with `headerShown={false}` or `headerTransparent`,
- the content of a full-screen [Modal](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md#modal).

```tsx
<Screen headerShown={false}>
  <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
    <Button title="Back" onPress={() => nav.pop()} />
  </SafeAreaView>
</Screen>
```

## Reading the insets

When you need the numbers, for example to pad a bottom bar yourself, use one of the two accessors. Both return an
`Insets` object (`{ top, right, bottom, left }` in points) and are reactive: code that reads them runs again when they
change, for example on rotation.

| Export | Returns |
|---|---|
| `safeArea()` | The surface's safe area: the parts not covered by system UI (notch, home indicator, title bar). |
| `useSafeAreaInsets()` | Call it in a component. It returns an accessor of the insets where that component renders: the nearest screen's (below its header), the nearest modal's, or else the surface's safe area. These are the same insets SafeAreaView uses. |

```tsx
import { Text, View } from "nsh";
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function BottomBar() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
  return (
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", padding: 8, paddingBottom: 8 + insets().bottom }}>
      <Text>Bottom bar</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edges` | `("top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left")[] \| null` | all four | The edges to pad. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The content. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the view. Its padding is added to the insets. |

`SafeAreaView` has no events and uses no theme colors.

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: the insets come from UIKit's safe area (status bar, notch or Dynamic Island, home indicator).
- **Android**: NSH reports only the parts of the system bars and the display cutout that overlap the NSH view. When
  NSH is [embedded](https://nsh.dev/docs/embedding-android.md) below a native toolbar, the view gets no top inset.
- **Mac Catalyst**: the top inset is the window's title bar.

## Related

- [Keyboard](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md) and [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md): avoiding the software keyboard.
- [Navigation](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md): screens and modals provide their insets.
- [Device and environment](https://nsh.dev/docs/device-and-environment.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view

---

# SelectList

`SelectList` shows a scrolling list of text options and marks the chosen one with a check mark. The core renders the
rows from your array of strings, so a list of thousands of options costs about as much as the visible rows, and no
JS runs while scrolling.

```tsx
import { SelectList } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { SelectList } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

const languages = ["English", "Deutsch", "Español", "Français", "日本語", "中文"];

function App() {
  const chosen = signal<number | null>(0);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, paddingTop: 48 }}>
      <Text style={{ padding: 16 }}>{`Language: ${chosen() === null ? "none" : languages[chosen()!]}`}</Text>
      <SelectList options={languages} value={chosen()} onSelect={(i) => chosen.set(i)} />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

SelectList fills its parent (`flex: 1`). To show it inside a scroll view or next to other content, give it a parent
with a fixed height:

```tsx
<View style={{ height: 240, borderRadius: 12, overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <SelectList options={cities} onSelect={(i) => console.log(cities[i])} />
</View>
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

- **Controlled**: pass `value` (the chosen index, or `null` for none) and update it in `onSelect`. The check mark
  follows `value`. If you do not update `value`, the check mark does not move.
- **Uncontrolled**: leave out `value`. The list keeps the choice itself and moves the check mark on each press.
  `onSelect` still reports each choice.

`onSelect` is called on every press, also when the user presses the option that is already chosen.

## Rows

Each row is at least 48 pt tall, with 16 pt horizontal padding, the option's text, and a check mark (✓) at the end of
the chosen row. Rows are separated by 1 pt dividers and highlighted while pressed.

> [!NOTE]
> Options are matched by their text when the array changes, so rows keep their place when you insert or remove
> options. Use unique option strings.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | `string[]` | required | The options, in order. |
| `value` | `number \| null` | none (uncontrolled) | The index of the chosen option, when the app controls it. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the list's root view. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onSelect` | `number`: the option's index | The user pressed an option. |

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Row background | `background` |
| Row while pressed | `list.active.background` |
| Text | `foreground` |
| Check mark | `primary.background` |
| Dividers | `border` |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

Each row has the `button` role, and the chosen row is reported as **selected**. Screen readers read the option's text.

## Related

- [ListView](https://nsh.dev/components/list-view.md): rows you render yourself.
- [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md): show a SelectList in a bottom sheet as a picker.
- [ActionSheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md): a short list of actions in a system dialog.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/select-list

---

# Sheet

`Sheet` is a panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen over a dimmed backdrop. The user closes it by dragging
it down, tapping the backdrop or pressing the Android back button. The drag and the animations run natively: the panel
follows the finger on the UI thread, with no JS and no render per frame.

```tsx
import { Sheet } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

`Sheet` is controlled. It is shown while `open` is true. When the user closes it, `onClose` is called, and you set
`open` to false:

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Sheet } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48 }}>
      <Button title="Share" onPress={() => open.set(true)} />
      <Sheet open={open()} onClose={() => open.set(false)}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }}>Share the photo</Text>
        <Button title="Copy link" variant="secondary" onPress={() => open.set(false)} />
        <Button title="Done" onPress={() => open.set(false)} />
      </Sheet>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Behavior

- **Opening**: when `open` becomes true, the panel slides in from below the screen with a spring, and the backdrop
  fades in as the panel rises.
- **Dragging**: the panel follows a vertical drag. When the user releases it more than 120 pt below its resting
  position, or flicks it down faster than 900 pt/s, it closes. Otherwise it springs back, continuing at the speed of
  the flick.
- **Closing by the user** (drag, backdrop tap, Android back button): the panel slides down in 220 ms, then `onClose`
  is called. Always set `open` to false in `onClose`: while `open` stays true, the sheet's modal stays presented
  after the panel has slid out of view, and it keeps covering the screen.
- **Closing from your code**: setting `open` to false removes the sheet at once, without the slide-down animation, and
  does not call `onClose`.
- **Content**: the children are made when the sheet opens and released once it is closed, so they start fresh each
  time (a form is empty again, a component reads the current state when it is made). Keep what must survive a close
  in a signal outside the sheet.

The sheet is presented in a transparent [modal](https://nsh.dev/elements/modal.md), so it covers everything, including a navigation
header and a tab bar. It can be declared anywhere in the tree.

## Layout

The panel is as tall as its content, and the content is stacked in a column with 12 pt gaps. The panel has a grabber
at the top, 16 pt horizontal padding, rounded top corners, and bottom padding of the safe area's bottom inset plus
16 pt, so the content stays above the home indicator.

For a list in a sheet, give the list's parent a height:

```tsx
<Sheet open={picking()} onClose={() => picking.set(false)}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }}>Choose a city</Text>
  <View style={{ height: 320 }}>
    <SelectList
      options={cities}
      value={city()}
      onSelect={(i) => {
        city.set(i);
        picking.set(false);
      }}
    />
  </View>
</Sheet>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the sheet is shown. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The panel's content. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the sheet's host view in your tree, not to the panel. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onClose` | none | The user closed the sheet (drag, backdrop tap or back button), after it slid away. Set `open` to false. |

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Panel | `background` |
| Backdrop | `overlay` |
| Grabber | `muted.background` |
| Top corners | `radius.lg`, at least 16 pt |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming). The default `overlay` color is light (5% black in light mode), so the backdrop is
only slightly dimmed. Set `overlay` in your theme for a darker backdrop.

## Accessibility

The backdrop is labeled "Close", so screen reader users can close the sheet by activating it. On Android, the back
button closes the sheet.

## Related

- [Modal](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md#modal): full-screen and page-sheet modals.
- [Animation](https://nsh.dev/docs/animation.md): native values and springs.
- [ActionSheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md): the system's action sheet.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/sheet

---

# StatusBar

`StatusBar` sets how the system status bar looks: the color of its content (time, battery, signal) and whether it is
hidden. You can render it as a component, so that the setting applies while that part of the UI is shown, or call its
static functions.

```tsx
import { StatusBar } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Rendering a StatusBar

A rendered `StatusBar` takes up no space. Its setting applies while it is mounted:

```tsx
import { mount, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { StatusBar } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#0b0b0f" }}>
      <StatusBar barStyle="light-content" />
      <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", padding: 16, paddingTop: 64 }}>Dark screen, light status bar</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

You can render several `StatusBar`s, for example one per screen. The **most recently mounted** one wins, **prop by
prop**: a `StatusBar` that only sets `hidden` keeps the `barStyle` of the one below it. When a `StatusBar` unmounts,
for example when its screen is popped, the previous setting applies again.

```tsx
function PhotoViewer() {
  return (
    <Screen headerShown={false}>
      <StatusBar hidden animated />
      …
    </Screen>
  );
}
```

## In a browser

The web has no status bar; the closest is the color browsers give their own bars around the page (the address bar on
phones, the title bar of an installed web app). `web={{ themeColor }}` sets it, as the page's
`<meta name="theme-color">`, with the same most-recent-wins rule; `barStyle` and `hidden` do nothing there.

```tsx
<StatusBar barStyle="light-content" web={{ themeColor: "#0b0b0f" }} />
```

## Setting it with functions

The static functions set a base setting. Every rendered `StatusBar` overrides it.

```tsx
StatusBar.setBarStyle("dark-content", true);
StatusBar.setHidden(true, "fade");
StatusBar.setHidden(false);
```

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `StatusBar.setBarStyle(barStyle: BarStyle, animated?: boolean \| null): void` | Sets the color of the content. `animated` defaults to `false`. |
| `StatusBar.setHidden(hidden: boolean, animation?: "none" \| "fade" \| "slide" \| null): void` | Hides or shows the bar. Any animation other than `"none"` animates the change. |

## Bar styles

| `barStyle` | Content |
|---|---|
| `"default"` | The platform's default for the current appearance (light or dark mode). |
| `"light-content"` | Light content, for dark backgrounds. |
| `"dark-content"` | Dark content, for light backgrounds. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `barStyle` | `"default" \| "light-content" \| "dark-content" \| null` | not set | The color of the content. |
| `hidden` | `boolean \| null` | not set | Hides the status bar. |
| `animated` | `boolean \| null` | not set | Animates changes of `barStyle` and `hidden`. |
| `android` | `{ backgroundColor?: string \| null }` | not set | Android only: the bar's background color. |
| `web` | `{ themeColor?: string \| null }` | not set | Browsers only: the page's theme color (`<meta name="theme-color">`). |

A prop that is not set leaves that part of the status bar to the `StatusBar` below, or to the functions. `StatusBar`
has no events.

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: hiding and showing animate with a fade; `"slide"` also fades. In an app
  [embedded](https://nsh.dev/docs/embedding-ios.md) in a native one, the host app's view controller decides how the status bar
  looks. The host applies NSH's setting by returning `NshAppView.preferredStatusBarStyle`,
  `NshAppView.prefersStatusBarHidden` and `NshAppView.preferredStatusBarUpdateAnimation` from its view controller.
- **Android**: `android={{ backgroundColor }}` colors the bar. It only applies before edge-to-edge (Android 15, API 35,
  draws apps behind the status bar).
- **Mac Catalyst** has no status bar.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If your `nsh.json` declares `"capabilities"`, the status bar can only be changed when it includes
> `"statusBar": true`. Otherwise changes are refused and logged. See
> [Sandbox and capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md).

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "statusBar": true
  }
}
```

## Related

- [nsh/android](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-android.md): `setStatusBarBackgroundColor` and other Android-only APIs.
- [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md): keeping content out from under the status bar.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/status-bar

---

# Stepper

`Stepper` shows a number between a − and a + button. Each press changes the number by `step`, within `min` and `max`.
Holding a button keeps stepping. The timer for the repeat runs in the core, so JS only receives `onChange` with each
new value.

```tsx
import { Stepper, type StepperRef } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Stepper } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const guests = signal(2);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <Text>{`${guests()} guests`}</Text>
      <Stepper value={guests()} min={1} max={12} onChange={(v) => guests.set(v)} />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

- **Controlled**: pass `value` and update it in `onChange`. The stepper shows `value`. A press reports the next value
  with `onChange`, and the number changes when you set the new `value`.
- **Uncontrolled**: leave out `value`. The stepper keeps its own value, starting at `defaultValue`, and reports each
  change with `onChange`.

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={5} min={0} max={50} onChange={(v) => console.log("now", v)} />
```

## Range, step and decimals

- The value always stays within `min` and `max`. If `min` is larger than `max`, the two are swapped. A negative `step`
  is used as positive.
- The number is shown with as many decimals as `step` has: `step={0.25}` shows `1.75`, `step={1}` shows `2`.
- Values are rounded to that number of decimals, which avoids floating-point drift such as `0.30000000000000004`.
- When `min`, `max` or `step` change, the value is moved back into the new range.

```tsx
<Stepper value={weight()} min={0} max={5} step={0.5} onChange={(v) => weight.set(v)} />
```

## Holding a button

A press steps once immediately. If the button is still held after 400 ms, the stepper steps again every 80 ms until the
button is released or the value reaches `min` or `max`. At a bound, that button is dimmed and disabled.

## Ref methods

Pass a `ref` to get a `StepperRef`, which reads and sets the value from your code:

```tsx
import { mount, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Stepper, type StepperRef } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  let stepper!: StepperRef;
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <Stepper ref={stepper} defaultValue={3} max={10} />
      <Button
        title="Reset"
        onPress={async () => {
          console.log("was", await stepper.value());
          stepper.setValue(0);
        }}
      />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `setValue(value: number): void` | Sets the value, rounded to the step's decimals and kept within the range, and reports it with `onChange` as a press would. On a controlled stepper, the number changes when you update `value`. |
| `value(): Promise<number>` | The value shown. It is a promise because the value lives in the core, not in JS. |
| `node: YNode` | The stepper's host node. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `number \| null` | none (uncontrolled) | The value, when the app controls it. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | `0` | The first value, when the app does not control it. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | The smallest value. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | The largest value. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | How much a press changes the value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No presses; both buttons dimmed. |
| `ref` | `StepperRef \| ((ref: StepperRef) => void)` | none | Receives the [ref](#ref-methods). |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout` | | | Applied to the stepper's root view (the row). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onChange` | `number`: the new value | A press, a held button's repeat or `setValue` changed the value. Not sent when the value would not change (at a bound). |

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Buttons | `secondary.background`, `secondary.active.background` while pressed, corner radius `radius` |
| − and + | `secondary.foreground`, `font.size` + 4 |
| Number | `foreground`, `font.size` + 1 |

The buttons are 40 × 40 pt. A disabled button, or one at a bound, is shown at 40% opacity. See
[Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

The buttons have the `button` role and the labels "Decrease" and "Increase". A button at a bound, or on a disabled
stepper, is reported as disabled. The number is a text that screen readers read as it is.

## Related

- [Group](https://nsh.dev/components/group.md): steppers in settings rows.
- [Input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input.md): free numeric input with `keyboardType`.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/stepper

---

# TextField

`TextField` is a single-line text input with an optional label above it, a border that changes color while focused,
and a clear button. It is built on the [`<Input>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/input.md) element.

```tsx
import { TextField } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { TextField } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const name = signal("");
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <TextField label="Name" placeholder="Your name" value={name()} onChange={(v) => name.set(v)} />
      <Text>{`Hello, ${name() || "nobody"}`}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## Controlled and uncontrolled

- **Controlled**: pass `value` and update it in `onChange`. The field shows `value`.
- **Uncontrolled**: leave out `value`. The field keeps its own text, starting at `defaultValue`, and reports changes
  with `onChange`.

```tsx
<TextField label="Notes" defaultValue="Draft" onChange={(text) => save(text)} />
```

## Variants

```tsx
<TextField label="Password" placeholder="At least 8 characters" secure />
<TextField label="Code" clearable={false} />
<TextField label="Account" value="ada@example.com" disabled />
```

- `secure` hides what is typed, for passwords.
- `clearable` (on by default) shows a × button at the end while there is text. Pressing it clears the text, reports
  `""` with `onChange` and keeps the input focused, so the user can type again.
- `disabled` makes the field read-only, dims it to 50% opacity and hides the clear button.

## Submitting

`onSubmit` is called with the text when the user presses the keyboard's return key:

```tsx
<TextField
  placeholder="Search"
  value={query()}
  onChange={(v) => query.set(v)}
  onSubmit={(text) => search(text)}
/>
```

> [!NOTE]
> TextField covers the common case. For keyboard types, return key labels, autofill, multiline text or a ref with
> `focus()`, use the [`<Input>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/input.md) element directly. See also
> [Forms and keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string \| null` | none | Shown above the input. |
| `placeholder` | `string \| null` | none | Shown while the input is empty. |
| `value` | `string \| null` | none (uncontrolled) | The text, when the app controls it. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `""` | The first text, when the app does not control it. |
| `secure` | `boolean` | `false` | Hides what is typed (passwords). |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows a clear button while there is text. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Not editable, 50% opacity. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the field's root view (the column holding the label and the input box). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onChange` | `string`: the new text | The user typed, deleted or pressed the clear button. |
| `onSubmit` | `string`: the text | The user pressed the return key. |

## Theming

| Part | Theme key |
|---|---|
| Label | `muted.foreground`, small text |
| Input box | `background`, corner radius `radius`, at least 44 pt tall |
| Border | `input.border`; `ring` while focused |
| Text | `foreground` |
| Placeholder | `muted.foreground` |
| Selection | `primary.background` |
| Clear button | `muted.background`; `secondary.active.background` while pressed |

See [Theming](https://nsh.dev/components.md#theming).

## Accessibility

The input is a native text field, so screen readers announce it as editable text. The clear button has the `button`
role and the label "Clear", and its touch area extends 8 pt beyond its 24 pt circle. The `label` is a separate text
above the input; it is not attached to the input as its accessibility label.

## Related

- [Input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input.md): the element TextField is built on.
- [Forms and keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md), [Keyboard](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md),
  [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/text-field

---

# KeyboardAvoidingView

`KeyboardAvoidingView` keeps its content above the software keyboard. When the keyboard shows or hides, the view makes
room by the keyboard's height, and the change animates with the keyboard. Use it for content that is **not** in a
scroll view, such as a message bar at the bottom of a chat screen.

```tsx
import { KeyboardAvoidingView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

> [!TIP]
> You do not need it for inputs inside a [scroll view](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md) or a [List](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md): NSH
> scrolls the focused input into view natively.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Input, mount, Scroll, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { KeyboardAvoidingView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const draft = signal("");
  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#ffffff" }}>
      <Scroll style={{ flex: 1 }} keyboardDismissMode="interactive">
        <Text style={{ padding: 16, paddingTop: 48 }}>Messages…</Text>
      </Scroll>
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8, padding: 8, borderTopWidth: 1, borderTopColor: "#e5e5e5" }}>
        <Input
          value={draft()}
          onChangeText={(v) => draft.set(v)}
          placeholder="Message"
          style={{ flex: 1, fontSize: 16, padding: 8 }}
        />
      </View>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

The view assumes that it reaches the bottom of the screen, as a screen's content does: it makes room by the full
keyboard height. If something is below it, such as a tab bar, subtract that with `keyboardVerticalOffset` (a negative
value) or add to it with a positive value.

## Behaviors

| `behavior` | How it makes room |
|---|---|
| `"padding"` (default) | Adds the keyboard's height to the view's bottom padding. The content above shrinks; the background still reaches the bottom of the screen. |
| `"height"` | Adds the keyboard's height as a bottom margin. The whole view, including its background, ends at the top of the keyboard. |
| `"position"` | Moves an inner content view up by the keyboard's height without changing its size. Style that inner view with `contentContainerStyle`. |

```tsx
<KeyboardAvoidingView behavior="position" contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16, gap: 12 }} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <TextField label="E-mail" />
  <Button title="Sign in" onPress={signIn} />
</KeyboardAvoidingView>
```

The padding or margin is added to what the view's own style sets, so your padding stays.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Avoid the keyboard. While false, the view does nothing. |
| `behavior` | `"padding" \| "height" \| "position"` | `"padding"` | How the view makes room (see [Behaviors](#behaviors)). |
| `keyboardVerticalOffset` | `number` | `0` | Added to the keyboard's height while it shows (for example, the height of a bar below the view). The total is never less than 0. |
| `contentContainerStyle` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | The inner view's style with `behavior="position"`. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The content. |
| `class`, `classList`, `style`, `testID`, `onLayout`, `ref` | | | Applied to the outer view. |

`KeyboardAvoidingView` has no events and uses no theme colors.

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: the room animates with the keyboard's own duration and an ease-in-ease-out curve.
- **Android**: where the window shrinks for the keyboard (an activity that resizes), the content already ends above
  the keyboard, the keyboard does not overlap the NSH view, and KeyboardAvoidingView adds nothing. Where the keyboard
  overlaps the view, it makes room as on iOS.
- **Mac Catalyst** has no software keyboard; the view never moves.

## Related

- [Keyboard](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard.md): `Keyboard.dismiss()` and the `keyboard()` height.
- [Forms and keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).
- [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view

---

# Alert

`Alert.alert` shows the platform's alert dialog: `UIAlertController` on iOS and `AlertDialog` on Android. It returns a
promise that resolves with the index of the button the user pressed. Unlike the other components in this set, an alert
has the platform's own look.

```tsx
import { Alert } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Alert, Button } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const answer = signal("–");
  const confirm = async () => {
    const i = await Alert.alert("Delete the photo?", "This cannot be undone.", [
      { text: "Cancel", style: "cancel" },
      { text: "Delete", style: "destructive" },
    ]);
    answer.set(i === 1 ? "deleted" : "kept");
  };
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <Button title="Delete…" variant="danger" onPress={confirm} />
      <Text>{answer()}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

With no buttons, the alert has one "OK" button:

```tsx
await Alert.alert("Saved", "Your changes were saved.");
```

## API

```ts
Alert.alert(
  title: string,
  message?: string | null,
  buttons?: AlertButton[] | null,
  options?: AlertOptions | null,
): Promise<number>
```

The promise resolves with the index of the pressed button in `buttons`, or `-1` when the alert was dismissed without
a button (Android, with `cancelable`). It does not reject.

### AlertButton

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string \| null` | `"OK"` | The button's label. |
| `style` | `"default" \| "cancel" \| "destructive"` | `"default"` | `cancel` marks the cancel button; `destructive` marks a destructive action (red on iOS). |

### AlertOptions

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cancelable` | `boolean` | `false` | Android: a tap outside the dialog or the back button dismisses it, and the promise resolves with `-1`. |

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: the buttons are laid out by `UIAlertController`. A button with `style: "cancel"` is placed where iOS puts
  cancel buttons, which may differ from its position in your array; the index you get back is always its index in
  `buttons`.
- **Android**: an `AlertDialog` shows at most three buttons. They are mapped by position: the last button is the
  positive button, the one before it the negative button, and the one before that the neutral button. Further buttons
  at the start of the array are not shown. Button styles do not change the look.

> [!TIP]
> Because the main thread never waits for JS, the dialog is shown and answered natively and your code continues when
> the promise resolves. You can `await` an alert inside any event handler, for example to confirm leaving a screen
> with [`preventBack`](https://nsh.dev/components/navigation.md#leaving-a-screen).

## Related

- [ActionSheet](https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet.md): a list of actions.
- [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md): a bottom sheet with your own content.
- [nsh/android](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-android.md): `Toast.show` for short messages on Android.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/alert

---

# ActionSheet

`ActionSheet.show` presents a list of actions: an action sheet (`UIAlertController`) on iOS and a list dialog on
Android. It returns a promise that resolves with the index of the chosen action.

```tsx
import { ActionSheet } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { ActionSheet, Button } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const chosen = signal("–");
  const share = async () => {
    const options = ["Cancel", "Copy link", "Save", "Delete"];
    const i = await ActionSheet.show({
      title: "Share the photo",
      options,
      cancelButtonIndex: 0,
      destructiveButtonIndexes: [3],
    });
    chosen.set(options[i] ?? "dismissed");
  };
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <Button title="Share…" onPress={share} />
      <Text>{chosen()}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## API

```ts
ActionSheet.show(options: ActionSheetOptions): Promise<number>
```

The promise resolves with the index of the chosen action in `options.options`. When the user dismisses the sheet
without choosing (a tap outside, the back button), it resolves with `cancelButtonIndex`, or with `-1` if there is no
cancel action. It does not reject.

### ActionSheetOptions

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | `string[]` | required | The actions' labels, in order. |
| `cancelButtonIndex` | `number \| null` | none | The index of the cancel action. |
| `destructiveButtonIndexes` | `number[] \| null` | none | The indexes of destructive actions (red on iOS). |
| `title` | `string \| null` | none | Shown above the actions. |
| `message` | `string \| null` | none | Shown below the title. |

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: the cancel action is shown separately at the bottom of the sheet. On iPad and Mac Catalyst the sheet is a
  popover, which hides the cancel action: a tap outside the popover dismisses it, and the promise resolves with
  `cancelButtonIndex` (or `-1`).
- **Android**: the actions are a list in a dialog. The cancel action is not listed; a tap outside or the back button
  cancels. A list dialog cannot show a message: without a `title`, the `message` is used as the title, and with a
  `title` the message is not shown. Destructive actions look like the others.

## Related

- [Alert](https://nsh.dev/components/alert.md): a dialog with up to three buttons.
- [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md): a bottom sheet with your own content, the same on both platforms.
- [SelectList](https://nsh.dev/components/select-list.md): choosing one of many options.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/action-sheet

---

# Keyboard

`nsh/ui/mobile` has two exports for the software keyboard: the `Keyboard` module, which hides the keyboard, and the
`keyboard()` accessor, which tells you how much of the screen the keyboard covers.

```tsx
import { Keyboard, keyboard } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Keyboard.dismiss

```ts
Keyboard.dismiss(): void
```

Unfocuses the focused input, which hides the keyboard. It does nothing if no input is focused.

```tsx
import { mount, signal, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Keyboard, TextField } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function App() {
  const name = signal("");
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, paddingTop: 48, gap: 12 }}>
      <TextField label="Name" value={name()} onChange={(v) => name.set(v)} />
      <Button title="Done" onPress={() => Keyboard.dismiss()} />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

> [!TIP]
> To hide the keyboard when the user drags a scroll view, set `keyboardDismissMode="on-drag"` or `"interactive"` on
> the [scroll view](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md) or [List](https://nsh.dev/elements/list.md) instead of calling `Keyboard.dismiss()`.

## keyboard()

```ts
keyboard: Accessor<{ height: number; duration: number }>
```

`keyboard()` returns the height of the software keyboard over the NSH surface, in points (0 while it is hidden), and
the duration of the keyboard's show or hide animation, in seconds. It is reactive: an effect or JSX expression that
reads it runs again when the keyboard shows, hides or changes height.

```tsx
import { Input, View } from "nsh";
import { keyboard, useSafeAreaInsets } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function MessageBar() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
  return (
    <View
      style={{
        flexDirection: "row",
        padding: 8,
        // The home indicator's inset only matters while the keyboard is hidden.
        paddingBottom: 8 + (keyboard().height > 0 ? 0 : insets().bottom),
      }}
    >
      <Input placeholder="Message" style={{ flex: 1 }} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

The height is the part of the keyboard that overlaps the NSH surface. When the window itself shrinks for the keyboard
(an Android activity that resizes), or when NSH is embedded in a view that ends above the keyboard, the height is 0.

> [!NOTE]
> To keep content above the keyboard, [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md) is usually simpler than
> reading `keyboard()` yourself: it animates with the keyboard natively.

## Related

- [KeyboardAvoidingView](https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard-avoiding-view.md).
- [TextField](https://nsh.dev/components/text-field.md) and [Input](https://nsh.dev/elements/input.md).
- [Forms and keyboard](https://nsh.dev/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/keyboard

---

# Navigation

`nsh/ui/mobile` provides native navigation: a `Stack` of `Screen`s driven by a navigator you create with
`createNavigator`, and `Modal` for content presented over everything else. A stack is `UINavigationController` on iOS,
with the native header and swipe back. On Android it is a stack of screens with a toolbar and predictive back.

```tsx
import { createNavigator, Modal, Screen, Stack } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

This page is the API reference. For a walkthrough, see the [Navigation guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/navigation.md).

## Usage

```tsx
import { mount, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, createNavigator, Screen, Stack } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

type Route = { name: "home" } | { name: "detail"; id: number };

const nav = createNavigator<Route>({ name: "home" });

function Home() {
  return (
    <Screen title="Inbox">
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
        <Button title="Open message 1" onPress={() => nav.push({ name: "detail", id: 1 })} />
      </View>
    </Screen>
  );
}

function Detail(props: { id: number }) {
  return (
    <Screen title={`Message ${props.id}`}>
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
        <Button title="Back" variant="secondary" onPress={() => nav.pop()} />
      </View>
    </Screen>
  );
}

function App() {
  return (
    <Stack navigator={nav} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      {(route) => (route.name === "home" ? <Home /> : <Detail id={route.id} />)}
    </Stack>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## How a stack works

- The navigator holds the **routes**: plain values of your choosing, from the bottom of the stack to the top. A route
  is usually an object that names the screen and carries its parameters.
- `Stack` calls its child function once for each route and shows the result as a screen. It does not call the
  function again for the same route, so a screen keeps its state (signals, scroll position, inputs) while it is in the
  stack, also while other screens cover it.
- When the user leaves a screen natively (the back button, swipe back, Android back), the stack removes its route from
  the navigator, so `nav.routes()` always matches what the user sees.
- Routes are compared by **identity** (`===`). Each route in a stack must be a distinct value: push a new object
  (`{ name: "detail", id }`) rather than reusing one, and avoid string routes for screens that can appear twice.
- If the child function returns something other than a `<Screen>`, the stack wraps it in a screen with default
  options. Return a `<Screen>` to set a title and other header options.

## createNavigator

```ts
function createNavigator<R>(initial: R | R[]): Navigator<R>
```

Creates a navigator whose stack starts with `initial` (one route or several). Create it once, for example at module
level, and pass it to `<Stack navigator>`. Any code can import it to navigate.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `routes: Accessor<readonly R[]>` | The routes, bottom to top. Reactive. |
| `push(route: R): void` | Pushes a screen. |
| `pop(count?: number): void` | Pops `count` screens (default 1). At least one screen always stays. |
| `popToTop(): void` | Pops back to the first screen. |
| `replace(route: R): void` | Replaces the top screen. |
| `reset(routes: R[]): void` | Replaces all screens. |
| `remove(route: R): void` | Removes a route wherever it is in the stack. |

```tsx
nav.push({ name: "detail", id: 7 });
nav.pop(2);
nav.reset([{ name: "home" }, { name: "detail", id: 1 }]);
const depth = () => nav.routes().length;
```

## Stack

```tsx
<Stack navigator={nav} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  {(route, index) => …}
</Stack>
```

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `navigator` | `Navigator<R>` | The navigator that holds the routes. Required. |
| `children` | `(route: R, index: Accessor<number>) => JSX.Element` | Renders a route. Return a `<Screen>` for header options. Required. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | The stack's style; usually `{ flex: 1 }`. |

The child function receives the route value itself and an accessor of its position in the stack.

## Screen

`Screen` is one screen of a stack and configures its header:

```tsx
<Screen
  title="Profile"
  headerTintColor="#ffffff"
  headerBackgroundColor="#1a7f37"
  headerTitleColor="#ffffff"
  headerRight={<Text onPress={edit} style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 17 }}>Edit</Text>}
>
  <Scroll style={{ flex: 1 }}>…</Scroll>
</Screen>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | none | The header's title. |
| `headerShown` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the header is shown. |
| `headerTransparent` | `boolean` | `false` | The content extends under a transparent header. |
| `headerTintColor` | `ColorValue` | platform | The color of the back button and the bar buttons. |
| `headerBackgroundColor` | `ColorValue` | platform | The header's background color. |
| `headerTitleColor` | `ColorValue` | platform | The title's color. |
| `headerBackVisible` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the back button is shown. |
| `headerLeft` | `JSX.Element` | none | Content at the left of the header, in place of the back button. |
| `headerRight` | `JSX.Element` | none | Content at the right of the header. |
| `headerTitle` | `JSX.Element` | none | Content that replaces the title. |
| `gestureEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | The interactive back gesture: iOS swipe back, Android predictive back that follows the finger. The back buttons work either way. |
| `preventBack` | `boolean` | `false` | The user cannot leave the screen. See [Leaving a screen](#leaving-a-screen). |
| `animation` | `"default" \| "fade" \| "none"` | `"default"` | How the screen enters and leaves. |
| `ios` | `{ headerLargeTitle?: boolean; headerBackTitle?: string }` | none | iOS only: a large title that shrinks into the bar as the content scrolls; the label of the back button that leads back to this screen. |
| `desktop` | `{ headerLargeTitle?: boolean; headerBackTitle?: string }` | none | Desktop only (macOS, Windows, Linux): the same options on a desktop header. |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | The screen's style. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The content. |
| `onBackRequest` | `() => void` | none | The user tried to leave a screen that has `preventBack`. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | none | The user left the screen natively and its route was removed. |

The header items (`headerLeft`, `headerRight`, `headerTitle`) are ordinary JSX: they can read signals, handle presses
and update while the screen is shown.

The screen's content starts below an opaque header. With `headerTransparent` or `headerShown={false}`, it starts at
the top of the screen; use [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md) or `useSafeAreaInsets()` to keep it clear of the header
and the status bar.

```tsx
<Screen title="Large title" ios={{ headerLargeTitle: true }}>
  <Scroll style={{ flex: 1 }}>…</Scroll>
</Screen>
```

### Leaving a screen

`preventBack` keeps the user on a screen, for example while a form has unsaved changes. While it is true, swipe back is
off, and the header's back button and the Android back button call `onBackRequest` instead of popping. Ask the user,
then pop yourself:

```tsx
import { Input, signal } from "nsh";
import { Alert, Screen } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function EditNote() {
  const text = signal("");
  const confirm = async () => {
    const i = await Alert.alert("Discard your changes?", undefined, [
      { text: "Keep editing", style: "cancel" },
      { text: "Discard", style: "destructive" },
    ]);
    if (i === 1) nav.pop();
  };
  return (
    <Screen title="Edit" preventBack={text().length > 0} onBackRequest={confirm}>
      <Input value={text()} onChangeText={(v) => text.set(v)} placeholder="A note" />
    </Screen>
  );
}
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The system asks whether the user may go back on the main thread, at the moment the user acts, and the main thread
> never waits for JS. So NSH answers from the `preventBack` value already mounted. Set `preventBack` as soon as there
> is something to lose, not in a handler that runs when the user goes back.

To turn off only the swipe gesture and keep the back buttons, use `gestureEnabled={false}`.

## Modal

`Modal` presents content over everything else, including the stack's header, in its own native window layer. It is
shown while `visible` is true (the default), and it is controlled: when the user asks to close it, `onRequestClose` is
called and you set `visible` to false.

```tsx
import { signal, Text, View } from "nsh";
import { Button, Modal, SafeAreaView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";

function Settings() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <View>
      <Button title="About" onPress={() => open.set(true)} />
      <Modal visible={open()} ios={{ presentationStyle: "pageSheet" }} onRequestClose={() => open.set(false)}>
        <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1, padding: 20, gap: 12 }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700" }}>About</Text>
          <Button title="Close" onPress={() => open.set(false)} />
        </SafeAreaView>
      </Modal>
    </View>
  );
}
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Shown while true. |
| `animationType` | `"slide" \| "fade" \| "none"` | `"slide"` | How the modal appears. |
| `transparent` | `boolean` | `false` | The background shows what is behind, for dialogs and overlays. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `false` | The user closes it natively (iOS sheet swiped down, Android back button); then `onRequestClose` and `onDismiss` are called. Without it, those gestures only ask to close. |
| `ios` | `{ presentationStyle?: "fullScreen" \| "pageSheet" \| "formSheet"; supportedOrientations?: (…)[] }` | none | iOS only: `pageSheet` and `formSheet` keep what is behind visible; the orientations the modal allows (default: the presenter's). |
| `desktop` | `{ presentationStyle?: "fullScreen" \| "pageSheet" \| "formSheet" }` | none | Desktop only (macOS, Windows, Linux): `pageSheet` and `formSheet` are cards centered in the window over a dimmed backdrop; clicking the backdrop or pressing Escape asks to close. |
| `android` | `{ statusBarTranslucent?: boolean }` | none | Android only: the content reaches under the status bar (by default it starts below it). |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | The modal's style. |
| `children` | `JSX.Element` | none | The content. |
| `onRequestClose` | `() => void` | none | The user asked to close it (Android back button, iOS sheet swipe). Set `visible` to false. |
| `onShow` | `() => void` | none | The modal was shown. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | none | The modal was dismissed. |

A modal provides its own insets to its content, so [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md) and `useSafeAreaInsets()`
inside it use the modal's insets. A modal with `transparent` and `animationType="fade"` works as a custom dialog:

```tsx
<Modal visible={open()} transparent animationType="fade" onRequestClose={close}>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.4)", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", padding: 32 }}>
    <View style={{ alignSelf: "stretch", backgroundColor: "#ffffff", borderRadius: 14, padding: 20, gap: 12 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" }}>A dialog</Text>
      <Button title="OK" onPress={close} />
    </View>
  </View>
</Modal>
```

See [Modal](https://nsh.dev/elements/modal.md) for more about the element.

## Platform notes

- **iOS**: `UINavigationController` with the native header, back button and swipe back. `ios={{ headerLargeTitle }}`
  and `headerBackTitle` are iOS only. Stack changes that arrive during a running transition are applied when it ends.
- **Android**: a stack with a toolbar. The system back button pops the top screen, with predictive back on Android
  versions that have it. See `BackHandler` in [nsh/android](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-android.md) to handle the back button
  yourself.
- **Mac Catalyst**: as on iOS. Page and form sheets are presented as macOS sheets the size of the window.

## Related

- [Navigation guide](https://nsh.dev/docs/navigation.md).
- [SafeAreaView](https://nsh.dev/components/safe-area-view.md): insets below headers and in modals.
- [Sheet](https://nsh.dev/components/sheet.md): a bottom sheet drawn by NSH, the same on both platforms.
- [Alert](https://nsh.dev/components/alert.md): confirming before leaving a screen.

Source: https://nsh.dev/components/navigation

---

# Modules

An NSH app imports everything it uses from a small set of modules. They are all native: the reactive graph, the renderer and every module are implemented in Rust inside the runtime, and the bundler keeps `import ... from "nsh/..."` as imports instead of copying code into your bundle. Your bundle only holds your own code.

```tsx
import { mount, signal } from "nsh";
import { createNativeValue } from "nsh/animated";
import { windowSize } from "nsh/device";
import { Button, SafeAreaView } from "nsh/ui/mobile";
```

## Two layers

- **`nsh` and `nsh/<module>`** are the primitives and the environment: reactivity, lists, canvas, animation, gestures, device information. Every UI set builds on them.
- **`nsh/ui/<set>`** is a whole UI for one form factor. Today that is `nsh/ui/mobile`: navigation, modals, the status bar, system dialogs and components such as `Button` and `TextField` (see [Components](https://nsh.dev/components.md)).

There is no catch-all module: each API lives in exactly one place. Platform-only APIs live in `nsh/ios`, `nsh/android` and `nsh/desktop` (macOS, Windows, Linux); all can be imported on every platform, so one bundle runs everywhere (their calls do nothing elsewhere, and `isAvailable` tells you which platform you are on).

Types are generated from the runtime: `nsh init`, `nsh build`, `nsh dev` and `nsh trace` write `.nsh/types` next to your app, so the TypeScript declarations always match the runtime you build with (see [Project structure](https://nsh.dev/docs/project-structure.md)).

## All modules

| Module | Exports | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `nsh` | `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `batch`, `untracked`, `cleanup`, `context`, `split`, `mount`; `View`, `Text`, `Scroll`, `Input`; the types of elements, styles, events and JSX (`YNode`, `ViewStyle`, ...) | [nsh](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh.md) |
| `nsh/animated` | `createNativeValue`, `NativeValue`, `NativeNode`, `Animated`, `Easing`, `LayoutAnimation` | [nsh/animated](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md) |
| `nsh/list` | `List` (virtualized, recycling list) | [nsh/list](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-list.md) |
| `nsh/canvas` | `Canvas`, `Path2D`, `CanvasRenderingContext2D`, `CanvasGradient` | [nsh/canvas](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-canvas.md) |
| `nsh/device` | `windowSize`, `colorScheme`, `fontScale`, `Platform`, `PixelRatio`, `I18nManager` | [nsh/device](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-device.md) |
| `nsh/gesture` | `PanResponder` | [nsh/gesture](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-gesture.md) |
| `nsh/image` | `Image` (the element), `Image.getSize`, `Image.prefetch` | [nsh/image](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-image.md) |
| `nsh/clipboard` | `Clipboard.setString`, `Clipboard.getString`, `Clipboard.hasString` | [nsh/clipboard](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-clipboard.md) |
| `nsh/keymap` | `keymap.bind` (keyboard shortcuts: `mod+k`, `ctrl+shift+p`, ...) | [nsh/keymap](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-keymap.md) |
| `nsh/native` | `nativeComponent` (components the embedding app registers) | [nsh/native](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-native.md) |
| `nsh/accessibility` | `AccessibilityInfo`, `screenReaderEnabled`, `reduceMotion` | [nsh/accessibility](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-accessibility.md) |
| `nsh/ios` | `isAvailable`, `InputAccessoryView` | [nsh/ios](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-ios.md) |
| `nsh/android` | `isAvailable`, `Toast`, `BackHandler`, `setStatusBarBackgroundColor` | [nsh/android](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-android.md) |
| `nsh/desktop` | `isAvailable`, `Window` (title, title bar, maximize, full screen), `titleBar`, `Menu` (application menu, context menus) | [nsh/desktop](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-desktop.md) |
| `nsh/webview` | `WebView` | [nsh/webview](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-webview.md) |
| `nsh/video` | `Video` | [nsh/video](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-video.md) |
| `nsh/ui/mobile` | Navigation (`createNavigator`, `Stack`, `Screen`, `Modal`), `SafeAreaView`, `StatusBar`, `Alert`, `ActionSheet`, `Keyboard`, `Button`, `TextField`, ... | [Components](https://nsh.dev/components.md) |
| Globals | `fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, `Blob`, `FormData`, `AbortController`, `Intl`, timers, `console`, `requestAnimationFrame`, ... (no import) | [Global APIs](https://nsh.dev/modules/globals.md) |

Reference pages that are not modules:

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Style reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference.md) | Every style key, its type and meaning |
| [Tailwind reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/tailwind-reference.md) | The Tailwind utilities and variants `class` accepts |

## Host elements

The host elements are components imported like everything else: `View`, `Text`, `Scroll` and `Input` from `nsh`, `Image` from `nsh/image`, `List` from `nsh/list`, `Canvas`, `WebView`, `Video` from their modules, `Modal` from `nsh/ui/mobile`, `InputAccessoryView` from `nsh/ios`. Only `If` and `Each` are globals. The compiler makes the elements in place, so the imports cost nothing at run time. Their props are documented under [Elements](https://nsh.dev/elements.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules

---

# nsh

`nsh` is the core module: the reactive API (signals, computed values, effects, context), `mount`, the host elements `View`, `Text`, `Scroll` and `Input`, and the TypeScript types of elements, styles and events. The reactive graph itself runs natively in Rust; reading a signal is a call into the runtime that costs a few nanoseconds, and only your own closures run in the JavaScript interpreter.

```ts
import { batch, cleanup, computed, context, effect, Input, mount, Scroll, signal, split, Text, untracked, View } from "nsh";
```

NSH's reactivity follows the same model as SolidJS: a component function runs **once**, and the parts of the UI that read signals are updated in place when those signals change. There is no re-render of the component and no virtual DOM. See [Reactivity](https://nsh.dev/docs/reactivity.md) for the guide.

## signal

```ts
function signal<T>(value: T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Signal<T>;
function signal<T = undefined>(): Signal<T | undefined>;

interface Signal<T> {
  (): T;                              // read (tracked)
  set(value: T): void;                // write
  update(fn: (value: T) => T): void;  // write from the current value
}

interface SignalOptions<T> {
  /** When a new value counts as a change (default `===`); `false`: always. */
  equals?: false | ((previous: T, next: T) => boolean);
}
```

A signal holds a value. Calling it reads the value and, inside a tracking scope (JSX expressions, `computed`, `effect`), subscribes that scope to it. `set` and `update` write it; everything that read it updates.

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";

function Counter() {
  const count = signal(0);
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 24, gap: 12 }}>
      <Text>Count: {count()}</Text>
      <Text onPress={() => count.update((n) => n + 1)}>Add one</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(Counter);
```

By default a write that is `===` to the current value does nothing. Pass `equals: false` to notify on every write (useful when you mutate an object in place and set the same object again), or your own comparison:

```ts
const items = signal<string[]>([], { equals: false });
const point = signal({ x: 0, y: 0 }, { equals: (a, b) => a.x === b.x && a.y === b.y });
```

## computed

```ts
function computed<T>(fn: (previous: T | undefined) => T, options?: SignalOptions<T>): Accessor<T>;

interface Accessor<T> {
  (): T;
}
```

A value derived from signals. `fn` runs again when a signal it read changes; readers of the computed value only update when its result changes (by `equals`, `===` by default). `fn` receives the previous result.

```ts
const first = signal("Ada");
const last = signal("Lovelace");
const full = computed(() => `${first()} ${last()}`);
full(); // "Ada Lovelace"
```

Use `computed` when a derivation is expensive or read in several places. For a cheap expression, a plain function (`const full = () => first() + " " + last()`) is just as reactive.

## effect

```ts
function effect(fn: () => void): void;
```

Runs `fn` after rendering, and again whenever a signal it read changes. Use effects for side effects: logging, timers, talking to native modules. An effect belongs to the component (or effect) it was created in and is disposed with it.

```ts
const query = signal("");
effect(() => {
  console.log("query is now", query());
});
```

To undo something before the effect runs again (or when its component goes away), call [`cleanup`](#cleanup) inside it.

## batch

```ts
function batch<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Runs `fn` and applies all its writes together at the end, so readers update once instead of once per write. Returns what `fn` returns.

```ts
batch(() => {
  first.set("Grace");
  last.set("Hopper");
}); // `full` recomputes once
```

## untracked

```ts
function untracked<T>(fn: () => T): T;
```

Runs `fn` without subscribing the current scope to what it reads. Use it to read a signal inside an effect or JSX expression without depending on it.

```ts
effect(() => {
  // Runs again when `query` changes, not when `page` changes.
  search(query(), untracked(() => page()));
});
```

## cleanup

```ts
function cleanup(fn: () => void): void;
```

Registers `fn` to run before the current effect runs again, or when the current component or effect goes away.

```tsx
function Clock() {
  const now = signal(new Date());
  const timer = setInterval(() => now.set(new Date()), 1000);
  cleanup(() => clearInterval(timer));
  return <Text>{now().toLocaleTimeString()}</Text>;
}
```

## context

```ts
function context<T>(defaultValue: T): Context<T>;

interface Context<T> extends Accessor<T> {
  Provider: (props: { value: T; children?: JSX.Element }) => JSX.Element;
}
```

A value a component provides to everything it renders, however deep. Calling the context (`Theme()`) reads the nearest provider's value, or `defaultValue` without one.

```tsx
import { context, mount, signal, Text, View } from "nsh";

const Theme = context<"light" | "dark">("light");

function Label(props: { text: string }) {
  return <Text style={{ color: Theme() === "dark" ? "#fff" : "#000" }}>{props.text}</Text>;
}

function App() {
  const dark = signal(false);
  return (
    <Theme.Provider value={dark() ? "dark" : "light"}>
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 24, backgroundColor: dark() ? "#000" : "#fff" }}>
        <Label text="Hello" />
        <Text onPress={() => dark.update((d) => !d)}>Toggle</Text>
      </View>
    </Theme.Provider>
  );
}

mount(App);
```

## mount

```ts
function mount<P extends object>(app: Component<P>, props?: P): () => void;
```

Renders `app` into the surface (the window, or the `NshAppView` / `NshView` the app is embedded in) and returns a function that removes it. Every app's entry file ends with `mount(App)`.

```tsx
mount(App);
```

## split

