```ts
      checked?: boolean;
      onSelect?: () => void;
      submenu?: MenuItem[];
    };
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | What the item shows. A role's item has a label of its own without it. |
| `onSelect` | Called when the item is chosen, by a click or its shortcut. |
| `shortcut` | Its keyboard shortcut: modifiers and one key joined by `+`, such as `"mod+n"`, `"mod+shift+z"`, `"alt+f4"` or `"f11"`. The modifiers are in the table below. Keys are letters, digits and punctuation, written as the character the key types on a US keyboard without Shift (`,`, `/`; `"shift+/"` for `?`), or a name: `plus` (the `=` / `+` key, also `=`), `minus` (also `-`), `space`, `enter` (`return`), `escape` (`esc`), `tab`, `backspace`, `delete` (`del`), `insert`, the arrows `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` (`arrowup`, …), `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `f1`–`f24`. Case does not matter (`"Mod+Shift+N"` is `"mod+shift+n"`; a capital letter is the same key, not Shift), and lowercase is the recommended style. An invalid shortcut (`"mod-n"`, `"mod++"`, `"mod+?"`) throws an error that gives the right spelling. `nsh/keymap` takes the same keystrokes. Menus show it in the platform's own style (`⇧⌘N` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+N` on Windows). |
| `enabled` | `false` grays the item out (default `true`). |
| `checked` | Set (to `true` or `false`) for an item with a check mark. |
| `submenu` | Makes the item a submenu (it needs a `label`). |
| `role` | A standard item the platform carries out (below). |

`null`, `undefined` and `false` items are left out, so `cond && { … }` works in a list.

Modifiers:

| Modifier | macOS | Windows | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mod` (also `cmdorctrl`) | Command (⌘) | Ctrl | Ctrl |
| `cmd` (also `command`, `meta`, `super`, `win`) | Command (⌘) | Windows key | Super |
| `ctrl` (also `control`) | Control (⌃) | Ctrl | Ctrl |
| `alt` (also `option`, `opt`) | Option (⌥) | Alt | Alt |
| `shift` | Shift (⇧) | Shift | Shift |

Use `mod` for an app's own shortcuts: it is the key each platform's apps use for them (⌘N on macOS, Ctrl+N on Windows and Linux), so one spelling fits everywhere. The Windows key and Super mostly belong to the system (Win+E, the GNOME overview), so `cmd` is rarely right outside macOS.

Roles:

| Role | Does | Platforms |
|---|---|---|
| `about`, `hide`, `hideOthers`, `showAll` | The app menu's standard items | macOS (left out elsewhere) |
| `quit` | Quits the app | All |
| `undo`, `redo`, `cut`, `copy`, `paste`, `selectAll` | Edit the focused text field (its own shortcuts stay its own) | All |
| `minimize`, `zoom`, `toggleFullScreen`, `close` | The window | All |

A role's item has the platform's label and shortcut unless it sets its own (macOS adds the app's name to `about`, `hide` and `quit`).

Menu shortcuts come first, as in native apps: a key an item takes never reaches the focused text field or NSH's own keys. Only a binding of [`nsh/keymap`](./nsh-keymap) of the same keystroke comes before them. So give the editing shortcuts (`mod+c`, `mod+v`, `mod+x`, `mod+a`, `mod+z`) only to the edit roles, which pass them to the text field, and avoid keys without a modifier (`escape`, the arrows, letters), which would take them from text fields and from back navigation.

```tsx
import { effect, signal } from "nsh";
import { Platform } from "nsh/device";
import { Menu } from "nsh/desktop";

const mac = Platform.OS === "macos";
const wrap = signal(true);

effect(() => {
  Menu.setApplicationMenu([
    mac && {
      label: "My App",
      submenu: [{ role: "about" }, { type: "separator" }, { role: "hide" }, { role: "hideOthers" }, { type: "separator" }, { role: "quit" }],
    },
    {
      label: "File",
      submenu: [
        { label: "New", shortcut: "mod+n", onSelect: () => createDocument() },
        { label: "Open…", shortcut: "mod+o", onSelect: () => openDocument() },
        !mac && { type: "separator" },
        !mac && { role: "quit", label: "Exit" },
      ],
    },
    {
      label: "Edit",
      submenu: [{ role: "undo" }, { role: "redo" }, { type: "separator" }, { role: "cut" }, { role: "copy" }, { role: "paste" }],
    },
    {
      label: "View",
      submenu: [
        { label: "Word Wrap", checked: wrap(), onSelect: () => wrap.update((w) => !w) },
        { role: "toggleFullScreen" },
      ],
    },
  ]);
});
```

A context menu, from a button's press:

```tsx
<View
  onPress={() =>
    Menu.popup([
      { label: "Rename", onSelect: rename },
      { label: "Duplicate", onSelect: duplicate },
      { type: "separator" },
      { label: "Delete", onSelect: remove },
    ])
  }
>
  <Text>More</Text>
</View>
```

> [!NOTE]
> Menus are the system's (NSMenu, Win32 menus, GTK popover menus): they look and behave like every other app's, follow the system's (or the app's) appearance and are keyboard accessible. `examples/desktop` is an app with a title bar of its own, an application menu and context menus.

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-desktop

---

# nsh/webview

`nsh/webview` exports `WebView`: a web page shown by the platform's own browser engine (`WKWebView` on iOS and Mac Catalyst, `android.webkit.WebView` on Android). It is a native view laid out like any other, so it scrolls, clips and overlaps other views correctly.

```ts
import { WebView, type WebViewNavigation, type WebViewProps } from "nsh/webview";
```

See [Web view and video](https://nsh.dev/docs/web-view-and-video.md) for the guide and [`<WebView>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/web-view.md) for its props.

## WebView

```ts
const WebView: (props: WebViewProps) => YNode;

interface WebViewProps extends Omit<ViewProps, "children" | "ios" | "desktop">, WebViewHostProps {
  source: string | { uri: string } | { html: string; baseUrl?: string };
  ios?: IOSWebViewHostProps;
  desktop?: DesktopWebViewHostProps;
}
```

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View, type YNode } from "nsh";
import { WebView, type WebViewNavigation } from "nsh/webview";

function Browser() {
  const nav = signal<WebViewNavigation | null>(null);
  let web!: YNode;
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 16, padding: 12 }}>
        <Text onPress={() => web.goBack()} style={{ opacity: nav()?.canGoBack ? 1 : 0.4 }}>Back</Text>
        <Text onPress={() => web.reload()}>Reload</Text>
        <Text numberOfLines={1} style={{ flex: 1 }}>{nav()?.title ?? ""}</Text>
      </View>
      <WebView ref={web} source="https://example.com" style={{ flex: 1 }} onNavigationStateChange={(n) => nav.set(n)} />
    </View>
  );
}

mount(Browser);
```

## Props

`WebView` takes the [view props](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md) (style, classes, layout, accessibility, `ref`; no children), plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string \| { uri: string } \| { html: string; baseUrl?: string }` | (required) | A URL, `{ uri }`, or inline HTML with an optional base URL for its relative links. |
| `injectedJavaScript` | `string` | | Runs after each page loads. |
| `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` | `string` | | Runs before each page's own scripts. |
| `userAgent` | `string` | platform's | The user agent string. |
| `scrollEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | The user can scroll the page. |
| `javaScriptEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Pages run scripts. |
| `ios` | `{ allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures?: boolean }` | | iOS only: swipe from the edges to go back and forward. |
| `desktop` | `{ allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures?: boolean }` | | macOS: two-finger trackpad swipes go back and forward; Windows: touchscreen swipes; Linux: touchpad swipes. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onLoadStart` | `WebViewNavigation` | A page starts loading. |
| `onLoad` | `WebViewNavigation` | A page finished loading. |
| `onError` | `{ message: string }` | A page failed to load. |
| `onNavigationStateChange` | `WebViewNavigation` | The URL, title, loading state or history changed. |
| `onMessage` | `{ data: string }` | The page called `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(data)`. |

```ts
interface WebViewNavigation {
  url: string;
  title: string;
  loading: boolean;
  canGoBack: boolean;
  canGoForward: boolean;
}
```

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `reload()` | Reloads the page. |
| `goBack()` | Goes back in its history. |
| `goForward()` | Goes forward in its history. |
| `stopLoading()` | Stops loading. |
| `injectJavaScript(script)` | Runs `script` in the page. |
| `postMessage(data)` | Sends `data` (a string) to the page: a `message` event on `window`, with `data` as `event.data`. |

## Talking to the page

The page sends strings to the app with `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(…)`; the app sends strings to the page with `ref.postMessage(…)`. Send JSON for structured data.

```tsx
const page = `<!doctype html><html><head><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width"></head>
<body>
  <button onclick="window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage('hello from the page')">Post to the app</button>
  <p id="got"></p>
  <script>
    window.addEventListener('message', (e) => { document.getElementById('got').textContent = e.data; });
  </script>
</body></html>`;

let web!: YNode;
const message = signal("");

<WebView ref={web} source={{ html: page }} style={{ height: 200 }} onMessage={(e) => message.set(e.data)} />
<Text onPress={() => web.postMessage("hi from the app")}>Post to the page</Text>
```

## Capabilities

When your app declares `capabilities` in `nsh.json`, a web view may only show and navigate to the hosts listed under `webview`; other top-level navigations are refused natively. An app without a `capabilities` key may show anything. See [Sandbox and capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md).

```json
{
  "capabilities": {
    "webview": { "hosts": ["example.com", "*.example.com"] }
  }
}
```

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-webview

---

# nsh/video

`nsh/video` exports `Video`: a video player built on the platform's player (`AVPlayer` on iOS and Mac Catalyst, `MediaPlayer` on Android). Playback is controlled with props, so pausing is a signal away.

```ts
import { Video, type VideoProps } from "nsh/video";
```

See [Web view and video](https://nsh.dev/docs/web-view-and-video.md) for the guide and [`<Video>`](https://nsh.dev/elements/video.md) for its props.

## Video

```ts
const Video: (props: VideoProps) => YNode;

interface VideoProps extends Omit<ViewProps, "children">, VideoHostProps {
  source: string | { uri: string };
}
```

```tsx
import { mount, signal, Text, View, type YNode } from "nsh";
import { Video } from "nsh/video";

function Player() {
  const paused = signal(true);
  const time = signal("");
  let video!: YNode;
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      <Video
        ref={video}
        source="https://example.com/clip.mp4"
        paused={paused()}
        muted
        repeat
        resizeMode="cover"
        style={{ height: 220, borderRadius: 8, overflow: "hidden", backgroundColor: "#000" }}
        onProgress={(e) => time.set(`${e.currentTime.toFixed(1)} / ${e.duration.toFixed(1)} s`)}
      />
      <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 16 }}>
        <Text onPress={() => paused.update((p) => !p)}>{paused() ? "Play" : "Pause"}</Text>
        <Text onPress={() => video.seek(0)}>Restart</Text>
        <Text>{time()}</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

mount(Player);
```

## Props

`Video` takes the [view props](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md) (style, classes, layout, accessibility, `ref`; no children), plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | `string \| { uri: string }` | (required) | The video's URL. |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `false` | Playback is paused. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` | No sound. |
| `volume` | `number` | `1` | 0..1. |
| `rate` | `number` | `1` | The playback speed. |
| `repeat` | `boolean` | `false` | Plays again from the start at the end. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the platform's playback controls. |
| `resizeMode` | `"cover" \| "contain" \| "stretch" \| "center"` | | How the video fits its box. |
| `progressUpdateInterval` | `number` | `250` | Milliseconds between `onProgress` events. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `onLoadStart` | | The video starts loading. |
| `onLoad` | `{ duration: number; width: number; height: number }` | It is ready to play: its length in seconds and its size. |
| `onProgress` | `{ currentTime: number; duration: number }` | While playing, every `progressUpdateInterval` ms. Seconds. |
| `onBuffer` | `{ isBuffering: boolean }` | Playback waits for data, or resumes. |
| `onEnd` | | Playback reached the end. |
| `onError` | `{ message: string }` | The video could not be loaded or played. |

## Ref methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `seek(seconds)` | Jumps to `seconds`. |

```ts
const aspect = signal(16 / 9);

<Video source={url} onLoad={(e) => aspect.set(e.width / e.height)} style={{ width: "100%", aspectRatio: aspect() }} />;
```

## Capabilities

When your app declares `capabilities` in `nsh.json`, remote video sources must be allowed under `network`, like `fetch`; a refused source shows nothing. See [Sandbox and capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-video

---

# Global APIs

Besides the ECMAScript standard library, an NSH app's JS environment has a set of standard globals: `fetch` with `Headers`, `Request` and `Response`; the Streams Standard; `URL` and `URLSearchParams`; `TextEncoder` / `TextDecoder`; `Blob`, `File` and `FormData`; `EventTarget`, `Event` and `AbortController`; timers, `requestAnimationFrame` and `console`; and `Intl` for number and date formatting. They are implemented natively in Rust, follow the WHATWG standards, and need no import, so the many JavaScript libraries built on these standards (HTTP clients, URL and encoding helpers, stream utilities) work unchanged.

This page lists every global an app has. UI is built with [elements](https://nsh.dev/elements.md) and [components](https://nsh.dev/components.md), and everything else an app uses comes from the [modules](https://nsh.dev/modules.md) it imports.

The TypeScript declarations of all of these are generated into `.nsh/types/nsh/globals.d.ts` (see [Project structure](https://nsh.dev/docs/project-structure.md)).

| Group | Globals |
|---|---|
| [Console and timing](#console-and-timing) | `console`, `performance` |
| [Timers and frames](#timers-and-frames) | `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, `clearInterval`, `queueMicrotask`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `cancelAnimationFrame` |
| [Base64 and errors](#base64-and-errors) | `atob`, `btoa`, `DOMException` |
| [Events and abort signals](#events-and-abort-signals) | `EventTarget`, `Event`, `CustomEvent`, `AbortController`, `AbortSignal` |
| [URLs](#urls) | `URL`, `URLSearchParams` |
| [Text encoding](#text-encoding) | `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder` |
| [Blobs and form data](#blobs-and-form-data) | `Blob`, `File`, `FormData` |
| [Fetch](#fetch) | `fetch`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response` |
| [Number and date formatting](#number-and-date-formatting) | `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `toLocaleString` |
| [Streams](#streams) | `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, `TransformStream`, readers, writers, controllers, `ByteLengthQueuingStrategy`, `CountQueuingStrategy`, `TextEncoderStream`, `TextDecoderStream` |

## Console and timing

```ts
declare var console: {
  log(...data: unknown[]): void;
  info(...data: unknown[]): void;
  debug(...data: unknown[]): void;
  warn(...data: unknown[]): void;
  error(...data: unknown[]): void;
};

declare var performance: {
  /** Milliseconds since the JS context started, with sub-millisecond precision. */
  now(): number;
};
```

`console` writes one line per call to the runtime's log (target `js`): `log` and `info` at info level, `debug`, `warn` and `error` at their levels. Arguments are joined with spaces; strings print verbatim, errors with their stack, functions as `[Function name]`, and objects and arrays as JSON (falling back to `String(value)` for cycles).

While a device is connected to the dev server, its log lines appear in the terminal running `nsh run` / `nsh dev`, prefixed with the device name; see [Dev server and debugging](https://nsh.dev/docs/dev-server-and-debugging.md).

> [!NOTE]
> Only the five methods above exist. There is no `console.table`, `console.group`, `console.time` or `console.assert`, and no `%s` / `%o` format substitutions.

`performance.now()` is the clock `requestAnimationFrame` passes to its callbacks. `performance` has no other members.

## Timers and frames

```ts
function setTimeout(handler: (...args: any[]) => void, timeout?: number, ...args: any[]): number;
function setInterval(handler: (...args: any[]) => void, timeout?: number, ...args: any[]): number;
function clearTimeout(id: number | undefined): void;
function clearInterval(id: number | undefined): void;
function queueMicrotask(callback: () => void): void;
/** Runs `callback` at the next display frame with its time in milliseconds. */
function requestAnimationFrame(callback: (time: number) => void): number;
function cancelAnimationFrame(id: number): void;
```

Timers behave as in browsers: a missing, negative or non-finite delay is 0, the returned id is a positive integer, and clearing an unknown id does nothing. `handler` must be a function (string handlers are not evaluated). Timers do not clamp nested delays to 4 ms.

> [!WARNING]
> The extra `...args` of `setTimeout` / `setInterval` are declared but currently not passed to the handler. Use a closure instead: `setTimeout(() => save(id), 100)`.

`requestAnimationFrame` callbacks run once, at the next frame the engine produces, all with the same `performance.now()` time. A callback that requests another frame is called at the following frame, so the usual loop works:

```ts
let start = 0;
function tick(time: number) {
  if (!start) start = time;
  progress.set(Math.min(1, (time - start) / 300));
  if (time - start < 300) requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}
requestAnimationFrame(tick);
```

> [!TIP]
> Driving an animation from JS frame by frame runs your code on every frame in QuickJS. For animations of styles and transforms, prefer [nsh/animated](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md), whose drivers run natively without calling back into JS (see [Animation](https://nsh.dev/docs/animation.md)).

## Base64 and errors

```ts
function atob(data: string): string;
function btoa(data: string): string;

class DOMException extends Error {
  constructor(message?: string, name?: string);
  readonly name: string;
  readonly message: string;
  readonly code: number;
}
```

`atob` / `btoa` convert between binary strings and Base64 as in browsers. `DOMException` is what aborted operations reject with: an `AbortController.abort()` without a reason gives a `DOMException` named `"AbortError"`, and `AbortSignal.timeout` one named `"TimeoutError"`.

## Events and abort signals

```ts
class EventTarget {
  constructor();
  addEventListener(type: string, listener: EventListenerOrEventListenerObject | null,
    options?: AddEventListenerOptions | boolean): void;
  removeEventListener(type: string, listener: EventListenerOrEventListenerObject | null,
    options?: { capture?: boolean } | boolean): void;
  dispatchEvent(event: Event): boolean;
}

interface AddEventListenerOptions {
  capture?: boolean;
  once?: boolean;
  passive?: boolean;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}

class Event {
  constructor(type: string, init?: { bubbles?: boolean; cancelable?: boolean; composed?: boolean });
  readonly type: string;
  readonly target: EventTarget | null;
  readonly currentTarget: EventTarget | null;
  readonly eventPhase: number; // NONE 0, CAPTURING_PHASE 1, AT_TARGET 2, BUBBLING_PHASE 3
  readonly bubbles: boolean;
  readonly cancelable: boolean;
  readonly defaultPrevented: boolean;
  readonly composed: boolean;
  readonly isTrusted: boolean;
  readonly timeStamp: number;
  returnValue: boolean;
  cancelBubble: boolean;
  readonly srcElement: EventTarget | null; // legacy: `target`
  initEvent(type: string, bubbles?: boolean, cancelable?: boolean): void; // legacy
  composedPath(): EventTarget[];
  preventDefault(): void;
  stopPropagation(): void;
  stopImmediatePropagation(): void;
}

class CustomEvent<T = any> extends Event {
  constructor(type: string, init?: EventInit & { detail?: T });
  readonly detail: T;
}

class AbortController {
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  abort(reason?: any): void;
}

class AbortSignal extends EventTarget {
  readonly aborted: boolean;
  readonly reason: any;
  onabort: ((event: Event) => void) | null;
  throwIfAborted(): void;
  static abort(reason?: any): AbortSignal;
  static timeout(milliseconds: number): AbortSignal;
  static any(signals: Iterable<AbortSignal>): AbortSignal;
}
```

These are the DOM Standard's classes with one difference: there is no tree, so an event is dispatched to its target only. Capture listeners run first, then the others, as the DOM does at the target; `bubbles` has no effect. The classes can be subclassed, which makes `EventTarget` a small event emitter:

```ts
class Channel extends EventTarget {
  send(message: string) {
    this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("message", { detail: message }));
  }
}

const channel = new Channel();
channel.addEventListener("message", (e) => console.log((e as CustomEvent<string>).detail));
channel.send("hello");
```

These events are unrelated to the events of elements (`onPress`, `onChangeText`, ...), which are props; see [Touch and gestures](https://nsh.dev/docs/touch-and-gestures.md).

`AbortSignal` cancels `fetch` requests and stream pipes, and removes listeners added with `{ signal }`:

```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
const signal = AbortSignal.any([controller.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)]);
fetch("https://api.example.com/search?q=nsh", { signal }).catch((e) => {
  if (e.name === "AbortError" || e.name === "TimeoutError") return;
  throw e;
});
// later, for example when the screen closes:
controller.abort();
```

## URLs

```ts
class URL {
  constructor(url: string | URL, base?: string | URL);
  static canParse(url: string | URL, base?: string | URL): boolean;
  static parse(url: string | URL, base?: string | URL): URL | null;
  /** A `blob:` URL `fetch` reads `blob` from, until revoked. */
  static createObjectURL(blob: Blob): string;
  static revokeObjectURL(url: string): void;
  href: string;
  readonly origin: string;
  protocol: string;
  username: string;
  password: string;
  host: string;
  hostname: string;
  port: string;
  pathname: string;
  search: string;
  hash: string;
  readonly searchParams: URLSearchParams;
  toString(): string;
  toJSON(): string;
}

class URLSearchParams {
  constructor(init?: string | Record<string, string> | Iterable<[string, string]> | URLSearchParams);
  readonly size: number;
  append(name: string, value: string): void;
  delete(name: string, value?: string): void;
  get(name: string): string | null;
  getAll(name: string): string[];
  has(name: string, value?: string): boolean;
  set(name: string, value: string): void;
  sort(): void;
  forEach(callback: (value: string, key: string, parent: URLSearchParams) => void, thisArg?: unknown): void;
  entries(): IterableIterator<[string, string]>;
  keys(): IterableIterator<string>;
  values(): IterableIterator<string>;
  [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<[string, string]>;
  toString(): string;
}
```

URLs are parsed per the URL Standard. A URL's `searchParams` is live in both directions: changing the parameters rewrites the query, and setting `search` or `href` parses it again.

```ts
const url = new URL("/v1/items", "https://api.example.com");
url.searchParams.set("page", "2");
url.searchParams.append("tag", "new");
url.href; // "https://api.example.com/v1/items?page=2&tag=new"
```

The iterators of `URLSearchParams` (and of `Headers` and `FormData`) iterate over a snapshot taken when the iterator was created, and have the iterator helpers (`map`, `filter`, `toArray`, ...).

`URL.createObjectURL(blob)` returns a `blob:` URL that `fetch` (with `GET`) can read until `revokeObjectURL` is called. Such URLs are understood by `fetch` only, not by `<Image>` or other elements.

## Text encoding

```ts
class TextEncoder {
  readonly encoding: "utf-8";
  encode(input?: string): Uint8Array;
  encodeInto(source: string, destination: Uint8Array): { read: number; written: number };
}

/** UTF-8, UTF-16LE / BE and windows-1252 (with the labels of latin1 and ASCII). */
class TextDecoder {
  constructor(label?: string, options?: { fatal?: boolean; ignoreBOM?: boolean });
  readonly encoding: string;
  readonly fatal: boolean;
  readonly ignoreBOM: boolean;
  decode(input?: BufferSource, options?: { stream?: boolean }): string;
}
```

`TextDecoder` knows fewer encodings than a browser: UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE and windows-1252 (which the labels `latin1`, `iso-8859-1`, `ascii` and the like also name, as the Encoding Standard specifies). Other labels throw a `RangeError`. With `{ stream: true }`, a multi-byte sequence cut between two chunks is kept for the next call.

## Blobs and form data

```ts
class Blob {
  constructor(blobParts?: Iterable<BlobPart>, options?: { type?: string; endings?: "transparent" | "native" });
  readonly size: number;
  readonly type: string;
  slice(start?: number, end?: number, contentType?: string): Blob;
  arrayBuffer(): Promise<ArrayBuffer>;
  bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  text(): Promise<string>;
  stream(): ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
}

class File extends Blob {
  constructor(fileBits: Iterable<BlobPart>, fileName: string,
    options?: { type?: string; endings?: "transparent" | "native"; lastModified?: number });
  readonly name: string;
  readonly lastModified: number;
  readonly webkitRelativePath: string;
}

class FormData {
  constructor();
  append(name: string, value: string | Blob, fileName?: string): void;
  delete(name: string): void;
  get(name: string): File | string | null;
  getAll(name: string): (File | string)[];
  has(name: string): boolean;
  set(name: string, value: string | Blob, fileName?: string): void;
  forEach(callback: (value: File | string, key: string, parent: FormData) => void, thisArg?: unknown): void;
  entries(): IterableIterator<[string, File | string]>;
  keys(): IterableIterator<string>;
  values(): IterableIterator<File | string>;
  [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<[string, File | string]>;
}

type BlobPart = ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView | Blob | string;
```

A blob holds its bytes in memory, and `slice` shares them instead of copying. Blobs are in-memory values only: there is no file system access behind `File`, and `FormData` has no constructor from a form element.

A `FormData` body is sent as `multipart/form-data`, and `Response.formData()` / `Request.formData()` parse both `multipart/form-data` and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

```ts
const form = new FormData();
form.append("title", "Holiday");
form.append("photo", new Blob([bytes], { type: "image/jpeg" }), "photo.jpg");
await fetch("https://api.example.com/upload", { method: "POST", body: form });
```

## Fetch

```ts
/**
 * HTTP through the platform's network stack (NSURLSession,
 * HttpURLConnection), streaming both ways; `data:` and `blob:` URLs are
 * answered locally.
 */
function fetch(input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>;

interface RequestInit {
  method?: string;
  headers?: HeadersInit;
  /** A ReadableStream is sent as it is read (chunked), with `duplex: "half"`. */
  body?: BodyInit | null;
  duplex?: "half";
  signal?: AbortSignal | null;
  /** "manual" gives the 3xx response itself. */
  redirect?: "follow" | "manual" | "error";
  credentials?: "omit" | "same-origin" | "include";
  cache?: "default" | "no-store" | "reload" | "no-cache" | "force-cache" | "only-if-cached";
  mode?: "same-origin" | "no-cors" | "cors";
  referrer?: string;
  referrerPolicy?: string;
  integrity?: string;
  keepalive?: boolean;
  priority?: "high" | "low" | "auto";
}

type HeadersInit = Headers | Record<string, string> | Iterable<[string, string]>;
type BodyInit = ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | Blob | BufferSource | FormData | URLSearchParams | string;
```

`fetch` sends HTTP and HTTPS requests through the platform's own network stack: `NSURLSession` on iOS and Mac Catalyst, `HttpURLConnection` on Android. So the system's proxy settings, TLS configuration and certificate trust apply. `data:` URLs and `blob:` URLs (from `URL.createObjectURL`) are answered locally without touching the network; any other scheme rejects.

```ts
type Todo = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean };

async function loadTodos(): Promise<Todo[]> {
  const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/todos", {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}
```

### Headers, Request and Response

```ts
class Headers {
  constructor(init?: HeadersInit);
  append(name: string, value: string): void;
  delete(name: string): void;
  get(name: string): string | null;
  getSetCookie(): string[];
  has(name: string): boolean;
  set(name: string, value: string): void;
  forEach(callback: (value: string, key: string, parent: Headers) => void, thisArg?: unknown): void;
  entries(): IterableIterator<[string, string]>;
  keys(): IterableIterator<string>;
  values(): IterableIterator<string>;
  [Symbol.iterator](): IterableIterator<[string, string]>;
}

interface Body {
  /** The body as it arrives (a byte stream), or null. */
  readonly body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null;
  readonly bodyUsed: boolean;
  arrayBuffer(): Promise<ArrayBuffer>;
  blob(): Promise<Blob>;
  bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  formData(): Promise<FormData>;
  json(): Promise<any>;
  text(): Promise<string>;
}

class Request implements Body {
  constructor(input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit);
  readonly method: string;
  readonly url: string;
  readonly headers: Headers;
  readonly destination: string;
  readonly referrer: string;
  readonly referrerPolicy: string;
  readonly mode: string;
  readonly credentials: string;
  readonly cache: string;
  readonly redirect: "follow" | "manual" | "error";
  readonly integrity: string;
  readonly keepalive: boolean;
  readonly isReloadNavigation: boolean;
  readonly isHistoryNavigation: boolean;
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  readonly duplex: "half";
  clone(): Request;
  // ...and the Body members
}

class Response implements Body {
  constructor(body?: BodyInit | null, init?: { status?: number; statusText?: string; headers?: HeadersInit });
  static json(data: unknown, init?: ResponseInit): Response;
  static error(): Response;
  static redirect(url: string | URL, status?: number): Response;
  readonly type: "basic" | "default" | "error";
  readonly url: string;
  readonly redirected: boolean;
  readonly status: number;
  readonly ok: boolean;
  readonly statusText: string;
  readonly headers: Headers;
  clone(): Response;
  // ...and the Body members
}
```

### Streaming

A response's `body` is a byte stream filled as the network delivers data, so large or long-lived responses (downloads, server-sent events, streamed model output) can be processed while they arrive. When more than 1 MiB is waiting unread, the request is paused until the app reads again.

```ts
const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/events");
const lines = res.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream());
for await (const chunk of lines) {
  console.log(chunk);
}
```

A `ReadableStream` request body is uploaded chunk by chunk as the network asks for it; pass `duplex: "half"` as the Fetch Standard requires:

```ts
await fetch("https://api.example.com/upload", {
  method: "PUT",
  body: blob.stream(),
  duplex: "half",
});
```

### Differences from browsers

- **No CORS and no origin.** An app is not a web page: it may talk to any host its [capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md) allow. `mode` is accepted and ignored.
- **No forbidden headers.** An app may set `Cookie`, `User-Agent`, `Origin` and any other header. When no `Accept` header is given, `Accept: */*` is sent.
- **`redirect: "manual"` delivers the 3xx response itself**, with its status and `Location` header, instead of an opaque filtered response. `"follow"` follows redirects (each hop is checked against the capabilities); `"error"` rejects when the response is a redirect.
- **A `FormData` body always gets `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=…`**, even when a `Content-Type` header was set. HTTP libraries often set a default content type and clear it only where they detect a browser; without the boundary the server cannot parse the body.
- **`credentials`, `cache`, `referrer`, `referrerPolicy`, `integrity`, `keepalive` and `priority`** are validated and kept on the `Request` object, but are not passed to the network stack: caching and cookie handling are those of the platform's stack.
- **Capabilities.** When the app declares `network` capabilities in `nsh.json` (or the embedding app grants fewer), a request to a host that is not allowed never reaches the network and `fetch` rejects with a `TypeError`. See [Sandbox and capabilities](https://nsh.dev/docs/sandbox-and-capabilities.md).
- **Errors.** Network failures reject with a `TypeError` whose message starts with `Network request failed:`; aborts reject with the signal's `reason`.

See [Networking](https://nsh.dev/docs/networking.md) for a guide to loading data in components.

## Streams

The full WHATWG Streams Standard: readable streams (default and byte streams, BYOB readers, `tee`, `pipeTo` / `pipeThrough`, `ReadableStream.from`, async iteration), writable streams, transform streams, the two queuing strategies and the text encoding streams.

```ts
class ReadableStream<R = any> {
  constructor(underlyingSource: UnderlyingByteSource, strategy?: { highWaterMark?: number });
  constructor(underlyingSource?: UnderlyingDefaultSource<R>, strategy?: QueuingStrategy<R>);
  static from<R>(iterable: Iterable<R | PromiseLike<R>> | AsyncIterable<R>): ReadableStream<R>;
  readonly locked: boolean;
  cancel(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
  getReader(options: { mode: "byob" }): ReadableStreamBYOBReader;
  getReader(): ReadableStreamDefaultReader<R>;
  pipeThrough<T>(transform: { writable: WritableStream<R>; readable: ReadableStream<T> },
    options?: StreamPipeOptions): ReadableStream<T>;
  pipeTo(destination: WritableStream<R>, options?: StreamPipeOptions): Promise<void>;
  tee(): [ReadableStream<R>, ReadableStream<R>];
  values(options?: { preventCancel?: boolean }): AsyncIterableIterator<R>;
  [Symbol.asyncIterator](options?: { preventCancel?: boolean }): AsyncIterableIterator<R>;
}

class ReadableStreamDefaultReader<R = any> {
  constructor(stream: ReadableStream<R>);
  readonly closed: Promise<void>;
  read(): Promise<{ done: false; value: R } | { done: true; value?: R }>;
  releaseLock(): void;
  cancel(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
}

class ReadableStreamBYOBReader {
  constructor(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>);
  readonly closed: Promise<void>;
  read<T extends ArrayBufferView>(view: T, options?: { min?: number }): Promise<ReadableStreamReadResult<T>>;
  releaseLock(): void;
  cancel(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
}

class ReadableStreamDefaultController<R = any> {
  readonly desiredSize: number | null;
  close(): void;
  enqueue(chunk?: R): void;
  error(e?: any): void;
}

class ReadableByteStreamController {
  readonly byobRequest: ReadableStreamBYOBRequest | null;
  readonly desiredSize: number | null;
  close(): void;
  enqueue(chunk: ArrayBufferView): void;
  error(e?: any): void;
}

class ReadableStreamBYOBRequest {
  readonly view: ArrayBufferView | null;
  respond(bytesWritten: number): void;
  respondWithNewView(view: ArrayBufferView): void;
}

class WritableStream<W = any> {
  constructor(underlyingSink?: UnderlyingSink<W>, strategy?: QueuingStrategy<W>);
  readonly locked: boolean;
  abort(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
  getWriter(): WritableStreamDefaultWriter<W>;
}

class WritableStreamDefaultWriter<W = any> {
  constructor(stream: WritableStream<W>);
  readonly closed: Promise<void>;
  readonly desiredSize: number | null;
  readonly ready: Promise<void>;
  abort(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
  releaseLock(): void;
  write(chunk?: W): Promise<void>;
}

class WritableStreamDefaultController {
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  error(e?: any): void;
}

class TransformStream<I = any, O = any> {
  constructor(transformer?: Transformer<I, O>, writableStrategy?: QueuingStrategy<I>,
    readableStrategy?: QueuingStrategy<O>);
  readonly readable: ReadableStream<O>;
  readonly writable: WritableStream<I>;
}

class TransformStreamDefaultController<O = any> {
  readonly desiredSize: number | null;
  enqueue(chunk?: O): void;
  error(reason?: any): void;
  terminate(): void;
}

class ByteLengthQueuingStrategy {
  constructor(init: { highWaterMark: number });
  readonly highWaterMark: number;
  readonly size: (chunk: ArrayBufferView) => number;
}

class CountQueuingStrategy {
  constructor(init: { highWaterMark: number });
  readonly highWaterMark: number;
  readonly size: (chunk: any) => 1;
}

class TextEncoderStream {
  readonly encoding: "utf-8";
  readonly readable: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
  readonly writable: WritableStream<string>;
}

class TextDecoderStream {
  constructor(label?: string, options?: { fatal?: boolean; ignoreBOM?: boolean });
  readonly encoding: string;
  readonly fatal: boolean;
  readonly ignoreBOM: boolean;
  readonly readable: ReadableStream<string>;
  readonly writable: WritableStream<BufferSource>;
}
```

The underlying source, sink and transformer objects (`UnderlyingDefaultSource`, `UnderlyingByteSource`, `UnderlyingSink`, `Transformer`) and `StreamPipeOptions` (`preventAbort`, `preventCancel`, `preventClose`, `signal`) have the standard shapes; their full declarations are in `globals.d.ts`.

`TextEncoderStream` keeps a surrogate pair cut between two string chunks together, and `TextDecoderStream` a multi-byte sequence cut between two byte chunks.

A transform stream that splits text into lines:

```ts
function lines(): TransformStream<string, string> {
  let rest = "";
  return new TransformStream({
    transform(chunk, controller) {
      const parts = (rest + chunk).split("\n");
      rest = parts.pop()!;
      for (const line of parts) controller.enqueue(line);
    },
    flush(controller) {
      if (rest) controller.enqueue(rest);
    },
  });
}

const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/log");
for await (const line of res.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).pipeThrough(lines())) {
  console.log(line);
}
```

## Number and date formatting

QuickJS has no `Intl` of its own; NSH adds one, formatting in Rust: `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.getCanonicalLocales`, and the `toLocaleString` of numbers and BigInts and `toLocaleString` / `toLocaleDateString` / `toLocaleTimeString` of dates, which take the same `locales` and `options`. Their declarations are TypeScript's own (the `ES2023` library), so they are not in `globals.d.ts`.

```ts
(1234567.891).toLocaleString();                                              // "1,234,567.891" (en-US)
(1234.5).toLocaleString("de-DE", { style: "currency", currency: "EUR" });  // "1.234,50 €"
new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { notation: "compact" }).format(1_500_000);      // "1.5M"
new Intl.NumberFormat("en", { style: "percent", signDisplay: "exceptZero" }).format(0.042); // "+4%"
new Date().toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", hour12: false });   // "09:05"
new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" }).format(date); // "Oct 16, 2026, 3:04 PM"
```

Without `locales`, the device's locale is used: its region format (iOS `NSLocale.currentLocale`, Android `Locale.getDefault()`), `en-US` in `nsh trace` and on the web.

- **Numbers**: the `decimal`, `percent`, `currency` (`currencyDisplay` `symbol`, `narrowSymbol`, `code`) and `unit` (common units: lengths, masses, durations, data sizes, temperatures, speeds) styles; `minimumIntegerDigits`, `minimum` / `maximumFractionDigits`, `minimum` / `maximumSignificantDigits`, `roundingPriority`, `trailingZeroDisplay`, `useGrouping`, `signDisplay`; `standard`, `scientific`, `engineering` and `compact` notation (`compactDisplay` `short` / `long`). Rounding is half away from zero, on the number as written (`1.005` rounds to `1.01`, as in browsers). `format` also takes BigInts and decimal strings, exactly. `formatToParts` and `resolvedOptions` work as in browsers.
- **Dates**: `weekday`, `year`, `month` (`numeric`, `2-digit`, `short`, `long`, `narrow`), `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `fractionalSecondDigits`, `hour12` / `hourCycle`, `timeZoneName` and `dateStyle` / `timeStyle`, in the Gregorian calendar. `timeZone` takes the device's zone, `UTC` or an offset (`"+08:00"`); other zone names throw a `RangeError` (there is no time zone database).
- **Locales**: the locale data is a table of common languages (English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Swedish, Polish, Turkish, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, Hindi, Chinese, Japanese, Korean) with their regional variants (`en-GB`, `en-IN`, `de-CH`, `es-MX`, `pt-PT`, `zh-TW`, ...), not the whole of CLDR, so details can differ from a browser's output. A locale without data falls back to the next one asked for, then the device's, then `en-US`; Russian, Swedish, Polish, Turkish, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai and Hindi dates have no month names (their months are written as numbers, their weekdays in English). Digits are always Latin.
- **Not there**: `Intl.Collator` (`String.prototype.localeCompare` is QuickJS's, which ignores the locale), `PluralRules`, `RelativeTimeFormat`, `ListFormat`, `DisplayNames`, `Segmenter` and `Intl.Locale`; `currencySign: "accounting"` and `currencyDisplay: "name"` format as `standard` and `code`.

## Performance

All of these classes are native: parsing URLs, encoding and decoding text, building multipart bodies and moving stream chunks happen in Rust, not in QuickJS. Still, every call from JS crosses into the runtime, so prefer whole-buffer operations (`res.json()`, `res.text()`, `encoder.encode(s)`) over byte-by-byte loops in JS. See [Performance](https://nsh.dev/docs/performance.md).

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules/globals

---

# Style reference

This page lists every key of the `style` prop. The keys and their types come from the generated declarations in `.nsh/types/nsh/types.d.ts`, so your editor checks them as you type. Layout is flexbox with a column default, numbers are points, and the CSS features are there too: grid, gradients, box shadows, filters, blend modes, outlines, transitions and keyframe animations.

For how to apply styles, combine them with classes and inherit text styles, see [Styling](https://nsh.dev/docs/styling.md). For the class syntax, see the [Tailwind reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/tailwind-reference.md).

## The four interfaces

Each interface extends the one before it:

| Interface | Extends | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `LayoutStyle` | | Layout of every element (flexbox, grid, sizes, spacing, position) |
| `ViewStyle` | `LayoutStyle` | `<View>`, `<Scroll>`, `<List>`, controls and every other element |
| `TextStyle` | `ViewStyle` | `<Text>` and `<Input>` (and views, whose text styles pass to the text inside them) |
| `ImageStyle` | `ViewStyle` | `<Image>` |

```tsx
import type { ViewStyle, TextStyle } from "nsh";
import { Text, View } from "nsh";

const card: ViewStyle = {
  padding: 16,
  borderRadius: 12,
  backgroundColor: "#fff",
  boxShadow: "0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08)",
};

const title: TextStyle = { fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600", color: "#111" };

<View style={card}>
  <Text style={title}>Hello</Text>
</View>;
```

`style` also takes an array; entries merge left to right and falsy entries are skipped, so conditional styles need no spreading:

```tsx
<View style={[card, selected() && { borderColor: "#2563eb", borderWidth: 2 }]} />
```

> [!NOTE]
> The inline `style` always wins over `class`. Setting a key to `null` or `undefined` resets it to its default.

## Value types

| Type | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `number` | Points (density-independent). `1` is one point on iOS and one dp on Android. |
| `DimensionValue` | `number` (points), `` `${number}%` `` (of the parent), or `"auto"`. |
| `LengthValue` | `number` (points) or `` `${number}%` ``. No `"auto"`. |
| `ColorValue` | A CSS color string: `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()`, `oklch()`, `oklab()`, or a named CSS color (`black`, `white`, `transparent`, `rebeccapurple`, ...). |
| `NativeNode` | A native animated value or a node derived from it (see [nsh/animated](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md)). Accepted by `backgroundColor`, `opacity` and the steps of `transform`; the value then animates on the UI thread without JS. |

Strings with CSS syntax (`boxShadow`, `backgroundImage`, `filter`, `gridTemplateColumns`, ...) take lengths in `px` and bare numbers (both points), `pt`, or `rem` (16 points).

## LayoutStyle

Layout is computed in Rust (flexbox and CSS grid). The defaults differ from CSS's: `display: "flex"`, `flexDirection: "column"`, `flexShrink: 0`, `alignContent: "flex-start"`, `alignItems: "stretch"`, and no automatic minimum size. See [Layout](https://nsh.dev/docs/layout.md).

### Display and position

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `display` | `"flex" \| "grid" \| "block" \| "none"` | The layout of the children. `"none"` removes the element from layout and hides it. `"block"` stacks children as CSS block layout does. Default `"flex"`. |
| `position` | `"relative" \| "absolute"` | `"absolute"` takes the element out of the flow and places it by `top` / `right` / `bottom` / `left` relative to its parent. Default `"relative"`. |
| `top` | `DimensionValue` | Offset from the parent's top edge (absolute) or from the element's own position (relative). |
| `right` | `DimensionValue` | Offset from the right edge. In right-to-left layouts it means the end edge. |
| `bottom` | `DimensionValue` | Offset from the bottom edge. |
| `left` | `DimensionValue` | Offset from the left edge. In right-to-left layouts it means the start edge. |
| `start` | `DimensionValue` | Left in left-to-right layouts, right in right-to-left ones. |
| `end` | `DimensionValue` | Right in left-to-right layouts, left in right-to-left ones. |
| `zIndex` | `number` | Order among siblings (stable for equal values); also the native stacking order. |
| `direction` | `"inherit" \| "ltr" \| "rtl"` | Layout direction, inherited by default. Right to left, `left` and `right` properties mean start and end. |

### Flexbox

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flexDirection` | `"row" \| "column" \| "row-reverse" \| "column-reverse"` | The main axis. Default `"column"`. |
| `flexWrap` | `"wrap" \| "nowrap" \| "wrap-reverse"` | Whether children wrap onto several lines. Default `"nowrap"`. |
| `flex` | `number` | One number, not the CSS shorthand: a positive number sets `flexGrow` to it, `flexShrink: 1` and `flexBasis: 0`; `0` makes the element inflexible; a negative number shrinks it down to its minimum size. |
| `flexGrow` | `number` | How much of the free space the element takes. Default `0`. |
| `flexShrink` | `number` | How much the element shrinks when space runs out. Default `0`, not `1` as in CSS. |
| `flexBasis` | `DimensionValue` | The main-axis size before free space is distributed. |
| `justifyContent` | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "space-between" \| "space-around" \| "space-evenly" \| "stretch"` | Distribution of children along the main axis. Default `"flex-start"`. |
| `alignItems` | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` | Alignment of children on the cross axis. Default `"stretch"`. |
| `alignSelf` | `"auto" \| "flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` | Overrides the parent's `alignItems` for this element. |
| `alignContent` | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "space-between" \| "space-around" \| "space-evenly"` | Distribution of wrapped lines (and grid tracks) on the cross axis. Default `"flex-start"`. |
| `gap` | `LengthValue` | Space between rows and columns of children. |
| `rowGap` | `LengthValue` | Space between rows. |
| `columnGap` | `LengthValue` | Space between columns. |

### Grid

Set `display: "grid"` to lay out children in a CSS grid. Track lists use CSS syntax.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gridTemplateColumns` | `string` | Column tracks: `"repeat(3, 1fr)"`, `"200px 1fr"`, `minmax()`, `auto-fill` / `auto-fit`, line names. |
| `gridTemplateRows` | `string` | Row tracks, same syntax. |
| `gridAutoColumns` | `string` | Size of implicitly created columns. |
| `gridAutoRows` | `string` | Size of implicitly created rows. |
| `gridAutoFlow` | `"row" \| "column" \| "dense" \| "row dense" \| "column dense"` | How items without a placement fill the grid. |
| `gridColumn` | `number \| string` | Column placement: `"1 / 3"`, `"span 2"`, a line number or a line name. |
| `gridColumnStart` | `number \| string` | Start column line. |
| `gridColumnEnd` | `number \| string` | End column line. |
| `gridRow` | `number \| string` | Row placement, same syntax as `gridColumn`. |
| `gridRowStart` | `number \| string` | Start row line. |
| `gridRowEnd` | `number \| string` | End row line. |
| `justifyItems` | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` | How grid items sit in their areas along the row. |
| `justifySelf` | `"auto" \| "flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` | Overrides `justifyItems` for this item. |

```tsx
<View style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(3, 1fr)", gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ gridColumn: "span 2", height: 60, backgroundColor: "#c7d2fe" }} />
  <View style={{ height: 60, backgroundColor: "#a5b4fc" }} />
</View>
```

### Size

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `DimensionValue` | Width. |
| `height` | `DimensionValue` | Height. |
| `minWidth` | `LengthValue` | Minimum width. |
| `minHeight` | `LengthValue` | Minimum height. |
| `maxWidth` | `LengthValue` | Maximum width. |
| `maxHeight` | `LengthValue` | Maximum height. |
| `aspectRatio` | `number` | Width divided by height; the missing dimension is computed from the other one. |

### Margin

Margins accept `"auto"` (absorbs free space, as in flexbox) and negative values.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` | `DimensionValue` | All four sides. |
| `marginHorizontal` | `DimensionValue` | Left and right. |
| `marginVertical` | `DimensionValue` | Top and bottom. |
| `marginTop` | `DimensionValue` | Top. |
| `marginRight` | `DimensionValue` | Right. |
| `marginBottom` | `DimensionValue` | Bottom. |
| `marginLeft` | `DimensionValue` | Left. |
| `marginStart` | `DimensionValue` | Left in left-to-right layouts, right in right-to-left ones. |
| `marginEnd` | `DimensionValue` | The opposite of `marginStart`. |

### Padding

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `padding` | `LengthValue` | All four sides. |
| `paddingHorizontal` | `LengthValue` | Left and right. |
| `paddingVertical` | `LengthValue` | Top and bottom. |
| `paddingTop` | `LengthValue` | Top. |
| `paddingRight` | `LengthValue` | Right. |
| `paddingBottom` | `LengthValue` | Bottom. |
| `paddingLeft` | `LengthValue` | Left. |
| `paddingStart` | `LengthValue` | Left in left-to-right layouts, right in right-to-left ones. |
| `paddingEnd` | `LengthValue` | The opposite of `paddingStart`. |

## ViewStyle

Everything drawn by a view. All keys of `LayoutStyle` apply too.

### Background

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `backgroundColor` | `ColorValue \| NativeNode` | The fill color. Takes a native animated color. |
| `backgroundImage` | `string` | CSS gradients drawn over the background color: `linear-gradient(...)`, `radial-gradient(...)`, `conic-gradient(...)`, several separated by commas. |
| `experimental_backgroundImage` | `string` | Alias of `backgroundImage`. |

```tsx
<View style={{ height: 120, borderRadius: 16, backgroundImage: "linear-gradient(135deg, #6366f1, #ec4899)" }} />
```

### Borders

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `borderWidth` | `number` | Width of all four sides. |
| `borderTopWidth` | `number` | Top side. |
| `borderRightWidth` | `number` | Right side. |
| `borderBottomWidth` | `number` | Bottom side. |
| `borderLeftWidth` | `number` | Left side. |
| `borderStartWidth` | `number` | Start side (left in left-to-right layouts). |
| `borderEndWidth` | `number` | End side. |
| `borderColor` | `ColorValue` | Color of all four sides. |
| `borderTopColor` | `ColorValue` | Top side. |
| `borderRightColor` | `ColorValue` | Right side. |
| `borderBottomColor` | `ColorValue` | Bottom side. |
| `borderLeftColor` | `ColorValue` | Left side. |
| `borderStartColor` | `ColorValue` | Start side. |
| `borderEndColor` | `ColorValue` | End side. |
| `borderStyle` | `"solid" \| "dashed" \| "dotted"` | Line style. Default `"solid"`. |

### Corners

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `borderRadius` | `number` | Radius of all four corners. |
| `borderTopLeftRadius` | `number` | Top-left corner. |
| `borderTopRightRadius` | `number` | Top-right corner. |
| `borderBottomRightRadius` | `number` | Bottom-right corner. |
| `borderBottomLeftRadius` | `number` | Bottom-left corner. |
| `borderTopStartRadius` | `number` | Top corner on the start side. |
| `borderTopEndRadius` | `number` | Top corner on the end side. |
| `borderBottomStartRadius` | `number` | Bottom corner on the start side. |
| `borderBottomEndRadius` | `number` | Bottom corner on the end side. |
| `borderCurve` | `"circular" \| "continuous"` | `"continuous"`: corners whose curvature eases into the edges, like iOS app icons. Where the box is too small the curve falls back to circular, so pills stay pills. Works on both platforms. |

### Outline

An outline is drawn outside the border and takes no space in layout.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `outlineWidth` | `number` | Line width. |
| `outlineColor` | `ColorValue` | Line color. |
| `outlineStyle` | `"solid" \| "double" \| "dashed" \| "dotted" \| "none" \| "hidden"` | Line style. |
| `outlineOffset` | `number` | Distance from the border edge; negative values move it inside. |

### Shadows

Two ways to cast a shadow: the CSS `boxShadow` (several layers, spread, inset) or the four `shadow*` keys.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `boxShadow` | `string` | CSS `box-shadow`: offsets, blur, spread and color, several layers separated by commas, `inset` for inner shadows. |
| `shadowColor` | `ColorValue` | Shadow color. |
| `shadowOffset` | `{ width: number; height: number }` | Offset. Default `{ width: 0, height: -3 }`. |
| `shadowOpacity` | `number` | Opacity, 0 to 1. Default `0` (no shadow). |
| `shadowRadius` | `number` | Blur radius. Default `3`. |

```tsx
<View style={{ padding: 16, borderRadius: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff",
  boxShadow: "0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 8px 24px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12)" }} />
```

> [!NOTE]
> On Android, shadows need a background: a view with a transparent background (text on nothing, for example) casts no shadow. For Android's material shadow use the `android={{ elevation }}` prop instead of a style.

### Opacity, visibility and overflow

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | `number \| NativeNode` | 0 (invisible) to 1. Takes a native animated value. |
| `visibility` | `"visible" \| "hidden" \| "collapse"` | Hidden views keep their space in layout (unlike `display: "none"`). |
| `overflow` | `"visible" \| "hidden"` | `"hidden"` clips children to the view's bounds (and corners). |
| `backfaceVisibility` | `"visible" \| "hidden"` | `"hidden"`: invisible while a 3D rotation turns it away. |

### Transforms

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transform` | `TransformStep[]` | A list of steps, applied right to left like CSS. |
| `transformOrigin` | `string \| (number \| string)[]` | The point `transform` acts around: keywords, percentages and lengths (`"top left"`, `"50% 0"`, `[10, 20]`). Default the center. |

A `TransformStep` is an object with one key:

| Step | Value | Native animated |
|---|---|---|
| `translateX`, `translateY` | `number` (points) | yes |
| `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY` | `number` (factor) | yes |
| `rotate`, `rotateZ`, `rotateX`, `rotateY` | `number` (degrees) or `string` (`"45deg"`, `"0.5rad"`) | yes |
| `skewX`, `skewY` | `number` (degrees) or `string` | no |
| `perspective` | `number` | no |

```tsx
<View style={{ transform: [{ perspective: 600 }, { rotateY: "20deg" }, { scale: 0.95 }] }} />
```

> [!NOTE]
> Android has no skew: `skewX` and `skewY` are ignored there.

### Filters and blending

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `filter` | `string` | CSS filters of the view and its content: `brightness()`, `contrast()`, `grayscale()`, `hue-rotate()`, `invert()`, `saturate()`, `sepia()`, `opacity()`, `blur()`, `drop-shadow()`. |
| `backdropFilter` | `string` | CSS filters of what is behind the view, such as `"blur(10px)"` for frosted glass. |
| `mixBlendMode` | `"normal" \| "multiply" \| "screen" \| "overlay" \| "darken" \| "lighten" \| "color-dodge" \| "color-burn" \| "hard-light" \| "soft-light" \| "difference" \| "exclusion" \| "hue" \| "saturation" \| "color" \| "luminosity" \| "plus-darker" \| "plus-lighter"` | How the view blends with what is behind it. |

> [!WARNING]
> Platform limits:
> - iOS applies only `opacity()`, `brightness()` up to 1 and `drop-shadow()` to views. `<Image>` takes every color filter and `blur()`, applied while the image is decoded.
> - iOS `backdropFilter` blur uses a system material at a fraction, an approximation of the exact radius.
> - Android needs API 31 for `blur()`, `drop-shadow()` and `backdropFilter`; below that only color filters apply. Blend modes need API 29.

### Transitions

When a transitioned property changes (from a new style, a class or a variant such as `active:`), the platform animates it natively. No JS runs during the animation.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transitionProperty` | `string` | Comma-separated properties that animate: `"all"`, `"colors"` (`color`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, ...), `"opacity"`, `"transform"`, `"boxShadow"`, `"borderRadius"`, `"borderWidth"`, or `"none"`. |
| `transitionDuration` | `number \| "${number}ms" \| "${number}s"` | Milliseconds as a number, or `"150ms"` / `"0.2s"`. |
| `transitionDelay` | `number \| "${number}ms" \| "${number}s"` | Delay before the transition starts. |
| `transitionTimingFunction` | `"linear" \| "ease" \| "ease-in" \| "ease-out" \| "ease-in-out" \| "cubic-bezier(...)"` | The easing curve. |

```tsx
<View
  onPress={() => open.set(!open())}
  style={{ height: open() ? 160 : 56, opacity: open() ? 1 : 0.8,
    transitionProperty: "opacity, transform", transitionDuration: 200 }}
/>
```

### Keyframe animations

Built-in keyframe animations, run natively (Tailwind's `animate-*`).

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `animationName` | `"none" \| "spin" \| "ping" \| "pulse" \| "bounce"` | The animation. |
| `animationDuration` | `number \| "${number}ms" \| "${number}s"` | Length of one iteration. |
| `animationDelay` | `number \| "${number}ms" \| "${number}s"` | Delay before the first iteration. |
| `animationTimingFunction` | `"linear" \| "ease" \| "ease-in" \| "ease-out" \| "ease-in-out" \| "cubic-bezier(...)"` | The easing curve. |
| `animationIterationCount` | `number \| "infinite"` | How many times it runs. |

For animations driven by values, gestures or springs, use [nsh/animated](https://nsh.dev/modules/nsh-animated.md) instead.

### Pointer

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | `"auto" \| "default" \| "pointer" \| "text" \| "grab" \| "grabbing" \| "not-allowed" \| ...` (every CSS cursor keyword, and `"none"`) | The pointer shape over the view, for pointers (iPad trackpads, Mac Catalyst, desktops). |

## TextStyle

Text styles apply to `<Text>` and `<Input>`. They are also inherited, as in CSS: text properties set on a view pass to the texts and inputs inside it, and nested `<Text>` spans inherit from their parent text. All keys of `ViewStyle` apply too. See [Text](https://nsh.dev/docs/text.md).

### Font

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `ColorValue` | Text color. |
| `fontSize` | `number` | Size in points. |
| `fontWeight` | `"normal" \| "bold" \| number \| "${number}"` | `"normal"` (400), `"bold"` (700) or 100–900. |
| `fontFamily` | `string` | A system family, or the name an imported font evaluates to (`import Inter from "./Inter.ttf"`). See [Fonts](https://nsh.dev/docs/fonts.md). |
| `fontStyle` | `"normal" \| "italic"` | Italic. |
| `fontVariant` | `("small-caps" \| "oldstyle-nums" \| "lining-nums" \| "tabular-nums" \| "proportional-nums")[]` | OpenType number and letter forms. `tabular-nums` keeps digits the same width, useful for counters and timers. |

### Spacing and alignment

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `lineHeight` | `number` | Line height in points. |
| `letterSpacing` | `number` | Extra space between characters, in points. |
| `textAlign` | `"auto" \| "left" \| "center" \| "right" \| "justify"` | Horizontal alignment. |
| `textAlignVertical` | `"auto" \| "top" \| "center" \| "bottom"` | Where text shorter than its box sits (a `<Text>` with a height). |
| `writingDirection` | `"auto" \| "ltr" \| "rtl"` | Base direction of the text; `"auto"` takes it from the content. |
| `textTransform` | `"none" \| "uppercase" \| "lowercase" \| "capitalize"` | Case transformation. |

> [!TIP]
> Tailwind's `leading-*` and `tracking-*` classes set line heights as multiples of the font size and letter spacing in `em`, so they scale with `text-*` sizes.

### Decoration

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `textDecorationLine` | `"none" \| "underline" \| "line-through" \| "underline line-through"` | Lines drawn with the text. |
| `textDecorationColor` | `ColorValue` | Color of the lines (default the text color). |
| `textDecorationStyle` | `"solid" \| "double" \| "dotted" \| "dashed" \| "wavy"` | Line style. |
| `textDecorationThickness` | `number \| "auto" \| "from-font"` | Line thickness. |
| `textUnderlineOffset` | `number \| "auto"` | Distance of the underline from the baseline. |

### Text shadow

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `textShadowColor` | `ColorValue` | Shadow color. |
| `textShadowOffset` | `{ width: number; height: number }` | Shadow offset. |
| `textShadowRadius` | `number` | Blur radius. |

> [!NOTE]
> iOS draws no gradients (`backgroundImage`) or inset box shadows on `<Text>`.

## ImageStyle

All keys of `ViewStyle`, plus:

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tintColor` | `ColorValue` | Recolors a template image (every opaque pixel takes this color), for monochrome icons. |

How an image fills its box is the `resizeMode` prop of `<Image>`, not a style; see [image](https://nsh.dev/elements/image.md).

## Props that look like styles

Some settings are props in NSH, not style keys. Their Tailwind classes exist, but an explicit prop wins over the class:

| Setting | Prop | Class |
|---|---|---|
| Line limit | `numberOfLines` on `<Text>` | `line-clamp-*`, `truncate` |
| Ellipsis position | `ellipsizeMode` on `<Text>` | `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip` |
| Touch pass-through | `pointerEvents` | `pointer-events-none`, `pointer-events-auto` |
| Image fit | `resizeMode` on `<Image>` | `object-cover`, `object-contain`, ... |
| Selectable text | `selectable` on `<Text>` | `select-text`, `select-none` |
| Placeholder color | `placeholderTextColor` on `<Input>` | `placeholder:text-*` |
| Material shadow (Android) | `android={{ elevation }}` | |

## Related

- [Styling](https://nsh.dev/docs/styling.md): `style`, `class`, inheritance and precedence.
- [Tailwind reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/tailwind-reference.md): every supported utility and variant.
- [Layout](https://nsh.dev/docs/layout.md): flexbox and grid in practice.
- [view](https://nsh.dev/elements/view.md), [text](https://nsh.dev/elements/text.md), [image](https://nsh.dev/elements/image.md): the elements these styles apply to.

Source: https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference

---

# Tailwind reference

Every element takes Tailwind CSS classes in its `class` prop (and conditional ones in `classList`). NSH resolves them in Rust against Tailwind 4's default theme: JS passes only the string, each distinct string is parsed once and cached, and variants such as `dark:` or `active:` are re-evaluated natively when the appearance, window size or press state changes, without running any JS.

This page lists what is supported. For an introduction see [Tailwind](https://nsh.dev/docs/tailwind.md); for the style keys the utilities set, see the [Style reference](https://nsh.dev/modules/style-reference.md).

```tsx
<View class="flex-row items-center gap-3 rounded-2xl bg-white p-4 shadow-md active:scale-[0.98] transition dark:bg-zinc-800">
  <Text class="text-base font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-white">Inbox</Text>
  <Text classList={{ "text-red-500": unread() > 0, "text-zinc-400": unread() === 0 }}>{unread()}</Text>
</View>
```

## How classes combine

- **Later wins.** Among utilities of the same variant level, the one later in the string wins: `"p-4 p-2"` is `p-2`. A component can take a `class` prop and append it to its own classes without `tailwind-merge`.
- **Variants apply after plain utilities**, in Tailwind's variant order: position (`first:` ...), `group-*:`, `focus-within:`, `hover:`, `focus:`, `active:`, `enabled:`, `disabled:`, motion, `max-*:` breakpoints, then breakpoints ascending, orientation, direction, `dark:`, then platform. So `"active:bg-red-500 bg-blue-500"` is red while pressed.
- **`style` wins over classes.** The inline `style` is applied on top of the resolved classes. An important utility (`!p-4` or `p-4!`) wins over the inline style too.
- **Text styles inherit.** Text utilities on a view (`text-white`, `font-bold`, `text-center`, ...) pass to the `<Text>` and `<Input>` elements inside it, as in CSS.
- **Display is CSS's.** `flex` and `inline-flex` make a row unless a direction utility says otherwise, wherever it is in the string (`flex-col flex` is a column). Views without `flex` keep NSH's column default.

## Units and the theme

Lengths are points (`1` = one point on iOS, one dp on Android). Tailwind's `1rem` is 16 points, so the theme matches the web at the same density: one spacing step is 4 points (`p-4` = 16 points), `text-base` is 16 points.

### Spacing values

Utilities that take a spacing value (padding, margin, gap, inset, width, height, `basis`, `translate`, `leading`) accept:

| Value | Example | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Steps (quarter steps allowed) | `p-4`, `gap-1.5`, `m-0.25` | step × 4 points |
| `px` | `p-px`, `-mt-px` | 1 point |
| `0` | `m-0` | 0 |
| Fraction | `w-1/2`, `left-1/3` | percentage of the parent |
| `full` | `w-full`, `inset-full` | 100% |
| `auto` (margin, inset, width, height, basis) | `mx-auto`, `w-auto` | `"auto"` |
| Arbitrary | `p-[13px]`, `w-[42%]`, `mt-[1.5rem]` | the given length |

Margins, insets, `translate`, `rotate`, `skew`, `scale`, `z`, `hue-rotate`, `tracking`, `underline-offset`, `outline-offset`, grid lines and gradient angles take a leading `-` for negative values: `-mt-2`, `-translate-x-1/2`, `-rotate-6`.

### Colors

The full Tailwind 4 palette is built in: `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `sky`, `blue`, `indigo`, `violet`, `purple`, `fuchsia`, `pink`, `rose`, `slate`, `gray`, `zinc`, `neutral`, `stone`, each in shades `50`, `100`–`900`, `950`; plus `black`, `white` and `transparent`. Your own colors come from `nsh.json` (see [Theme customization](#theme-customization)).

Every color utility takes:

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| A theme color | `bg-sky-500`, `text-brand` |
| An opacity modifier (percent) | `bg-black/50`, `ring-black/5` |
| An arbitrary opacity | `text-black/[0.35]` |
| An arbitrary color | `bg-[#0ea5e9]`, `border-[rgb(0_0_0_/_0.1)]`, `text-[oklch(70%_0.2_50)]` |
| An arbitrary color with a modifier | `bg-[rgb(0_0_255)]/25` |

`currentColor` and `inherit` are not color values; rings default to the element's text color when no ring color is given.

## Arbitrary values

Square brackets pass a value the theme does not have: `w-[37px]`, `grid-cols-[200px_1fr]`, `bg-[linear-gradient(45deg,red,blue)]`.

- `_` stands for a space (`grid-cols-[1fr_2fr]`); write `\_` for a literal underscore.
- Lengths: a bare number or `px` (points), `pt`, `rem` (16 points), and `%` where percentages make sense.
- Angles (`rotate-[...]`, `hue-rotate-[...]`, `bg-linear-[...]`): `deg`, `rad`, `grad`, `turn`.
- Times (`duration-[...]`, `delay-[...]`): `ms` or `s`; a bare number is milliseconds.
- Type hints settle ambiguous values: `text-[length:22px]` is a size, `text-[color:#333]` a color; `border-[length:3px]` likewise.

Arbitrary CSS properties (`[mask-type:luminance]`) are not supported.

## Layout

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `flex`, `inline-flex` | `display: "flex"`, and a row unless a direction utility is present |
| `grid`, `inline-grid` | `display: "grid"` |
| `block`, `flow-root` | `display: "block"` (block layout) |
| `inline`, `inline-block` | `display: "flex"` (there is no inline formatting context: they lay out as views) |
| `hidden` | `display: "none"` |
| `relative`, `static`, `sticky` | `position: "relative"` (`sticky` does not stick) |
| `absolute`, `fixed` | `position: "absolute"` (`fixed` is relative to the parent, not the screen) |
| `inset-<n>`, `inset-x-<n>`, `inset-y-<n>` | `top` / `right` / `bottom` / `left` |
| `top-<n>`, `right-<n>`, `bottom-<n>`, `left-<n>` | the matching offset |
| `start-<n>`, `end-<n>` | `start` / `end` (direction-aware) |
| `z-<n>`, `z-auto`, `z-[<n>]` | `zIndex` (`z-auto` is 0) |
| `visible` | `visibility: "visible"` |
| `invisible`, `collapse` | `visibility: "hidden"` (keeps its space) |
| `overflow-hidden`, `overflow-clip`, `overflow-x-hidden`, `overflow-y-hidden` | `overflow: "hidden"` |
| `overflow-visible` | `overflow: "visible"` |
| `aspect-square`, `aspect-video`, `aspect-<a>/<b>`, `aspect-[<a>/<b>]`, `aspect-auto` | `aspectRatio` (1, 16/9, a/b, none) |

Scrolling is an element, not a class: `overflow-auto` and `overflow-scroll` are not supported; use [scroll](https://nsh.dev/elements/scroll.md).

## Flexbox and grid

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `flex-row`, `flex-row-reverse`, `flex-col`, `flex-col-reverse` | `flexDirection` |
| `flex-wrap`, `flex-wrap-reverse`, `flex-nowrap` | `flexWrap` |
| `flex-1` | grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0 |
| `flex-<n>` | grow n, shrink 1, basis 0 |
| `flex-auto` | grow 1, shrink 1, basis auto |
| `flex-initial` | grow 0, shrink 1, basis auto |
| `flex-none` | grow 0, shrink 0, basis auto |
| `flex-[<grow>]`, `flex-[<grow>_<shrink>_<basis>]` | the CSS shorthand: `flex-[2]`, `flex-[3_0_50%]` |
| `grow`, `grow-<n>`, `grow-[<n>]` | `flexGrow` (bare: 1) |
| `shrink`, `shrink-<n>`, `shrink-[<n>]` | `flexShrink` (bare: 1) |
| `basis-<n>` | `flexBasis` (spacing, fraction, `full`, `auto`, arbitrary) |
| `justify-start`, `justify-end`, `justify-center`, `justify-between`, `justify-around`, `justify-evenly`, `justify-stretch`, `justify-normal` | `justifyContent` |
| `items-start`, `items-end`, `items-center`, `items-baseline`, `items-stretch` | `alignItems` |
| `self-auto`, `self-start`, `self-end`, `self-center`, `self-stretch`, `self-baseline` | `alignSelf` |
| `content-start`, `content-end`, `content-center`, `content-between`, `content-around`, `content-evenly`, `content-stretch`, `content-normal` | `alignContent` |
| `justify-items-start`, `-end`, `-center`, `-stretch`, `-normal` | `justifyItems` |
| `justify-self-auto`, `-start`, `-end`, `-center`, `-stretch` | `justifySelf` |
| `place-content-center`, `-start`, `-end`, `-between`, `-stretch` | `alignContent` and `justifyContent` |
| `place-items-center`, `-start`, `-end`, `-stretch` | `alignItems` and `justifyItems` |
| `place-self-auto`, `-center`, `-start`, `-end`, `-stretch` | `alignSelf` and `justifySelf` |
| `gap-<n>`, `gap-x-<n>`, `gap-y-<n>` | `gap`, `columnGap`, `rowGap` |
| `space-x-<n>`, `space-y-<n>` | `columnGap`, `rowGap` (a gap, not margins on the children) |
| `grid-cols-<n>` | `gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))"` |
| `grid-cols-[<tracks>]`, `grid-cols-none` | `gridTemplateColumns` (`grid-cols-[200px_1fr]`) |
| `grid-rows-<n>`, `grid-rows-[<tracks>]`, `grid-rows-none` | `gridTemplateRows` |
| `col-span-<n>`, `col-span-full`, `col-auto`, `col-<n>`, `col-[<value>]` | `gridColumn` |
| `col-start-<n>`, `col-end-<n>` (and `-auto`) | `gridColumnStart`, `gridColumnEnd` |
| `row-span-<n>`, `row-span-full`, `row-auto`, `row-<n>`, `row-[<value>]` | `gridRow` |
| `row-start-<n>`, `row-end-<n>` (and `-auto`) | `gridRowStart`, `gridRowEnd` |
| `grid-flow-row`, `grid-flow-col`, `grid-flow-dense`, `grid-flow-row-dense`, `grid-flow-col-dense` | `gridAutoFlow` |
| `auto-cols-auto`, `-min`, `-max`, `-fr`, `auto-cols-[<track>]` | `gridAutoColumns` |
| `auto-rows-auto`, `-min`, `-max`, `-fr`, `auto-rows-[<track>]` | `gridAutoRows` |

`order-*` is accepted but has no effect: children keep their order.

## Spacing

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `p-<n>`, `px-<n>`, `py-<n>` | `padding`, `paddingHorizontal`, `paddingVertical` |
| `pt-<n>`, `pr-<n>`, `pb-<n>`, `pl-<n>` | `paddingTop` / `Right` / `Bottom` / `Left` |
| `ps-<n>`, `pe-<n>` | `paddingStart`, `paddingEnd` |
| `m-<n>`, `mx-<n>`, `my-<n>` | `margin`, `marginHorizontal`, `marginVertical` |
| `mt-<n>`, `mr-<n>`, `mb-<n>`, `ml-<n>` | `marginTop` / `Right` / `Bottom` / `Left` |
| `ms-<n>`, `me-<n>` | `marginStart`, `marginEnd` |

## Sizing

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `w-<n>`, `h-<n>` | `width`, `height` (spacing, fraction, `full`, `auto`, arbitrary) |
| `size-<n>` | `width` and `height` |
| `min-w-<n>`, `max-w-<n>`, `min-h-<n>`, `max-h-<n>` | the matching limit |
| `w-screen`, `w-dvw`, `w-svw`, `w-lvw` | the window width (also on `min-w-` / `max-w-`) |
| `h-screen`, `h-dvh`, `h-svh`, `h-lvh` | the window height (also on `min-h-` / `max-h-`) |
| `w-min`, `w-max`, `w-fit` (and `h-`) | `auto` (sized by content) |
| `min-w-min`, `min-w-max`, `min-w-fit` (and `min-h-`) | 0 |
| `max-w-none`, `max-h-none`, `max-w-min`, `max-w-max`, `max-w-fit` | no limit |
| `w-<container>`, `min-w-<container>`, `max-w-<container>` | a container width (below) |

Container widths (points): `3xs` 256, `2xs` 288, `xs` 320, `sm` 384, `md` 448, `lg` 512, `xl` 576, `2xl` 672, `3xl` 768, `4xl` 896, `5xl` 1024, `6xl` 1152, `7xl` 1280, `prose` 520.

## Typography

### Font

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `font-sans` | the system font |
| `font-serif`, `font-mono` | `fontFamily: "serif"` / `"monospace"` |
| `font-thin` (100), `font-extralight` (200), `font-light` (300), `font-normal` (400), `font-medium` (500), `font-semibold` (600), `font-bold` (700), `font-extrabold` (800), `font-black` (900) | `fontWeight` |
| `font-[<weight>]`, `font-[<family>]` | a numeric weight, otherwise a family: `font-[650]`, `font-[Inter]` |
| `italic`, `not-italic` | `fontStyle` |
| `normal-nums`, `small-caps`, `oldstyle-nums`, `lining-nums`, `tabular-nums`, `proportional-nums` | `fontVariant` (they combine) |

### Size, color and line height

`text-<size>` sets the font size and Tailwind's matching line height:

| Class | Size | Line height |
|---|---|---|
| `text-xs` | 12 | 16 |
| `text-sm` | 14 | 20 |
| `text-base` | 16 | 24 |
| `text-lg` | 18 | 28 |
| `text-xl` | 20 | 28 |
| `text-2xl` | 24 | 32 |
| `text-3xl` | 30 | 36 |
| `text-4xl` | 36 | 40 |
| `text-5xl` | 48 | 1× |
| `text-6xl` | 60 | 1× |
| `text-7xl` | 72 | 1× |
| `text-8xl` | 96 | 1× |
| `text-9xl` | 128 | 1× |

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `text-<size>/<leading>` | size and line height: `text-sm/6` (24 points), `text-lg/tight` |
| `text-[<length>]` | `fontSize`: `text-[22px]`, `text-[length:22px]` |
| `text-<color>` | `color` |
| `leading-none` (1), `leading-tight` (1.25), `leading-snug` (1.375), `leading-normal` (1.5), `leading-relaxed` (1.625), `leading-loose` (2) | `lineHeight` as a multiple of the font size |
| `leading-<n>`, `leading-[<length>]` | `lineHeight` in points (`leading-6` = 24) |
| `tracking-tighter` (-0.05em), `tracking-tight` (-0.025em), `tracking-normal` (0), `tracking-wide` (0.025em), `tracking-wider` (0.05em), `tracking-widest` (0.1em) | `letterSpacing` relative to the font size |
| `tracking-[<value>]` | `letterSpacing`: `tracking-[0.2em]`, `tracking-[1px]` |

### Alignment, case and wrapping

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right`, `text-justify` | `textAlign` |
| `text-start` | `textAlign: "auto"` |
| `text-end` | `textAlign: "right"` |
| `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize`, `normal-case` | `textTransform` |
| `truncate` | one line, tail ellipsis, no wrapping, `overflow: hidden` |
| `line-clamp-<n>`, `line-clamp-none` | `numberOfLines` (`none` removes the limit) |
| `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip` | `ellipsizeMode` `"tail"` / `"clip"` |
| `whitespace-nowrap`, `text-nowrap` | lines never wrap |
| `whitespace-normal`, `text-wrap`, `text-balance`, `text-pretty` | lines wrap (balancing is not done) |
| `select-text`, `select-all`, `select-none` | `selectable` |

### Decoration and shadow

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `underline`, `line-through`, `no-underline` | `textDecorationLine` |
| `decoration-solid`, `decoration-double`, `decoration-dotted`, `decoration-dashed`, `decoration-wavy` | `textDecorationStyle` |
| `decoration-<n>`, `decoration-[<length>]` | `textDecorationThickness` |
| `decoration-auto`, `decoration-from-font` | `textDecorationThickness: "auto"` |
| `decoration-<color>` | `textDecorationColor` |
| `underline-offset-<n>`, `underline-offset-[<length>]`, `underline-offset-auto` | `textUnderlineOffset` |
| `text-shadow-2xs`, `-xs`, `-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | a text shadow from the theme |
| `text-shadow-<color>` | its color (keeps each layer's alpha unless the color has one) |
| `text-shadow-none` | removes it |

Tailwind's text shadows have several layers; natively one shadow is drawn, the widest layer.

### Inputs

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `placeholder:text-<color>` | `placeholderTextColor` |
| `caret-<color>` | the cursor color |

## Backgrounds

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `bg-<color>` | `backgroundColor` |
| `bg-[<gradient>]` | `backgroundImage`: `bg-[linear-gradient(45deg,red,blue)]`, `bg-[radial-gradient(...)]` |
| `bg-linear-to-t`, `-tr`, `-r`, `-br`, `-b`, `-bl`, `-l`, `-tl` | a linear gradient toward a side or corner (`bg-gradient-to-*` is the v3 name) |
| `bg-linear-<angle>`, `bg-linear-[<angle>]` | a linear gradient at an angle: `bg-linear-45`, `-bg-linear-12`, `bg-linear-[0.25turn]` |
| `bg-radial` | a radial gradient from the center |
| `bg-conic`, `bg-conic-<angle>` | a conic gradient, optionally starting at an angle |
| `from-<color>`, `via-<color>`, `to-<color>` | the gradient's stops (default transparent at the ends) |
| `from-<p>%`, `via-<p>%`, `to-<p>%` | stop positions: `via-40%`, `from-[15%]` |
| `bg-none` | removes the gradient |

```tsx
<View class="h-32 rounded-2xl bg-linear-to-br from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 via-40% to-pink-500" />
```

## Borders

| Class | Sets |
|---|---|
| `border`, `border-<n>`, `border-[<length>]` | `borderWidth` (bare: 1) |
